Patch What it shows Segments: Two-Humped Envelope Five segments draw an envelope no ADSR can: a quick rise, a dip, a second slower swell and a long fade, and every note of the tune follows that shape. Change a segment's Level or Time and hear the hump move. Segments: Looping Filter Shape Set to run freely, the chain of four segments repeats like an LFO with a shape you choose: a fast ramp up, a step, a hold and a slide back. It sweeps the filter on a plucked arpeggio; stretch Time Scale or change the Shape knobs to reshape the sweep. Segments: Bouncing Ball Eight segments alternate between a tiny rise and a fall to zero, each bounce shorter and quieter than the last, so one gate rings out as a dropped ball. Move the Level of a segment to change how high it bounces. Segments: Segment Gates as Drummer A free-running chain of four equal segments hands out a gate at each step, and those gates play a kick, hat, snare and hat: the segments are the sequencer. Change a segment's Time to shift the groove, or raise Count to add steps. Segments: Swell and Breath One three-segment shape (rise, hold while the key is down, fall) opens the filter on a pad while its inverted output fades a noise wash down, so the sound turns from airy to tonal and back with every chord. Try Release set to Jump to cut the swell short when the chord ends. Presets The preset bar of the Segments view has 15 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Classic Pluck Instant attack, exponential fall: the all-round plucked envelope. Soft Pad Slow swell, a gentle settle and a long fade. Organ Gate Fast on, sustain high, short release: organ-style keying. Piano Decay Strong hit, quick drop, then a long tail. Reverse Swell Builds slowly and cuts off: for reversed-style hits. Bowed Strings Bow attack with a slight bloom and a soft release. Kick Pitch Drop Very fast pitch-drop curve: patch to oscillator pitch for kicks. Double Hit Two quick strikes in a row: flams and clap-like bursts. Triple Stutter Three decaying hits: a rhythmic stutter from one gate. Triangle Loop LFO Free-running up-and-down triangle LFO at about 1 Hz. Staircase Up Stepped rise of held plateaus: a rough step sequencer for pitch. Wobble Loop Irregular free-running wobble for filter or pitch. Long Evolve Multi-stage slow movement over half a minute for ambient textures. Velocity Snap Pluck whose level follows the played velocity. Finish Tail Plays through all stages even on a short note: one-shot percussion. Reference Knobs Knob Range Default Time 1 … 8 0.5 ms – 30 s 5 ms, 300 ms, 250 ms, 400 ms, then 250 ms Level 1 … 8 −1 … +1 1.0, 0.7, 0, 0, then 0 Shape 1 … 8 −1 … +1 0, +0.5, 0, +0.5, then 0 Time Scale ×0.1 – ×10 ×1 Vel Amount 0 – 100 % 0 % Every knob is a modulation destination. Settings Setting Values Default Count 1 – 8 4 Run Gated, Free Gated Release Jump, Finish Jump Sync Off, On Off Per segment (in the editor): Type (Ramp, Step, Hold), Loop, Wait (Time, Gate, Trigger; holds only), Seg In (Advance, Jump) and the note value used with Sync (1/4 by default). A new module is an ADSR: Ramp, Ramp, Hold (Gate), Ramp. Inputs Input Signal What it does Gate gate starts the chain; falling, goes to the release Velocity control scales the levels through Vel Amount (unpatched: full) Seg 1 … 8 trigger ends that segment ( Advance ) or jumps to it ( Jump ) Outputs Output Signal What it does Out control the chain Inv control the chain upside down Seg 1 … 8 gate high while that segment runs Loop trigger a new loop pass starts End trigger the last segment finished Active gate from the start until End

title: Function
text: Function Function in the module view Introduction The Function is a slope generator : it rises to 1 and falls back to 0. That one gesture covers a lot of jobs. Left running in a loop it's an LFO. Started by a trigger it's an attack/decay envelope. It can lock to Live's tempo. Its four outputs are related copies of the same slope, shifted in phase or stretched in time, so one module can move several things in a coordinated way. How does it work? Each cycle has two parts: a rise from 0 to 1 that takes Rise seconds and a fall back to 0 that takes Fall seconds. Shape bends both slopes: straight at 0, exponential toward +1, logarithmic toward −1. The view draws the resulting slope live. Cycle on (LFO). The slope repeats. One cycle lasts Rise + Fall , so equal values give a triangle and lopsided values give a ramp or a saw. A rising edge at Trig restarts the cycle from the beginning (hard reset). EOC fires at the end of every cycle. Cycle off (envelope). The Function waits. A rising edge at Trig starts the rise from wherever the output is, then the fall follows on its own. How long the trigger stays high doesn't matter. EOC fires when output A has fallen back to 0. Sync. With a note value selected, the cycle (or the whole envelope) lasts exactly that long at the current tempo. Rise and Fall then only set the proportion between rise and fall, not the time. While Live's transport is playing, a cycling Function is locked to the song position, so it lines up with the bar wherever you start playback. With the transport stopped it runs at the tempo without the lock. Starting the transport always restarts it. Spread derives outputs B, C and D from A: Cycling: B, C and D are shifted in phase by Spread × ¼ cycle each. At 100 % the four outputs are a quarter cycle apart (0°, 90°, 180°, 270°). Envelope: B, C and D take longer, each by a factor of (1 + Spread) more than the one before. At 100 % B is twice as long as A, C four times and D eight times. At 0 % Spread all four outputs are identical. How to use it? LFO: leave Cycle on, set Rise and Fall , and patch A onto any knob, e.g. a filter's cutoff. Set the depth with the cable's amount. Tempo-synced LFO: choose a Sync value such as 1/4 or 1 bar. Set Rise short and Fall long for a ramp down on every beat. Envelope: turn Cycle off and patch a gate or trigger into Trig . Short rise and longer fall gives a pluck; Shape toward +1 makes it snappier. Movement across several voices or parameters: with Spread up, patch A, B, C and D to four different destinations. They move together but not in lockstep: four phases of one LFO, or four envelopes of growing length. Sequencing events: EOC fires once per cycle or at the end of the envelope. Use it as a clock for Random or to trigger another envelope. Self-cycling with a twist: with Cycle off, patch EOC back into Trig . It loops, and you can patch other triggers in as well. Presets The preset bar of the Function view has 15 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Slow Triangle LFO A gentle 0.25 Hz triangle sweep for filters and pans. Pluck Envelope Snappy one-shot decay: patch a gate into Trig and A onto a cutoff or level. Soft Swell A slow one-shot swell and fade for pads. Ramp Down Beat Tempo-synced saw falling on every beat: instant pumping. Ramp Up Bar Rising ramp that resets every bar, for risers and builds. Vibrato Wobble About 6 Hz triangle: patch to pitch with a small amount. Quarter-Phase Quad Four outputs a quarter cycle apart for coordinated movement. Growing Echoes A through D are one-shot decays of 1x, 2x, 4x and 8x length. Eighth Pulse Short percussive curve on every eighth note. Lazy Drift Very slow, uneven wave with offset outputs for evolving textures. Bouncy Curve Exponential bounce, like a ball losing energy each beat. Reverse Swell Slow-start rise that cuts off: a reverse-style swell. Half-Bar Staggered Synced slope with phase-shifted outputs for rolling motion. Audio-Rate Buzz Fast triangle in the audible range: a FM or ring-style source. Eight-Bar Rise Huge synced build-up that restarts every eight bars. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Function does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Function under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Function: Filter Sweeper With Cycle on, the Function is a free-running rise-and-fall LFO: its A output opens and closes the filter on a plucked line. Change Rise and Fall for a lopsided sweep, or Shape to bend the slopes. Function: Plucked Envelope Cycle is off, so every sequencer gate triggers one rise-and-fall: the A output shapes the volume and the B output, lagging behind through Spread, opens the filter slightly later. Try a slower Rise for swells or a longer Fall for ringing notes. Function: Four Related Curves A, B, C and D are the same slow cycle at different delays, set by Spread, and here each one moves something else: filter cutoff, resonance, oscillator shape and reverb size. Raise Spread to pull them further apart, or lower it to make them move as one. Function: Bouncing Pad Locked to the beat with Sync, the Function acts as a rhythmic pump on a held pad: Fall sets how fast the volume swells back after each bounce. Change Sync for a faster or slower pulse, or Shape for a softer curve. Function: Swell and Chime One trigger per bar starts a long swell that fades a pad in and out; when it finishes, its End output triggers a second Function that plays a short chime. Lengthen the first Fall to push the chimes later. Reference Knobs and settings Control Range Default Rise 1 ms – 10 s 250 ms Fall 1 ms – 10 s 250 ms Shape −1 … +1 0 (linear) Spread 0 – 100 % 0 % Cycle on / off on Sync Free, 1/32, 1/16, 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, 1 bar, 2 bars, 4 bars, 8 bars Free Rise: duration of the rising part. Its knob centre is 250 ms. In sync mode only the ratio Rise : Fall counts. Fall: duration of the falling part, same range. With Cycle on, the frequency is 1 / (Rise + Fall): 250 ms + 250 ms = 2 Hz. Shape: the curve of both slopes. 0 is linear. Positive values are exponential: the rise starts slowly and speeds up, the fall drops fast and then eases out. This is the punchy, natural-sounding envelope. Negative values are logarithmic, the other way round: the rise shoots up and settles, the fall lingers and then drops away. Spread: how far B, C and D differ from A. Phase offsets when cycling, longer durations as an envelope (see above). Cycle: on loops the slope (LFO); off makes a one-shot envelope started by Trig . Sync: Free uses the times from Rise and Fall . A note value fixes the total length to that note at Live's tempo (4/4 assumed). Rise and Fall then share that time in their ratio. Rise , Fall , Shape and Spread are modulation destinations. Modulating Rise or Fall from another Function gives an LFO with a wandering rate. Inputs Input Signal What it does Trig gate rising edge: restarts the cycle (Cycle on) or starts the envelope (Cycle off) Outputs Output Signal What it does A control, 0 – 1 the slope B control, 0 – 1 A shifted ¼ × Spread in phase, or stretched by (1 + Spread) C control, 0 – 1 shifted ½ × Spread, or stretched by (1 + Spread)² D control, 0 – 1 shifted ¾ × Spread, or stretched by (1 + Spread)³ EOC trigger end of cycle: once per loop, or when A's envelope finishes

title: Six Slopes
text: Six Slopes Six Slopes in the module view Introduction Six Slopes is six slope generators on one set of knobs . Each slope rises and falls; together they can be six envelopes, six LFOs or, at audio rate, six oscillators that form a chord of harmonics. The trick is the Harmonics knob. In the middle all six run at the same speed. Turn it right and they spread out over the overtone series (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 times as fast); turn it left and they slow down over the undertones (½, ⅓ … ⅙). In between, the speeds are uneven, so looping slopes drift in and out of phase: slow, shifting patterns from one knob. How does it work? One slope. Rate sets how fast channel 1 runs; Skew is the share of the slope spent rising (25 %: a quick rise and a longer fall), and Curve bends it: −1 logarithmic, 0 straight, +1 exponential. The Pitch input adds octaves to the rate of all six. Six speeds. Each channel runs at channel 1's rate times its ratio. With Harmonics at +1 the ratios are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6: channel 6 is six times as fast, so its envelope is six times as short. At −1 they're 1, ½, ⅓, ¼, ⅕, ⅙. Snap rounds the ratios: Integer snaps to whole numbers (or whole-number fractions to the left), so the knob steps through whole-number chords: at 0.4 the ratios are 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3. Just snaps each ratio to the nearest note of a just scale (1, 9/8, 5/4, 4/3, 3/2, 5/3, 15/8, in any octave): in Sound mode, six notes of a pure, beatless chord. The lane next to each slope shows its current ratio as a fraction (or the note it plays in Sound mode). Shared triggers. Every channel has its own Trig input. An unpatched Trig listens to the nearest patched one above it, so one gate into Trig 1 starts all six, and with Harmonics up the six envelopes end one after another, a natural "strum" of decays. Patch Trig 4 too, and channels 4–6 follow it while 1–3 still follow Trig 1 . Modes AR: a one-shot envelope per trigger. The rise starts from wherever the level is, so a retrigger during the fall never jumps. ASR: rises while the gate is high, holds at the top, falls when the gate goes low (from wherever it is, even during the rise). Loop: six LFOs. A Trig rising edge restarts that channel's cycle. With nothing patched they run freely, all starting together. Sound: six oscillators. Rate now spans 16 Hz – 4 kHz with C4 in the middle; Skew moves the wave from saw to triangle to ramp and Curve bends it (+0.5 is close to a sine). A Trig edge hard-syncs its channel. Partials above a quarter of the sample rate fade out instead of aliasing. Sync (AR, ASR, Loop) makes channel 1's slope one note value long at the current tempo; the others keep their ratios. In Loop with the transport playing every channel is locked to the song position, so with whole-number ratios they meet again on every note value, after loop jumps too, and every render is the same. Pitch then shifts in whole octaves. Levels and Sum Level scales all six. Tilt balances them: at +1 channel 1 is silent and channel 6 at full level, at −1 the other way round (a darker chord in Sound mode, as with natural overtones). Sum mixes the six: six unipolar slopes reach full scale when about half of them are up. In Loop it's a complex, slowly changing contour; in Sound mode it's the mixed tone, gently limited. End 1 fires when channel 1 finishes its slope or cycle. Active is high while any channel moves (AR, ASR) and always in Loop and Sound. How to use it? Strummed decays: a sequencer gate into Trig 1 , AR, Skew 5 %, Harmonics +0.6; patch the six outputs to six VCAs or filter cutoffs. Six-part rhythm envelopes: six drum triggers into the six Trigs, one envelope each, with one set of shape knobs. Phasing LFOs: Loop, Harmonics at a small, uneven value like 0.13: six slow waves that drift apart and back. Sum onto a filter for a contour that never quite repeats. Polyrhythm on the grid: Loop, Sync 1 bar, Snap Integer, Harmonics +1: six LFOs at 1–6 cycles per bar, locked to the song. A just chord: Sound, Snap Just, Pitch from Voice In › Pitch , Sum into a VCA. Turn Harmonics for different chords and Tilt to the left for a softer tone. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Six Slopes does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Six Slopes under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Six Slopes: Looping Chord In Loop mode six slopes breathe at related rates, and each one swells a different note of a chord, so the harmony slowly rearranges itself. Move Harmonics to change how far apart the rates are and Skew to shift each swell between rise and fall. Six Slopes: Harmonic Bell One trigger starts all six slopes in AR mode; with Harmonics up, the higher slopes die away faster, so each note sparkles then settles into its lower partials. Move Harmonics down for a darker, longer ring or change Rate to stretch the whole decay. Six Slopes: Sound Mode Voice In Sound mode the slopes run at audio rate and follow the sequencer's pitch, so the Six Slopes is the oscillator itself; the Sum output is a rich, buzzy tone. Try Snap on Integer or Just for harmonic spacing, or Curve and Skew for different timbres. Six Slopes: Locked Motion Sync ties the Loop mode to the tempo and Snap on Integer keeps every rate an exact multiple, so six slopes move filter, tone, pulse and volume in polyrhythm that never drifts. Change Sync or Harmonics and listen to the grooves reshuffle. Six Slopes: Chord Unfolds In ASR mode each of six slopes rises while a gate is held and falls when it ends; with Harmonics below zero the lower notes of the chord arrive first and the top ones drift in last. Change Harmonics, Rate or the sequencer's gate length to alter the unfolding. Presets The preset bar of the Six Slopes view has 14 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Overtone Cascade Six looping slopes at overtone ratios: rich, related motion. Undertone Drift Slopes spread downward: slower and slower layers. Unison Pulse All six at one rate: use the sum or stagger with triggers. Six Plucks Fast attack decays on each trigger: six different plucks. Swell Gates Rise, hold while gated, fall: six sustained envelopes. Slow Breath Ten-second cycles: very slow evolving modulation. Synced Eighths Tempo-locked slopes with overtone ratios. Quarter Note Saws Rising ramps locked to the beat. Just Intervals Rates snapped to just-intonation ratios: consonant polyrhythms. Integer Ratios Whole-number rate ratios: layers that realign cleanly. Bipolar Wander Bipolar outputs for pitch or pan wandering. Tilted Levels Higher slopes louder: emphasises the faster layers. Audio Rate Slopes Slopes as audio oscillators at harmonic ratios. Sharp Curves Strongly curved spikes: percussive modulation. title: Tidal
text: Tidal Tidal in the module view Introduction Tidal is a slope generator : a voltage that rises and falls, again and again. Slow, it's a swell that takes minutes; medium, it's an LFO; fast, it's a tone you can hear. Trigger it and it becomes an envelope. One knob, Skew , decides how the cycle is split between rising and falling, Curve bends the slopes, and Smooth either rounds everything into a sine-like curve or folds it into a bright, many-peaked contour. Four outputs carry four related versions of the same slope, so one Tidal can move four things in a pattern that belongs together. How does it work? One cycle is a rise and a fall. Frequency sets how many cycles per second; Range picks the knob's span: Slow (one cycle per 1000 s up to 1 Hz), Medium (0.02–50 Hz) or Audio (8 Hz – 8 kHz, C4 at the centre). The Pitch input adds octaves (1 V/oct), so in the Audio range Tidal plays in tune. Skew is the share of the cycle spent rising. At 50 % it's a triangle; at 0 % a falling saw, at 100 % a rising saw. The total time stays the same. In the Audio range Skew stops just short of the ends, so the wave never jumps vertically. Curve bends both slopes: −1 logarithmic (quick start, slow arrival), 0 straight, +0.5 a round cosine (a sine-like wave at Skew 50 %), +1 exponential (slow start, quick arrival). Smooth below 0 passes each output through a gentle low-pass that follows the cycle rate: at −1 every shape becomes an almost pure sine, and Tidal restores its full level once per cycle so the swing doesn't shrink. Above 0 it folds : the slope is amplified and mirrored back into range each time it hits an edge. At +1 a triangle turns into seven peaks per cycle: busy contours at LFO rates, rich tones at audio rate. Modes Loop: cycles all the time. A rising edge on Trig restarts the cycle. AD: waits at 0. A rising edge on Trig plays one rise and one fall, then End fires. A new trigger during the fall rises again from where the level is, without a jump. AR: rises while Trig is high, holds at the top, and falls when it goes low, from wherever the level is. Rise time is Skew ÷ Frequency, fall time the rest. AD and AR are always unipolar (0 … 1). In Loop, Polarity chooses −1 … +1 or 0 … 1. The four outputs A is the main slope. B , C and D follow it as Relation says, and Spread sets how far apart they are (at 0 all four are the same): Phase: each output is shifted along the cycle. At +1 the four are a quarter cycle apart (0°, 90°, 180°, 270°); negative Spread shifts the other way. In AD/AR the envelopes start one after another instead, a quarter of the slope's length apart at ±1. Level: the outputs get quieter: B at two thirds, C at a third, D at nothing for Spread ±1. Below 0, B and D are also upside down: a fan that alternates. Ratio: rhythmic ratios that come back together. Spread picks a set (the knob shows it): 2 · 3 · 4, then 3/2 · 2 · 3, 4/3 · 3/2 · 2, 5/4 · 3/2 · 7/4, 5/3 · 7/4 · 9/4, faster on the right, the slower reciprocals on the left. All four restart together whenever their pattern repeats (for 4/3 · 3/2 · 2: every 6 cycles of A). Harmonic: frequency ratios. At +1 B, C and D run 2, 3 and 4 times as fast as A (overtones), at −1 at ½, ⅓ and ¼ (undertones). In between the ratios are uneven and the outputs slowly drift against each other. In AD and AR, Ratio and Harmonic change each output's length instead: an output at ratio 2 is an envelope half as long. One trigger, four accents. Timing Free: Frequency and Pitch, modulated every sample (smooth FM). Sync: one cycle per note value (1/32T … 8 bars). While the transport plays, the cycle is locked to the song position: always at the same point at the same bar, even after a loop jump, and the Ratio and Harmonic outputs lock with it. Pitch still shifts the speed in whole octaves (+1: two cycles per note value). Clock: patch a clock into Clock and Tidal measures its tempo (averaging the last four pulses) and runs at Ratio × the clock. For ×2 and faster the cycle restarts on every pulse, for ÷2 and slower on every n-th pulse, so it stays in step. After a pause the measurement starts again instead of jumping to a wild rate. The Frequency knob then shows the ratio and the measured BPM. Clock wins over Sync, Sync over Frequency. Rise is high while A rises. End fires when A finishes a cycle (Loop) or reaches 0 (AD, AR). Both come from A before smoothing, so they're on time even when Smooth delays the curve. How to use it? Slow swell: Range Slow , Frequency to a few minutes per cycle, A onto a filter's cutoff. Skew 80 % for long rises and quicker falls. Circular motion: Relation Phase , Spread +1, Curve +0.5: A and B are a sine and a cosine. Patch them to two pans, or A to a filter and C (the opposite) to a reverb send. Polyrhythm: Relation Ratio , Sync 1 bar, Spread at 4/3 · 3/2 · 2: four modulations that meet again every six bars. Accent pattern: Mode AD , Relation Harmonic , Spread +1, one trigger from a sequencer: four envelopes of four lengths onto four VCAs. Oscillator: Range Audio , Pitch from a sequencer or Voice In › Pitch , A into a VCA's audio input. Turn Skew for saw-to-triangle, Smooth up for folded overtones, down for a pure sine. Clocked LFO: a sequencer's clock into Clock , Ratio ÷4: one cycle per bar that follows tempo changes and a manual clock. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Tidal does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Tidal under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Tidal: Slow Tide On the Slow range the Tidal loops over many seconds and its four outputs trail one another through Phase: the filter opens, the resonance swells and the tone shape drifts, in turn. Move Skew to make the tide rise slowly and fall fast, or switch Relation to Ratio. Tidal: Audio-Rate Voice With Range on Audio and the sequencer's pitch patched in, the Tidal becomes an oscillator: A is the main tone while B, C and D add related shapes. Skew, Curve and Smooth change the waveform, Spread changes how the other outputs differ. Tidal: Synced Groove Sync locks the looping Tidal to the beat, so its slopes pulse a bass line in time: A makes the volume duck and bounce, B opens the filter on the off-beats. Change Sync or Skew to move the bounce, or Polarity to flip it. Tidal: Triggered Decays In AD mode each sequencer gate fires one quick rise-and-fall: A shapes the volume of a bright pluck, while B, with Spread, opens the filter for a vowel-like wah on every note. Increase Frequency to shorten the whole shape or Skew to move its peak. Tidal: Swell and Splash In AR mode a held gate makes the Tidal rise, and when it finishes falling its End output fires a snare: a pad swells in, fades, and the drum answers. Change Frequency to stretch the swell, or Skew to move where it peaks. Presets The preset bar of the Tidal view has 16 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Gentle Loop A plain 1 Hz triangle-like loop with four related outputs. Slow Tide Minute-long swells: ambient filter and level motion. Rising Saw Ramp up then quick drop: repeating risers. Falling Saw Instant rise and linear fall: sidechain-like pumping. Plucked AD One-shot attack and decay per trigger: a snappy envelope. Pad AR Rise while held, fall on release: a soft pad envelope. Synced Quarter Locked to the tempo at quarter notes. Synced Dotted Eighth Dotted-eighth swells for rhythmic filter movement. Wide Phase Outputs Four outputs at different phases: stereo or multi-target motion. Harmonic Stack Outputs carry harmonics of the main rate: complex contours. Ratio Cluster Outputs at related speeds, starting from a triplet ratio. Level Fan Same rate, four different depths for scaled modulation. Smooth Sine-ish Heavily smoothed slope: nearly a sine for vibrato. Bipolar Wobble Centred wobble for vibrato and pitch effects. Unipolar Pump Positive-only fast-attack pump for ducking. Audio Rate Tone Slope oscillator at audio rate: a raw, lo-fi tone source. Reference Knobs Knob Range Default Frequency Slow 0.001–1 Hz, Medium 0.02–50 Hz, Audio 8 Hz – 8 kHz 1 Hz (Medium) Skew 0 – 100 % 50 % Curve −1 … +1 0 Smooth −1 … +1 0 Spread −1 … +1 0 Every knob is a modulation destination. Changing Range keeps the knob's position and the cycle's phase. Settings Setting Values Default Mode AD, Loop, AR Loop Range Slow, Medium, Audio Medium Relation Ratio, Phase, Level, Harmonic Phase Sync Free, 8 bars … 1/32T (straight, dotted, triplet) Free Ratio ÷16, ÷8, ÷6, ÷4, ÷3, ÷2, ×1, ×2, ×3, ×4, ×6, ×8, ×16 ×1 Polarity (Loop) Bipolar, Unipolar Bipolar Sync To Auto, Clock, Transport Auto Sync To: what steps the module. Auto : the clock pulses while Clock is patched, otherwise the transport. Clock : only the pulses step it. Transport : the song position steps it, and a patched Clock is ignored. With Transport , Sync still picks a note value or free running. Inputs Input Signal What it does Trig gate AD: starts a slope. AR: high rises and holds, low falls. Loop: a rising edge restarts the cycle Clock trigger follow this clock at Ratio Pitch pitch added to Frequency in octaves Outputs Output Signal What it does A control the main slope B, C, D control related slopes ( Relation , Spread ) Rise gate high while A rises End trigger A finished a cycle or reached 0

title: LFO
text: LFO LFO in the module view Introduction The LFO is a low-frequency oscillator : it moves up and down by itself, slower than you can hear, and makes whatever it's patched into move with it. Patch it onto a filter's cutoff for a sweep, onto an oscillator's pitch for vibrato, or onto a VCA's gain for tremolo. Pick a wave, set the speed, done. It can run freely or lock to a clock or the song's tempo. How does it work? Speed. Sync chooses what times the cycle: Free: Rate sets the speed in Hz. Clock: the cycle follows the pulses at the Clock input, phase-locked. Rate is a note value (1/64 … 16 bars, with dotted and triplet values) and a pulse counts as a 1/16 step, as for the sequencers. A Clock that stops holds the wave in place. Tempo: Rate is a note value and one cycle takes exactly that long. While the transport plays, the LFO follows the song position: it's always at the same point of its wave at the same bar, even after a loop jump, and renders the same every time. When the transport is stopped it keeps running at the synced speed. Waves. Wave chooses what Out plays: Sine and Triangle : smooth up and down. Both start at the middle, rising. Saw Up / Saw Down : a ramp that jumps back at the end of each cycle. Square : high, then low. Width sets how much of the cycle is high (it only shows for this wave). Random Step : a new random value each cycle, held until the next. Random Smooth : glides from one random value to the next. There is a single output, Out . For two waves at once, use two LFOs. Shape. Three small knobs change the character of every wave: Morph (12 o'clock is the plain wave) bends each wave its own way: Sine and Triangle square up (right) or soften towards a triangle or spikes (left); the saws turn convex or concave; Square rounds its edges (right) or splits into 2–4 pulses (left); Random Step glides (right) or steps through fewer levels (left); Random Smooth eases like a step (right) or runs straight (left). Skew moves the peak of the cycle: a triangle becomes a ramp at the ends. Curve bends the wave towards exponential (up) or logarithmic (down). Phase shifts the wave within its cycle. Polarity chooses between Bipolar (−1 … +1, moves both ways around the knob) and Unipolar (0 … 1, only upwards). Random values repeat on every render. Reset and Fade. A trigger at Reset restarts the cycle (on a free-running LFO) and the fade-in. With Fade above 0, the output starts at 0 and grows to full over that time after each Reset and each time the transport starts. How to use it? Filter sweep: Out onto a Multi Filter's Cutoff ; set the cable's amount for the depth. Vibrato in a Voice Cell: put the LFO inside the cell, Out onto the oscillator's Pitch knob with a small amount, Voice In › Trigger into Reset , and set Fade to half a second: each note starts straight and then begins to wobble. Rhythmic movement: set Sync to Tempo, Rate to 1/8 and Wave to Square onto a VCA's gain for a tempo-locked chop. Two related movements: use two LFOs with Phase 0° and 90° for circular stereo movement. Wobbling the wobble: patch another LFO onto Rate . Clocking other modules: a Square LFO with a small Width onto a sequencer's Clock or an envelope's Gate gives a pulse at every cycle. Presets The preset bar of the LFO view has 20 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Gentle Sine Slow sine for subtle filter or pitch drift. Vibrato Classic vibrato speed that fades in after the note starts. Tremolo Unipolar triangle for amplitude tremolo. Beat Pump Falling ramp locked to the beat: sidechain-like ducking. Eighth Chop Square gate on every eighth for rhythmic chopping. Slow Sweep A 20-second triangle for long filter sweeps. Rising Saw Ramp that climbs over two bars and snaps back. Sample and Hold Random stepped values, a classic sample-and-hold. Smooth Random Wandering smooth random for organic movement. Narrow Pulse Thin pulse for staccato jumps. Wide Slow Tide A four-bar sine swell locked to the song. Triplet Feel Wobble Fast synced triangle for shimmering wobble. Offset Sine Sine starting at its peak: pair with another LFO for quadrature. Fast Flutter Tape-like flutter, best used very lightly. Wild Random Fast random jitter for glitchy modulation. Ramp from Triangle Skew pushes the triangle's peak to the end: a rising ramp. Exponential Sine Curve bends the sine towards exponential: slow start, fast finish. Soft Square Morph rounds the edges of the square into a trapezoid. Dotted Eighth A triangle locked to a dotted eighth. Triplet Pulse Square gate on eighth-note triplets. Demo patches Five whole patches show what LFO does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick LFO under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows LFO: Vibrato and Tremolo One slow LFO gently bends the pitch of a held lead and a second one swells its volume; Fade lets the vibrato arrive only after the note has settled. Raise the vibrato Rate or the cable amounts, or move Fade to zero. LFO: Synced Wobble A triangle LFO locked to eighth notes sweeps the low-pass filter of a bass line, a classic wobble that stays in time with the drums. Change Rate for a slower or faster wobble, switch Wave from Triangle to Square, or raise Resonance. LFO: Random Steps The LFO's Random Step wave picks a new level every sixteenth and sends it to the filter, so a repeating line is coloured differently on each step, always the same way. Switch Wave to Random Smooth for a gliding version. LFO: Auto Pan Two LFOs, half a cycle apart through Phase, raise and lower the left and right volume of a pad in opposite directions, so it travels across the stereo field. Change Rate, or set both Phase values the same to hear it collapse to a plain tremolo. LFO: Gate Chopper A square LFO locked to sixteenths chops a held pad into a rhythmic gate, and its rising edge also triggers the hi-hat on every pulse. Move Width to make the chops shorter or longer, or change Rate for another pattern. Reference Knobs Knob Range Default Rate 0.01 – 50 Hz 1 Hz Phase 0 – 360° 0° Pulse Width 5 – 95 % 50 % Fade 0 – 10 s 0 s Every knob is a modulation destination. Settings Setting Values Default Wave Sine, Triangle, Saw Up, Saw Down, Square, Random Step, Random Smooth Sine Sync Free, 1/32, 1/16, 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, 1 bar, 2 bars, 4 bars, 8 bars Free Polarity Bipolar, Unipolar Bipolar Seed 0 – 999 1 Inputs Input Signal What it does Reset trigger restarts the cycle (free-running) and the fade-in Clock trigger the pulses a Clock-synced LFO follows (a pulse is a 1/16 step) Outputs Output Signal What it does Out control the wave chosen in Wave

title: Organic LFOs
text: Organic LFOs Organic LFOs in the module view Introduction Organic LFOs are eight slow LFOs that move like a group of living things : related, but never quite in step. Think of a field of grass in the wind, a flock of birds, or eight musicians breathing together without a conductor. One Rate sets the pace, Spread fans the eight speeds apart, and Drift lets each one wander a little in speed and shape, so the pattern never lines up exactly and never sounds mechanical. Yet nothing is left to chance: the wandering comes from the Seed , so every render of your song moves exactly the same way. How does it work? The fan. LFO 1 runs at Rate . With Spread at +1 the others get faster, up to LFO 8 at about 16 times the speed; at −1 they get slower; at 0 all eight share LFO 1's speed. Each LFO also gets a tiny seeded offset, so no two of them settle into a simple, repeating relation. Drift lets every LFO wander along a slow, smooth curve of its own: its speed (at 100 %, between about 21 % slower and 27 % faster) and its shape. A fast LFO wanders faster than a slow one; the wandering always takes a few of its cycles. At 0 % everything is exact. Anchor keeps LFO 1's speed exact (only its shape drifts), so it stays in time with the song while the others float around it. Twist changes the shape of all eight: at −1 soft, rounded plateaus (almost a square), at 0 a sine, at +1 a fast rise to a narrow peak and a long, lazy fall. Drift moves each LFO's twist a little around this. Scatter sets how far apart the eight start after a Reset or a transport start: at 0 % they all start together (and with Spread and Drift at 0, all eight are identical), at 100 % they start anywhere in their cycle. Sum mixes the eight into one complex contour, gently limited. Max follows whichever LFO is highest at the moment: a restless upper outline, mostly in the upper half, great in Unipolar for brightness or density. Level scales every output. Free or locked Free: the LFOs run on their own. Their wandering is counted from the last Reset or transport start, so the same patch rendered from the same start moves the same way. Bars: Rate picks a note value for LFO 1 (64 bars … 1/4T). While the transport plays, everything is worked out from the song position: LFO 1 sits at the same point at the same bar, the others move along their own paths, and jumping around the song (or rendering again) gives exactly the same movement. Drift shifts the phases instead of the speeds here. When the transport stops they run on at the current tempo. Turn Spread while locked and the fan re-forms around the song position, so set it rather than sweep it. Changing the Seed (or the Lock) gives a different group; the outputs fade over 50 ms so it doesn't click. How to use it? Living pad: eight outputs onto the cutoffs, pans or levels of eight voices or layers. Rate 0.05 Hz, Spread +0.4, Drift 40 %. One complex contour: Sum onto a filter or reverb mix: a curve that feels alive but never repeats within a song. Breathing in time: Lock Bars, Rate 4 bars, Anchor on, Drift 30 %: LFO 1 breathes with the bars, the others follow loosely. Brightness that peaks: Max in Unipolar onto a filter cutoff: every time one of the eight peaks, it opens. Different per voice: inside a Voice Cell, add Voice In › Random to Twist or Rate so each note gets its own movement. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Organic LFOs does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Organic LFOs under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Organic LFOs: Living Pad Eight slow, related movements are spread over a pad: the filter, the oscillator shape and the reverb size each follow a different one, so the sound breathes without ever repeating exactly. Change Rate, Spread and Drift on the module to speed up or loosen the group. Organic LFOs: Breathing Chord Six of the eight outputs swell six notes of a chord in and out, so the harmony rearranges itself in a slow, natural way. Lower Scatter to make the voices move more alike, or turn Spread negative to reverse the order. Organic LFOs: Lively Pluck At a faster Rate with plenty of Drift, the same eight movements become a restless wobble: they open the filter, change the tone and add resonance to a plucked line, never twice the same way. Slow Rate and Drift down for a calmer feel. Organic LFOs: Bar-Locked Breath With Lock set to Bars the group repeats in step with the song, so the filter movement over a bass line and beat comes back exactly each time. Switch Lock back to Free and the same movement slips out of time. Organic LFOs: Wandering Voices Four held notes each wander across the stereo field, steered by different outputs, while Twist bends how the group is related. Change Twist and Spread to change how the voices follow each other. Presets The preset bar of the Organic LFOs view has 14 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Living Group Eight related slow movers: a good default for evolving patches. Glacial Extremely slow drift for long-form changes. Gentle Breath Soft, breathing movement at reduced depth. Swarm Faster, busier group, like insects. Tight Family LFOs stay close together: subtle, related motion. Wide Spread Rates spread widely from slow to quick. Inverted Spread Spread reversed: the order of speeds flips. Twisted Twist skews the phases so the group chases itself. Counter Twist Twist the other way for opposite phase relations. Unipolar Drift Positive-only values, ideal for levels and mix knobs. Bar Locked Locked to the song for repeatable movement. Restless Drift Maximum drift: the group wanders and never repeats. Free Start Starts at random positions instead of anchored. Different Seed Another family of movements from a different seed. Reference Knobs Knob Range Default Rate 0.002 – 20 Hz, or a note value with Lock = Bars 0.2 Hz Spread −1 … +1 +0.5 Drift 0 – 100 % 30 % Twist −1 … +1 0 Scatter 0 – 100 % 100 % Level 0 – 100 % 100 % Every knob is a modulation destination. Settings Setting Values Default Lock Free, Bars Free Anchor On, Off On Polarity Bipolar, Unipolar Bipolar Seed 0 – 999 1 Inputs Input Signal What it does Reset trigger restarts all eight at their scattered start phases (Free) Outputs Output Signal What it does Out 1 … Out 8 control the eight LFOs, slowest to fastest (Spread ≥ 0) Sum control the eight mixed and soft-limited Max control the highest of the eight

title: Quad LFO
text: Quad LFO Quad LFO in the module view Introduction Quad LFO is four LFOs in one module , with one Mode that decides how they belong together: four free speeds, one speed in four quarter-steps (quadrature), one speed with an adjustable phase spread, or one speed divided into slower and faster related speeds. It's the quickest way to circular stereo movement, rotating pans, four voices that move together but not in unison, or interlocking polyrhythms. Each of the four picks its own wave and depth, and everything can lock to the song's bars. How does it work? Waves. Each LFO has its own Wave : Sine, Triangle, Saw Up, Saw Down, Square (with the shared Pulse Width ), Random Step and Random Smooth: the same waves as the LFO module. Random values come from Seed and differ per channel, and every render repeats them. Modes. Free: four LFOs, four Rate knobs. Quadrature: one speed ( Rate 1 ), the four a quarter cycle apart: 0°, 90°, 180°, 270°. Two sines a quarter apart draw a circle: patch Out 1 and Out 2 to the X and Y of anything (or to two pans). Phase: like Quadrature, but Spread sets the distance between neighbours (0–360°). At 0° all four move together; at 120° three of them share the cycle evenly; at 180° 1 and 3 match, as do 2 and 4. Divide: one speed, and each LFO runs at its Divide setting of it: ×4, ×3, ×2, ÷1 … ÷8, ÷12, ÷16. With ÷1 ÷2 ÷3 ÷4 they meet again every 12 cycles of LFO 1, and they really do meet: the four restart together whenever their pattern repeats. Switching Mode keeps LFO 1 where it is; the others glide to their new place over 5 ms, so a switch never clicks. Level sets each LFO's depth; a negative level turns it upside down. Polarity chooses −1 … +1 or 0 … 1; in Unipolar, a negative level gives the inverted wave (1 − v) instead of going below 0. Sum is the average of the four. Cycle 1 … 4 fire once per cycle of each LFO, where its wave starts. In Quadrature and Phase they come from LFO 1's cycle, so turning or modulating Spread moves the pulses but never adds extra ones. Timing Free rates: each Rate in Hz (0.01–50 Hz), modulated per sample. Sync on: the Rate knobs pick note values instead (16 bars … 1/32T, straight, dotted and triplet; modulation steps through them). While the transport plays, every LFO is locked to the song position: always at the same point at the same bar, after loop jumps too, and renders repeat. With the transport stopped they run on at the current tempo. Clock: patch a clock and LFO 1 runs one cycle per Clock Ratio pulses, measured from the clock (averaging four pulses) and restarted on every Clock Ratio -th pulse so it stays in step. The other LFOs follow LFO 1 in the shared modes and Divide; in Free mode only LFO 1 follows the clock. After a pause the measurement starts over. Clock wins over Sync. Reset restarts all four (at their offsets in Quadrature and Phase). With Sync on and the transport playing, Reset moves the grid instead: the next sample counts as the start of the cycle, until the transport starts again. A transport start resets everything. Hold freezes all four while it's high and lets them continue where they were. While locked to the song, the outputs freeze and on release jump back to the song position, smoothed over 5 ms. How to use it? Circular panning: Quadrature, Sine on 1 and 2, Out 1 and Out 2 onto two pans (or a mixer's X/Y). Switch the view to XY to see the circle. Four voices, one breath: Phase mode, Spread 90°, the four outputs onto four filter cutoffs in a Voice Cell's neighbours: the same movement, passed along. Polyrhythmic modulation: Divide, Sync on, Rate 1 at 1 bar, Divide ÷1 ÷2 ÷3 ÷4: four movements that line up every twelve bars, on the same bar every time. Random per voice: Free, Random Smooth on all four, slightly different rates: four unrelated, gentle wanderings from one seed. Gating on the beat: a sequencer's clock into Clock , Clock Ratio 4, Square on LFO 1: a chop that follows the clock, even a swung or manual one. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Quad LFO does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Quad LFO under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Quad LFO: Quadrature Chord In Quadrature mode the four LFOs are a quarter-turn apart, so four notes of a chord swell one after another in a rotating pattern. Change Rate to turn it faster, or switch Mode to Free to let each LFO run at its own speed. Quad LFO: Divided Movements Locked to the tempo in Divide mode, the four LFOs run at whole fractions of one rate: the fastest shapes the tone, slower ones open the filter over two, four and eight times as long. Change a Divide setting or switch Sync off to unlock it. Quad LFO: Stereo Filter Sweep Phase mode keeps all four LFOs at the same rate but staggered by Spread. Here two of them sweep a separate filter for each channel, so the pad's brightness moves from left to right. Widen or narrow Spread, or change Rate 1 for a faster sweep. Quad LFO: Free Texture In Free mode the four LFOs run at unrelated rates with different waves (sine, smooth random, triangle and stepped random); their Sum output moves the filter while the others change tone and resonance, an endlessly shifting texture. Change a Rate or Wave to steer it. Quad LFO: Clocked and Held The LFOs follow a clock from the sequencer rather than a free rate, and a second, sparser gate patched to Hold freezes them for a moment. The result is a filter movement that stops and resumes in time with the notes. Change Clock Ratio for a faster or slower cycle. Presets The preset bar of the Quad LFO view has 15 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Quadrature Sine Four sines 90 degrees apart: circular motion for panning or filters. Slow Drift Four unrelated very slow sines: gentle, never-repeating drift. Vibrato Pair Two close vibrato rates: use out1 and out2 on left and right pitch. Wide Phase Spread One rate, four phases 120 degrees apart: wide stereo movement. Triangle Cascade Closely staggered triangles for a rolling sweep across four targets. Polyrhythm Divide Square waves divided from one rate: interlocking pulse patterns. Synced Quarters Clock-locked divisions from fast to very slow, all in tempo. Double Time Rise Tempo-synced rising ramps at related speeds. Tremolo Square Hard on/off amplitude chop: patch out1 into a VCA. Soft Tremolo Smooth classic tremolo depth for an amp. Sample and Hold Steps Four random step streams at different speeds. Random Glide Smooth random wandering on four outputs: organic pad motion. title: Shape Sequencer
text: Shape Sequencer Shape Sequencer in the module view Introduction The Shape Sequencer draws a control voltage in time with the music . You choose how long the loop is and how finely it is divided, then place shapes in the steps: a rising saw, a falling saw, a plateau, a curve. Patch its output onto a volume for a sidechain pump, a filter cutoff for a rhythmic sweep, or a pan for a hopping stereo image. It outputs CV only. What the shape moves is up to the module you patch it to. How does it work? Length and steps. Length sets the loop in beats (4 beats is one bar, up to 64). Steps divides it into equal cells, from 1 to 32: the grid you paint on. Any number works, 4 or 8 as well as 5 or 7. A loop of 4 beats on 4 steps has a step per beat; 8 beats on 8 steps does too. Shapes. Pick a shape in the palette and click or drag over steps to place it: Saw up and Saw down ramp between two levels. Plateau holds one level. Curve is an S-shaped glide between two levels. Triangle rises to a peak and falls back. Pulse holds one level for the first half of the shape and another for the second. Erase removes what is on a step (a step with nothing plays 0). Choose Select to stop placing and just pick shapes. Changing the step count later. The steps are only a grid: the shapes keep their place in the loop. Draw four shapes on 4 steps, switch to 8, and each shape now covers two steps. Paint a new shape onto one step of it and the shape is cut to what is left, so you can replace one quarter note with two eighths and leave everything else as it was. Editing a shape. Click a shape to select it. Its handles appear: a yellow square for each level (drag it up or down), and a white dot on the line that bends the curve (drag it up or down). Flip swaps the start and end levels, so a saw up becomes a saw down. Reset shape straightens the curve. Running it. Sync decides what starts the loop: Transport: the loop follows the song position, so it is always on the grid, even after a loop jump. It rests while the song is stopped. Trigger: a pulse at Trig / Gate starts the loop from the beginning. A new pulse restarts it. Playback chooses Loop (keeps cycling) or Once (plays one pass and holds the last value). Gate: the loop runs while the gate is high and rests when it falls. A pulse at Reset sends the loop back to the start. Output. Depth scales the shape, Offset moves it up or down, Polarity chooses 0 … 1 or −1 … +1, and Slew rounds off the corners. Rate plays the loop at half or double speed (a quarter to four times). Step sends a pulse at the start of every shape, and Cycle a pulse at each start of the loop, to trigger other modules in time with the shapes. How to use it? Sidechain pump: Saw up on each beat (Length 4, Steps 4, four Saw up shapes) into a VCA's gain. Raise Slew a little for a softer pump. Rhythmic filter: Length 4 on 8 steps with Saw down, Plateau and Pulse mixed, into a filter's cutoff. One-shot swell: Sync Trigger, Playback Once, Length 8, a single Curve across a few steps; trigger it from a button. Auto-pan: Polarity Bipolar, Triangle shapes into a pan. Settings and knobs Setting Values Default Length 1 – 64 beats 4 Steps 1 – 32 4 Sync Transport, Trigger, Gate Transport Playback Loop, Once (Trigger sync only) Loop Polarity Unipolar, Bipolar Unipolar Knob Range Default Depth 0 – 100 % 100 % Offset −1 … +1 0 Slew 0 – 100 % 0 Rate 1/4×, 1/2×, 1×, 2×, 4× 1× Every knob is a modulation destination. Inputs Input Signal What it does Trig / Gate gate Starts the loop (Trigger) or runs it while high (Gate) Reset trigger Back to the start of the loop Outputs Output Signal What it does Out control The drawn shape, after Depth, Offset and Slew Step trigger A pulse at the start of each shape Cycle trigger A pulse at each start of the loop Demo patches Five whole patches show what Shape Sequencer does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Shape Sequencer under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Shape Sequencer: Sidechain Pump Four saw-up shapes, one per beat, are the gain of a held pad: each beat the sound ducks and swells back, like a sidechained compressor you can draw. Select a shape and drag its bend dot to change how quickly the pad recovers, or its start square to change how deep the duck goes. Shape Sequencer: Filter Steps A bar cut into eight steps mixes saws, plateaus, a pulse and a triangle, and moves a filter over an arpeggio so every eighth note opens differently. Set Steps to 16 and replace one shape with two shorter ones, or drag the yellow squares to change how high each shape lifts the cutoff. Shape Sequencer: Auto-Pan Set to Bipolar, two bars of triangles and plateaus swing a bell-like melody left and right: the shape's centre is the middle of the stereo field. Change Length to 16 beats for a slower drift, or raise Slew to round the corners. Shape Sequencer: One-Shot Swell A note every four bars triggers a four-bar shape, played once: a slow curve up, a peak and a long fall, which opens a filter and lifts a drone's volume together. Try Playback on Loop to hear it repeat on its own, or change Length to shorten the swell. Shape Sequencer: Steps as Triggers The Step output pulses at the start of every shape and Cycle once per loop, so the shapes themselves play drums: Step is the kick, Cycle the snare, while the shape swells the hats. Set Steps to 8 and paint two shapes into a step to double the kick pattern.

title: Neuron
text: Neuron Neuron in the module view Introduction Neuron holds two simple artificial neurons. Each one adds up three weighted inputs, lets the sum charge a leaky "membrane" and fires a gate when the membrane crosses a threshold. The two neurons listen to each other out of the box, so with no cable at all they already play a two-voice rhythm. Patch slow modulation in, or the outputs back into the inputs, and you get rhythms and gestures nobody programmed. How does it work? Sum. Each neuron computes W1 · In 1 + W2 · In 2 + W3 · In 3 . In 1 reads +1 while nothing is patched, so W1 works as a bias knob. In 2 reads 0 while nothing is patched. In 3 hears the other neuron while nothing is patched: its Out or its Gate , chosen with Cross , one sample late. That's a much tighter feedback loop than a cable could make. Membrane. The membrane follows the sum with a delay set by Leak : a short burst at the input moves it a little, a sustained input charges it fully. Leak 0 makes the membrane equal the sum. Gate. In Compare mode the gate is high while the membrane is above the threshold, with Hysteresis as a gap between the on and off levels (no chatter on wobbly inputs). In Spike mode the neuron fires : when the membrane crosses the threshold, the gate goes high for Pulse , the membrane drops to 0 and stays there during the pulse, then charges again. A constant input above the threshold gives a steady rhythm: the higher the input and the shorter the leak, the faster it fires. At or below the threshold it never fires. Out. A smooth version for modulation. In Compare mode it rises from 0 at the threshold with a slope of Sharp , up to 1. In Spike mode the ramp ends at the threshold, so Out shows the membrane charging and drops at each spike: a saw locked to the neuron's rhythm. Sharp 1 is gentle; 100 is almost a gate. Logic. AND , OR and XOR combine the two gates; Diff is A Out − B Out. Neuron has no randomness: the same inputs always give the same outputs. With Reset on Start on, both neurons are cleared when the transport starts, so every render is identical. How to use it? The default rhythm: patch A Spike and B Spike to two drums. A fires regularly from its bias; as A charges, its Out pushes B down, so B fires in irregular gaps. Rhythm from a level: an LFO or envelope into A In 2 : the higher the level, the faster A fires. Velocity to density: inside a Voice Cell, Voice In › Velocity into In 2 : louder notes fire faster. A Schmitt trigger: A Mode on Compare , a noisy signal into A In 2 , W1 0, Hysteresis up until it stops chattering. Audio: Leak near 0 and Cross on Gate oscillates at audio rate. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Neuron does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Neuron under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Neuron: Self-Playing Rhythm Two neurons charge up, fire and listen to each other, and that conversation is a drum pattern: A fires the kick, B the snare, and the logic outputs add hats and claps where they agree or differ. Change the Threshold or Leak of either neuron and the rhythm re-forms. Neuron: Spiking Melody Neuron A's gate plays the notes and its membrane level, passed through a Quantizer, picks the pitch: as the neuron charges the notes climb, then drop when it fires. Lower the Threshold for a faster tune, or raise Leak to flatten the climb. Neuron: Call and Response With Cross on Gate, each neuron's firing nudges the other, so a low bass note from A is answered by a high bell from B. Set Cross to Off and the two stop listening and drift apart; change B's W3 to turn the answer into a hesitation. Neuron: Slow Charge The neurons' membrane levels (A Out and B Out) are slow, irregular swells here: one fades a pad in and out and the other opens its filter. Lower Leak for longer swells, or raise Sharp on a neuron for a harder snap at the top. Neuron: Driven by an LFO A slow triangle LFO feeds the neurons' inputs: when it is high they fire fast and when it is low they go quiet, so a bass, tom and hat pattern speeds up and thins out in waves. Change the LFO Rate or the neuron weights to change the ebb and flow. Presets The preset bar of the Neuron view has 13 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Default Rhythm Two neurons that answer each other: a rhythm with no cables. Steady Pulse Two independent steady pulse trains, no cross talk. Slow Heartbeat Low, slow double-thump patterns. Fast Chatter Rapid spikes for glitchy triggers. Call and Response B only fires after A: a delayed answer. Mutual Silence Each neuron inhibits the other for alternating bursts. Compare Gates Self-switching gates that settle into slow on-off patterns. Smooth Out Gentle control outputs with soft slopes for modulation. Logic Mix Long pulses so the AND, OR and XOR outputs show overlaps. Gate Cross Neurons listen to each other's gates instead of their outputs. Independent Pair No cross talk: two polyrhythmic pulses of different speeds. Sparse Triggers Barely above threshold: occasional, slow triggers. Chaotic Pair Strong coupling creates unpredictable patterns. Reference Knobs and settings Per neuron (A and B): Control Range Default A / B W1, W2, W3 −2 … +2 A: 0.6, 1, 0.5 · B: 0.9, 1, −1 Threshold −1 … +1 0.5 Hysteresis 0 – 100 % 10 % Leak 0 – 5 s 250 ms / 400 ms Sharp 1 – 100 4 Pulse 1 ms – 1 s 30 ms (Spike mode only) Setting Values Default A Mode, B Mode Compare, Spike Spike Cross Out, Gate, Off Out Reset on Start on / off on W1 … W3: the weight of each input; negative weights inhibit. Threshold: the level the membrane must cross. Drag the dashed line in the view to set it. Hysteresis: the gap between the on and off levels: the gate switches on at Threshold + Hysteresis / 4 and off at Threshold − Hysteresis / 4. Leak: the membrane's time constant. 0 = no delay. Sharp: the slope of Out . Pulse: the gate length in Spike mode, and the time the membrane rests after firing. Cross: what In 3 hears from the other neuron while unpatched. Reset on Start: clear both neurons when the transport starts. All knobs are modulation destinations. Inputs Input Signal What it does A In 1, B In 1 control weighted by W1; unpatched: +1 A In 2, B In 2 control weighted by W2; unpatched: 0 A In 3, B In 3 control weighted by W3; unpatched: the other neuron (see Cross ) Reset trigger clears both membranes and ends any spike Outputs Output Signal What it does A Gate, B Gate gate the neuron's firing state A Out, B Out control, 0 … 1 the sharpened membrane A Spike, B Spike trigger a pulse each time the gate goes high AND, OR, XOR gate logic of A Gate and B Gate Diff control, −1 … +1 A Out − B Out

title: Random
text: Random Random in the module view Introduction Random produces a new random value on every step: the classic stepped "sample and hold" modulation. What makes it musical is its memory . The Loop knob moves it from always new values, through a pattern that slowly changes, to a fixed loop that repeats exactly. Every value comes from a seed, so a patch sounds the same every time you play it back. How does it work? Steps. Random moves to its next value on each step. Where the steps come from, in order of priority: Clock input patched: every rising edge at Clock is a step. Sync set to a note value: one step per note value at Live's tempo. While the transport plays, the steps are locked to the song position. Sync on Free: steps run at Rate , in Hz. Each new step fires a pulse at Trig . Memory. The values sit in a loop of Length slots. Each time the loop comes round, every slot gets a new value with a probability of 1 − Loop , and otherwise keeps the old one: Loop 0 %: every step is new. Pure randomness. Loop 50 %: about half of the values change each pass. A pattern that evolves. Loop 100 %: nothing changes. A locked sequence of Length steps. The values are a function of the seed and the step number, not of what came before. With Sync on and the transport running, the step number comes from the song position, so a section always plays the same values, even if you start playback in the middle. Starting the transport restarts the sequence. Shaping. Each raw value is scaled to Bias ± Spread and clipped to −1 … +1. Semitones rounds it to steps of 1/12 (one semitone at 1 V/oct). Smooth glides from one value to the next instead of jumping. How to use it? Random modulation: patch Out onto a filter's cutoff or an oscillator's shape. Set the depth with the cable's amount. Melodies: turn on Semitones , lower Spread (e.g. 25 % = ±3 semitones), patch Out into an Oscillator's Pitch and Trig into an ADSR's gate. Keep the cable amount at 100 % so the notes stay on semitones. Raise Loop until you like the phrase, then set it to 100 % to keep it. Find a different phrase: change Seed . Each seed is its own sequence. Play in time with something else: patch a clock or a gate into Clock , e.g. a Function's EOC or a sequencer's gate. Wandering, smooth modulation: raise Smooth for drifting values instead of steps. At 100 % the value glides over most of a step. Only positive values: set Bias to +0.5 and Spread to 50 % for 0 … 1. Presets The preset bar of the Random view has 14 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Quarter Steps Eight random levels per quarter-note step, mostly repeating. Locked Loop A fixed eight-step pattern that repeats exactly. Always New Never repeats: every step is fresh. Melody Generator Locked steps snapped to semitones: patch to pitch. Dark Walk Mostly low values with the occasional jump. Bright Sparks High-leaning fast steps for sparkly accents. Smooth Wander Free-running steps blended into a gliding random curve. Slow Drift Very slow random wander for subtle movement. Three Step Cycle A 3-step loop against 4/4 for polymetric feel. Five Against Four Five-step quantized loop that drifts across the bar. Narrow Wobble Small random variations: gentle humanizing. Long Pattern A long locked sequence of 32 steps. Slow Bar Changes One new value per bar for chord or key changes. Fast Glitch Rapid random steps for glitchy mod. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Random does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Random under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Random: Wandering Melody Every eighth note the Random module picks a new value; with Semitones on they land on exact notes, so a steady rhythm plays a never-repeating tune. Raise Spread for a wider range, move Bias up or down to place it higher or lower, or change Seed for a new tune. Random: Locked Loop Loop at its top setting repeats an eight-step random pattern exactly, here moving a bass line's filter in time with the drums. Turn Loop down and the pattern slowly mutates, down to fully new values every step; change Length to repeat after more or fewer steps. Random: Smooth Drift With Smooth turned up the random steps glide into one another, making a slow, irregular drift that moves a pad's brightness and tone. Lower Smooth to bring back the steps, or raise Rate to make the drift busier. Random: Tom Roll The Random module's trigger output fires a tom at irregular moments while its stepped output retunes it each time, a loose, tuned roll over a steady kick. Raise Rate for a busier roll or pull Spread in for a narrower range of pitches. Random: Raised Bells A high Bias and a narrow Spread keep the random notes in a bright upper range, like a music box wandering over a held drone. Set Bias to zero and widen Spread to bring the bells down across the whole range. Reference Knobs and settings Control Range Default Rate 0.05 – 50 Hz 2 Hz Spread 0 – 100 % 100 % Bias −1 … +1 0 Smooth 0 – 100 % 0 % Loop 0 – 100 % 0 % Sync Free, 1/32, 1/16, 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, 1 bar, 2 bars, 4 bars, 8 bars 1/4 Length 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 12, 16, 32 steps 8 steps Semitones on / off off Seed 0 – 999 1 Rate: steps per second. Only used when Sync is Free and Clock is not patched. Spread: the width of the range. At 100 % values cover −1 … +1 (around Bias ); at 0 % every value equals Bias . Bias: the centre of the range. Values beyond ±1 are clipped, so a high bias with a wide spread makes values stick to the top. Smooth: glide between values, as a share of the step length. 0 % jumps; higher values slide. The glide follows the step length, so it works the same at any rate or tempo. Loop: the chance that a slot keeps its value when the loop comes round. 0 % always new, 100 % locked. Sync: Free steps at Rate . A note value sets one step per note at Live's tempo (4/4 assumed). Ignored while Clock is patched. Length: the number of slots in the loop. It sets how long a locked pattern is before it repeats. Semitones: rounds each value to the nearest 1/12, i.e. to semitones for pitch inputs. The rounding happens before Smooth , so gliding still slides between the notes. Seed: picks the sequence. The same seed always gives the same values. Rate , Spread , Bias , Smooth and Loop are modulation destinations. Inputs Input Signal What it does Clock gate when patched, every rising edge advances one step; overrides Rate and Sync Outputs Output Signal What it does Out control, −1 … +1 the current value Trig trigger one pulse on every new step

title: Uncertainty
text: Uncertainty Uncertainty in the module view Introduction Uncertainty is six random generators in one module, each with a different character: two Fluctuating voltages that wander continuously, two Quantized voltages that jump between a few levels, a Stored value whose distribution you can skew and whose values can depend on each other, and an Integrated voltage that turns the stored values into random slopes. Whenever something in a patch should move unpredictably, one of these six probably fits. How does it work? Fluctuating 1 and 2 are smooth curves through random points. In Free mode the points come on average every 1 / Rate seconds, irregularly spaced so there is no audible pulse. With F Sync on a note value and the transport playing, the points sit on the grid and the curve is a function of the song position. Spread sets the size. The two have different default rates, so they rarely move together. Quantized 1 and 2 jump on each clock to one of 2, 4, 8 or 16 levels ( Bits 1 … 4). With Interval Even the levels spread evenly over 0 … 1 (1 bit is a random on/off voltage). With an interval in semitones each level is that many semitones above the last: 3 bits with 7 semitones jumps between eight notes a fifth apart. Few levels give a small vocabulary the ear hears as a pattern. Quantized 2 has its own Clock Q2 input; while it's unpatched it follows Quantized 1's clock divided by Q2 Divide . Stored takes a new value on each Store event. Three controls shape it: Correlation: how much each value depends on the previous one. 0 %: independent. Positive: each value stays near the last, a slow stepped wander. Negative: values alternate high and low, a zig-zag. The overall spread of values stays the same. Shape: Uniform , Bell (values gather in the middle) or Edges (values are pushed outward). Distribution: skews the values toward the top (+) or the bottom (−). Integrated uses Stored as a slope: it rises while Stored is positive and falls while it's negative, at a speed set by Integrate , and bounces back from ±1. The result is a line that changes direction and speed at every Store event. With positive Correlation it makes long sweeps; with negative Correlation it trembles around a point. Clocks. Each clock follows its input when patched, else the song position when its Sync is on a note value (at the synced length while the transport is stopped), else its Rate . A synced Fluctuating curve holds while the transport is stopped. Repeatable. Every value comes from Seed . Synced generators are a function of the song position and render the same from any start; the free ones and Integrated render the same from the same start. How to use it? Slow, organic movement: Fluct 1 and Fluct 2 to two filter cutoffs or pans. A small random melody: Quant 1 with Q1 Interval 2 semitones and 3 bits into an oscillator's pitch, Q Sync 1/8. Random octaves: Q2 Interval 12, Q2 Bits 2. A random on/off switch: 1 bit on Quantized 2, Q2 Divide /4. A drifting value per note: inside a Voice Cell, Voice In › Trigger into Store , Correlation +80 %: each note's value is near the last one. Random sweeps: Integrated to a filter cutoff, Correlation +60 %. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Uncertainty does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Uncertainty under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Uncertainty: Fluctuating Filter The two fluctuating curves wander at unrelated speeds: one opens and closes the filter on a plucked line, the other changes the tone shape. Raise F1 Rate and F2 Rate to speed them up, or lower F1 Spread to shrink the sweep. Uncertainty: Stepped Levels Quantized outputs jump between a few evenly spaced levels (Q1 Bits sets how many): Q1 pushes the pitch up by octaves and Q2 moves the filter, both in time with the eighth notes. Try Q1 Interval at 7 st for stacked fifths or raise the bits for more levels. Uncertainty: Stored Per Note Each note of the line tells the Store input to take a fresh stored value, which then holds until the next note; it sets the filter, and the Store Trigger output also fires a hi-hat. Raise Correlation so each value leans on the last, or move Distribution to favour low or high settings. Uncertainty: Integrated Drift The Integrated output is the running total of the stored steps, so it wanders like a slow random walk; here it steers the brightness of a held pad and the stored value tilts the oscillators. Change Integrate to make the walk shorter-lived or longer, and Store Rate for how often it is nudged. Uncertainty: Extreme Moods Setting Shape to Edges makes the random values favour the extremes, so the filter on this bass line jumps between very closed and wide open instead of sitting in the middle. Switch Shape to Bell or Uniform to hear it settle. Presets The preset bar of the Uncertainty view has 16 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Slow Random Drift Two lazy fluctuating curves: gentle analogue-style drift. Lively Fluctuation Faster, wider random curves for obvious movement. Synced Fluctuation Fluctuations that move in step with the tempo. Eighth Note Steps Two random step sequences: eighths and quarters. Sixteenth Chaos Dense sixteenth-note random steps with many levels. Octave Jumps Random steps in octave leaps: wild but tonal pitch jumps. Fifths and Fourths Random steps in fifths and fourths: open, melodic. Whole-Tone Walk Whole-tone random steps for a floating melody. Bell Distribution Values cluster near the middle, with rare extremes. Edge Seeker Values favour the extremes: dramatic jumps. Biased High Stored value skewed upward: mostly high, occasionally low. Correlated Walk Each stored value resembles the last: a gradual random walk. Anti-Correlated Stored values alternate high and low: a zigzag. Integrator Wander The integrated output smooths the stored value into slow glides. Slow Store Everything stretched over bars for evolving ambient control. Free Clocked Chaos All generators unsynced and fast: loose, jittery movement. Reference Knobs and settings Control Range Default F1 Rate, F2 Rate 0.01 – 20 Hz 0.5 Hz, 0.17 Hz F1 Spread, F2 Spread 0 – 100 % 100 % Q Rate 0.05 – 40 Hz 2 Hz Store Rate 0.05 – 40 Hz 1 Hz Distribution −100 … +100 % 0 % Correlation −95 … +95 % 0 % Integrate 0.01 – 10 /s 0.5 /s F Sync Free, 1/32 … 8 bars Free Q Sync Free, 1/32 … 8 bars 1/8 Store Sync Free, 1/32 … 8 bars 1/4 Q1 Bits, Q2 Bits 1 – 4 3, 2 Q1 Interval, Q2 Interval Even, 1, 2, 5, 7, 12 st Even Q2 Divide /1, /2, /3, /4, /8 /2 Shape Uniform, Bell, Edges Uniform Seed 0 – 999 1 F Rate: the average number of points per second of a Fluctuating curve (Free mode). Changing it stretches the curve; it never jumps. F Spread: the size of a Fluctuating output. Q Rate / Store Rate: the free clocks of Quantized 1 and Stored (shown while their Sync is Free ). Distribution, Correlation, Shape: shape Stored (see above). Integrate: the speed of Integrated per unit of Stored. Bits: 2^Bits levels. Interval: Even spreads them over 0 … 1; semitones stack them at 1 V/oct. Q2 Divide: while Clock Q2 is unpatched, Quantized 2 steps on every n-th step of Quantized 1. Seed: one seed; each generator has its own stream of it. All knobs are modulation destinations. Inputs Input Signal What it does Clock Q1 trigger each pulse steps Quantized 1 Clock Q2 trigger each pulse steps Quantized 2; unpatched: Quantized 1's clock / Q2 Divide Store trigger each pulse takes a new Stored value Outputs Output Signal What it does Fluct 1, Fluct 2 control, −1 … +1 continuously wandering voltages Quant 1, Quant 2 control (0 … 1, or 1 V/oct) stepped random on 2^Bits levels Stored control, −1 … +1 the stored value Integrated control, −1 … +1 random slopes from the stored values Store Trig trigger a pulse when Stored takes a new value

title: Wobble
text: Wobble Wobble in the module view Introduction Wobble turns one stream of random values into three shapes of movement. Stepped jumps to each new value, Smooth glides to it, and Wobble glides with momentum: it overshoots, wobbles around the value and settles. Patch them to related destinations (Stepped to pitch, Wobble to the filter) and the movements belong together. Around them sit bursts of quick triggers, a step clock, a Compare gate and a Chaos knob that feeds the module back into itself. How does it work? Steps. Wobble takes a new random value on each step. Steps come from: Clock patched: every rising edge. Sync on a note value: one step per note value. While the transport plays the steps are locked to the song position. Sync on Free: steps at Rate . Each step fires Clock . With Sample patched, each step samples that signal instead of taking a random value: a sample and hold with three output shapes. While Hold is high no new values are taken (and Clock stays quiet), but Smooth and Wobble keep settling. Smooth follows Stepped through a smooth low-pass filter. Smooth sets how slowly: at 0 % it almost jumps, at 50 % it arrives just in time for the next step, at 100 % it barely moves before the next value comes. The filter follows the step length, so the character is the same at any rate or tempo. Wobble uses the same filter with resonance. Wobble 0 % behaves like Smooth; higher values overshoot each new value and ring around it. When the next step comes before it settles, the wobbles overlap: that's where the bouncing comes from. Beyond ±1 the output is softly limited to ±1.5. Burst. On each step, with the chance Burst , a burst of 2 … Burst Size quick triggers fires over the first half of the step: rolls for drums or quick re-triggers of an envelope. Compare is high while Stepped is above Smooth: an irregular gate whose rhythm follows the movement. Chaos feeds the module back into itself. The new values are bent toward the current Smooth value and folded, so above about 40 % they cluster, run in streaks and break away. In Free mode fast wobbles also speed up the steps, and burst spacing gets irregular. Steps that follow the song position stay on the grid. Repeatable. The random values come from Seed and the step number. With Chaos at 0 and Sync on a note value, Stepped is a function of the song position. With Chaos up, a render from the same start position is always identical. How to use it? Three related movements: Stepped to an oscillator's pitch (through a quantizer), Wobble to the filter cutoff, Smooth to the pan. Bouncy filter: Wobble 80 %, Smooth 40 %, Sync 1/8, into a filter's cutoff. Slow drift: Smooth 100 %, Rate 0.1 Hz: a wandering line. One value per note: inside a Voice Cell, Voice In › Trigger into Clock : every note gets a new value that wobbles into place. Drum rolls: Burst into a drum's trigger, Burst 30 %, Sync 1/4. A sample and hold: patch a signal into Sample and a clock into Clock . Demo patches Five whole patches show what Wobble does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Wobble under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Wobble: Three Shapes One random stream, three ways: Stepped jumps the filter, Smooth glides the tone and Wobble overshoots and rings on the reverb. All three follow the same underlying values, so they feel related. Change Smooth and Wobble on the module to reshape the glides and overshoots. Wobble: Ringing Filter With Wobble high, every jump of the random value overshoots and rings before it settles, so the filter on this held chord seems to bounce. Reduce Wobble for a plain glide, or increase Chaos for a more unstable movement. Wobble: Burst Percussion The Burst output fires a quick run of triggers every so often: here they flutter a hi-hat and clap while the clock output keeps the kick steady. Raise Burst for more frequent runs, and change Burst Size for longer flutters. Wobble: Quantised Tune The Stepped output goes through a Quantizer to become a melody in a scale, and the Compare output decides when a note plays, so both pitch and rhythm are random but musical. Raise Wobble's Rate for a busier tune or change the Quantizer's Scale. Wobble: Sample and Hold A triangle LFO patched into Sample is read at each tick of the Wobble clock, and the Stepped output holds the value in between: a classic sample-and-hold filter pattern that stays related to the LFO. Change the LFO rate or the Wobble Sync to change the pattern. Presets The preset bar of the Wobble view has 15 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Gentle Wander Slow smooth random movement: gentle, subtle drift. Classic Sample and Hold Use the stepped output for random sample-and-hold steps. Lazy Steps Slow random jumps for evolving filter changes. Silky Glide Fully smoothed glides between random values. Springy Overshoot Wobble output overshoots and rings after each jump. Jelly Wobble Heavy ringing wobble: gelatinous pitch and filter motion. Synced Eighths Random steps locked to eighth notes.
