title: Resonator
text: Resonator Resonator in the module view Introduction The Resonator is a tuned body that rings when something hits it. Feed it any audio (a drum loop, noise bursts, a voice, a sequenced click) and it answers with pitched, physical-sounding tone: a struck bar, a plate, a bell, a plucked string, or a set of strings ringing in sympathy. Without input it is an instrument of its own: every trigger at Strum fires a small internal exciter. Up to four voices take turns on the strums, so chords and overlapping notes ring out naturally, and the Odd and Even outputs give a wide stereo image from a mono source. How does it work? Three models of the body: Modal: a bank of 16, 32 or 64 ringing partials. Structure sets their ratios: harmonic string (0 %), stiff string (25 %), free bar (50 %), membrane/plate (75 %) and a bell-like inharmonic set drawn from Seed (100 %), gliding smoothly in between. Sympathetic: eight strings with no excitation of their own. They pick up whatever matches their tuning in the input, like the sympathetic strings of a sitar. Structure chooses the tuning of the set: octaves, fifths, major, minor, sus, add9, detuned unisons, inharmonic. String: one plucked string (a waveguide), tuned exactly. Structure is its stiffness, from a soft nylon string to a metal bar. In every model Damping sets how long the fundamental rings, Brightness how much high content there is and how fast it dies, and Position where the body is struck and heard (50 % is the middle, which cancels the even partials). Voices and strums. With Polyphony 1 there is one voice: Strum fires the exciter and takes the current Pitch . With 2 or 4, each strum moves on to the next voice. That voice gets the input and follows Pitch ; the earlier ones ring out at the pitch they were strummed at. A strum on a voice that is still ringing adds to it, like hitting a string again. The internal exciter is a 3 ms burst of noise with a click, darker or brighter with Brightness , at the level of Exciter . With Strum Source › Input onsets , the Resonator listens to its input and strums on every hit it hears. A drum loop played into a four-voice Resonator then spreads its hits over the voices, and each hit takes the current Pitch . A body fed with a loud input in tune with its partials can build up far above the input level, so both outputs pass a soft limiter. How to use it? Tuned percussion from a drum loop: drum loop → In , Model Modal , Structure 50 – 100 %. Sequence Pitch , or use Input onsets with Polyphony 4 for overlapping notes. Plucked instrument: a sequencer's gate → Strum , its pitch → Pitch , Model String . Raise Damping for short plucks, Brightness for twang. Sympathetic shimmer: any melodic sound → In , Model Sympathetic , Structure at the tuning you like, Dry up to hear the source too. Stereo: Odd → left, Even → right. Width 0 % makes both the same. In a Voice Cell: keep Polyphony at 1 and let the cell provide the voices: Voice In › Trigger → Strum , Pitch → Pitch . Strum button: fires the exciter, for trying sounds without patching. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Resonator does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Resonator under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Resonator: Bell Strikes A sequencer strums the Modal model with its own internal exciter and pitches it, so each note rings like a struck bell or bar. Move Structure to change the metal, and Damping to shorten the ring. Resonator: Sympathetic Drone A plucked melody is fed into sympathetic strings tuned to a fixed root, so the drone strings glow along with whatever notes match them. Change Frequency to retune the drone, or Damping for a shorter shimmer. Resonator: Plucked Strings The String model plays a bouncy bass-and-treble pattern, four voices deep so older notes keep ringing under new ones. Try Position for a hollower or brighter pluck, and Brightness for nylon versus steel. Resonator: Drum Body A drum beat excites a Modal resonator that is tuned low, so every kick and hat rings the same plate-like body. Turn Dry up to bring the raw drums back, or sweep Frequency to retune the whole kit. Resonator: Morphing Plate A slow LFO sweeps Structure through string, bar and plate territory while the same strummed notes play, so the instrument seems to change material as it rings. Patch the LFO into Brightness too, or change its speed. Presets The preset bar of the Resonator view has 14 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Glass Bar A struck bar: bell-like tuned percussion. Hollow String A plucked string with a round body. Bright Harp Four plucked strings: arpeggios turn harp-like. Tuned Plate A metallic plate ring. Bell Tower Low, long bell with many partials. Sympathetic Drone Strings that ring along with a melody fed in. Sitar Shimmer Buzzing sympathetic strings. Drum Tuner Short tuned ring for drum loops. Damped Marimba Short, woody mallet tone. Kalimba Pluck Fast-decaying plucks. Eternal String A very long-ringing string. Wide Chord Body Four voices spread wide for chord-like clouds. Octave Metal High, clangy metal, bright and inharmonic. Onset Strummer Plays the string on every hit in the input; no strum cable needed. Reference Knobs and settings Control Range Default Frequency −48 … +48 semitones around C4 0 (C4) Structure 0 – 100 % 25 % Brightness 0 – 100 % 60 % Damping 0 – 100 % 45 % Position 0 – 100 % 30 % Input Gain −24 … +24 dB 0 dB Exciter 0 – 100 % 50 % Width 0 – 100 % 100 % Dry 0 – 100 % 0 % Model Modal, Sympathetic, String Modal Polyphony 1, 2, 4 1 Modes 16, 32, 64 (Modal) 32 Strum Source Jack, Input onsets Jack Seed 0 – 999 1 Frequency: the fundamental; Pitch adds to it. Modulation moves it in semitones. Structure: the partial ratios (Modal), the tuning of the set (Sympathetic) or the stiffness (String). Its name follows the model. Brightness: the high-frequency content: tilts the partials and makes the high ones decay faster; also colours the exciter. Damping: how long the fundamental rings: 0 % = 30 s, 50 % ≈ 1.2 s, 100 % ≈ 50 ms. Position: where the body is excited and heard. 0 % and 100 % are the ends; 50 % is the middle and cancels the even partials. Input Gain: the level of In into the body. Exciter: the level of the internal exciter on each strum. 0 % switches it off. Width: 0 % gives both outputs the mono sum; 100 % fully separates odd and even. Dry: the input (after Input Gain ) mixed into both outputs. Model: Modal, Sympathetic or String (see above). Switching fades the sound out and in again. Polyphony: how many voices take turns on the strums. Modes: the number of partials of the Modal body: more sounds richer and costs more. Strum Source: Jack strums only from the Strum input; Input onsets also strums on every hit detected in In . Seed: the bell partials (Modal, Structure 100 %), the inharmonic tuning (Sympathetic) and the exciter's noise. Every knob is a modulation destination: patch a cable onto it to move it. Inputs Input Signal What it does In audio the excitation; feeds the most recently strummed voice Strum trigger starts the next voice, takes Pitch for it and fires the exciter Pitch pitch 1 V/oct, 0 V = C4, added to Frequency ; the newest voice follows it Outputs Output Signal What it does Odd audio odd partials / odd strings / the first pickup: the left channel Even audio even partials / even strings / the second pickup: the right channel Mix audio Odd + Even, mono

title: Stretch
text: Stretch Stretch in the module view Introduction Stretch records what you send it and plays it back at another speed without changing the pitch : a voice at a quarter of the speed is still the same voice, a chord stretched to ten times its length becomes an evolving pad. It can also freeze a moment, scrub through the recording from a CV, shift the pitch independently, and run the recording backwards. It is stereo. Two things are its own. Hold Range loops a small window of the recording, so you can stay inside one syllable or one beat. And the stretch factor can wobble : a slow wave or a random walk modulates it, so time itself speeds up and slows down. How does it work? The module writes its input into a buffer (up to 30 seconds, you choose Length ). A play head moves through the recording at one divided by Stretch seconds of recording per second, and a loop goes round at the end. Two engines turn the head's position into sound: Grains cuts short overlapping grains from the head and plays them again. The grains are lined up by their waveforms, so a tone keeps its pitch. Grain is their length, Overlap how many sound at once, Scatter spreads where each starts: a clean texture at 0, a cloud at 100 %. Best for rhythmic and textural material, and cheap. Smear is a phase vocoder : it analyses the spectrum at the head and lets every partial go on turning at its own measured frequency. Tones stretch smoothly into long drones; transients smear. Window sets the frame length: 1024 is quicker, 4096 has the finest pitch resolution. Smear sounds are delayed by one window. Record says how the tape works: Once records from the start until Length is full (or until you press New Take , or a trigger arrives at New Take ), then stops; Rolling never stops and keeps the last Length seconds; Off plays what is there. Mix blends the live input (0 %) with the stretched sound (100 %). Stretch is the time factor, ×0.1 (ten times faster) to ×8 (eight times slower). Freeze stops the head; Reverse runs it backwards. Pitch shifts the sound up or down 24 semitones, independent of speed. Hold Range loops a window: Start is where it begins and Range how long it is, both as a share of the recording. Position moves the head by hand or CV. With Position Mode Offset it is added to the moving head (a CV makes the playback jump around); with Scrub it is the head itself: 0 % at the start of the window, 100 % at its end, and Stretch no longer matters. Scrubbing a frozen sound gives you a spectral scrubber. Wobble is the depth of the stretch modulation (up to ±1.5 octaves of factor), Wobble Rate its speed and Wobble Shape sine, random or saw. The Head output (0…1) shows where in its window the head is. How to use it? Slow a sound down: play something while Record is Once , then set Stretch to 4. Freeze a moment: switch Freeze on at the moment you like, or patch a button to the Freeze input. Pad from anything: Smear , Stretch 8, a bit of Wobble and Mix at 100 %. Granular scatter: Grains , a long Grain , Scatter high and Overlap 4×. Looping a syllable: Hold Range with a small Range ; move Start to pick the syllable. Scrub with a CV: Position Mode Scrub and an LFO or a pad into Position . Live stretching: Record Rolling with a short Length : the head slides through the last seconds of what you play. Slowed and low: Stretch 2 with Pitch −12 is the classic slowed-down sound. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Stretch does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Stretch under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Stretch: Melody into Pad A plucked loop is recorded into a four second rolling tape and played back four times slower by the Smear engine, so the notes melt into a slowly changing pad over a plain beat. Try Stretch at 8 for a still drone, Wobble for a drifting sense of time, or Mix lower to hear the live melody under the pad. Stretch: Granular Cloud An arpeggio is cut into 250 ms grains that are scattered around the play head, four at a time, while the head crawls through a four second tape at a quarter of the speed. The result is a shimmering cloud with the dry arpeggio underneath. Move Scatter between 0 and 100 %, shorten Grain for a glitchier texture, or raise Pitch. Stretch: Frozen Scanner A short chord progression is recorded once, then the tape is frozen and Position Mode is set to Scrub, so a slow LFO on Position sweeps a spectral scanner back and forth through the chords. It sounds like one sustained organ whose harmony slides between the recorded chords. Change the LFO rate, or turn Freeze off to hear the tape move again. Stretch: Hold Range Stutter Hold Range loops a window of only 4 % of a one-bar tape, which stutters a bright pluck line into a tiny repeating loop. A slow random source moves Start, so the stutter keeps landing on a different piece of the phrase. Change Range for longer or shorter loops, or Grains for a rougher edge. Stretch: Time Wobble A drum and bass loop is replayed from a rolling tape seven semitones up while Wobble with a random shape keeps changing the stretch factor, so the groove slows down, speeds up and smears as if time itself was swaying. Turn Wobble down for a steady pitch-shifted copy, or set Pitch to -12 for a heavy, slowed sound. Presets The preset bar of the Stretch view has 15 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Half Speed Plays the recording at half speed with the pitch where it was. Slow Motion Four times as long: transients melt, tones hold. Crawl The longest stretch with the finest frequency resolution. Double Time Twice as fast, same pitch. Granular Cloud Long scattered grains: a cloud made from the recording. Freeze Frame Stops time at the head and holds that moment as a drone. Scrub Pad Position is the play head: move it by hand or with a CV to scrub. Loop Window Loops a small window of the recording over and over. Time Wobble Time itself sways: the sound speeds up and slows down but never changes pitch. Drunk Time Time takes an uneven walk around a slow stretch. Backwards Smear The recording plays backwards, slowly. Octave Down Slow Half speed, an octave lower: the classic slowed-down sound. Shimmer Stretch A slow sheen an octave above, mixed under the live sound. Rolling Capture Keeps recording round a four-second loop while the head stretches through it. Stutter Loop A tiny window of the last seconds on repeat. Origin The Grains engine is waveform-similarity overlap-add; the Smear engine is the phase vocoder with identity phase locking. Both are published techniques, written for this module from their descriptions; no source code was ported.

title: Attenuverter
text: Attenuverter Attenuverter in the module view Introduction Makes two signals smaller, bigger, upside down or shifted, both by the same Scale and Offset . In the module view the knobs sit next to a line that shows the result. With nothing patched, an input is a knob you set by hand, so the Attenuverter is also a macro control: one Out can feed many destinations with the same value. How does it work? Each of the two inputs computes Out = In × Scale + Offset Scale runs from −2 to +2: +1 passes the signal unchanged, 0 mutes it, −1 turns it upside down, and values beyond ±1 boost a weak signal. Offset shifts the result up or down. An unpatched In counts as a constant +1 , so an empty input outputs Scale + Offset . Every cable already has its own amount at the destination. The Attenuverter is for scaling once, at the source: one knob changes the depth for every destination, and that knob can itself be modulated. How to use it? One depth for many destinations: LFO → In 1 , Out 1 to several knobs at full amount. Scale 1 now sets all depths at once. Macro knob: leave In 1 unpatched, set Scale to 0 and use Offset as a manual control. Patch Out 1 to several knobs and move them together. Unipolar from bipolar: an LFO (−1 … +1) with Scale 0.5 and Offset 0.5 runs from 0 to 1. Invert: Scale −1 makes an envelope fall instead of rise. Two signals, one depth: patch both into In 1 and In 2 and one Scale moves them together. Different settings? Add another Attenuverter; to add signals together use a CV Mixer. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Attenuverter does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Attenuverter under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Attenuverter: Opposite Sweeps One slow LFO enters two Attenuverters, one scaled +1 and one -1, and they open the left filter while closing the right one, so the arpeggio seems to travel across the stereo field. Change the scale of either one to unbalance the sweep. Attenuverter: Manual Offsets With nothing patched in, each Attenuverter is a constant set by its Offset: one transposes the sequencer up a fourth and the other holds the filter at a fixed opening. Turn the first Offset to change key while the music plays. Attenuverter: Wandering Sum Three unrelated modulators, a slow sine, a triangle and a smooth random line, are summed by a CV Mixer and the Attenuverter sets how far the total sweeps the filter along a path that rarely repeats. Change the Attenuverter scale for a wider or narrower sweep, or a CV Mixer level to give one modulator more say. Attenuverter: Hard-Clipped Sweep A triangle LFO is doubled by the Scale and hard-clipped, so the filter spends most of the time fully open or fully closed and only moves quickly in between. Set Clip to Off or Soft to round the sweep, or lower Scale to reduce the effect. Attenuverter: Kick Ducking A kick's envelope goes through an Attenuverter set to scale -1 with offset +1, turning a short burst into a short dip, and that dip pumps the volume of a chord pad on every beat. Lower the negative Scale for a gentler duck. Reference Knobs and settings Control Range Default Scale −2 … +2 +1 Offset −1 … +1 0 Clip Off, Soft, Hard Off Scale: the gain. Negative values invert. Offset: added after scaling. Clip: limits both outputs to ±1. Soft leaves values up to ±0.8 untouched and bends smoothly into ±1; Hard cuts off at ±1. Inputs Input Signal What it does In 1, In 2 control The signals. Unpatched: a constant +1. Outputs Output Signal What it does Out 1, Out 2 control In × Scale + Offset, for each input

title: CV Mixer
text: CV Mixer CV Mixer in the module view Introduction The CV Mixer combines up to four modulation signals into one. Adding them up is only one way: it can also average them, follow whichever is highest or lowest, or scan across them with one knob. Simple shapes combined like this become complex, living modulation. How does it work? Each channel's input is multiplied by its Level (−1 … +1, so it can also invert). Then Mode decides how the four channels combine: Sum: all channels added. Average: the sum divided by the number of channels in use. Max: the highest channel at every moment. Min: the lowest channel at every moment. Scan: a crossfade from channel 1 to channel 4, set by the Scan knob. The result is multiplied by Master , Offset is added, and Clip keeps it in range. Inv is the same signal upside down; Abs is its absolute value. A channel counts as "in use" when its input is patched. Channel 1 also counts when unpatched with a Level other than 0: its input then reads +1, so Level 1 works as a manual offset. Max , Min and Average ignore unused channels. How to use it? Blend two LFOs: a slow and a fast LFO into In 1 and In 2 , mixed by their levels. Two simple waves give a much less predictable shape. A floor for an envelope: envelope and a slow LFO into two channels, Mode Max . The output follows the envelope, but never falls below the LFO. Pick a modulator with one knob: four different sources, Mode Scan , and patch an LFO or a macro onto Scan to move between them. Bipolar to unipolar: Abs turns a −1 … +1 LFO into a 0 … 1 shape at twice the rate. Demo patches Five whole patches show what CV Mixer does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick CV Mixer under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows CV Mixer: Three Waves Summed A sine, a triangle and a stepped random line are added by the CV Mixer in Sum mode, and the result sweeps the arpeggio's filter in a pattern that takes a long time to come round. Pull a channel's Level to zero to hear its share disappear. CV Mixer: Averaged Drift Four smooth random lines are averaged into one gentle, never-settling signal that detunes a two-voice pad, so the chord drifts in and out of tune with itself. Change Mode to Sum for a wilder drift, or raise Master to deepen it. CV Mixer: Max Swells Two unipolar LFOs at different speeds go into Max mode, which always passes the larger one, so the pad swells whenever either wave rises and the volume rarely falls to silence. Switch to Min to hear it only when both are high. CV Mixer: Min as a Gate Maker Two square LFOs of different lengths go into Min mode, which only stays high while both are high, an AND of the two, and the result opens the envelope on a held chord to cut it into a shifting rhythm. Change either LFO's sync to rewrite the pattern. CV Mixer: Scanning Four Notes Four stepped random lines sit in the four channels and Scan, swept by a slow triangle, fades from one to the next; the result is snapped to a scale to play the oscillator, so the tune walks between four moving lines. Move Scan by hand to pick which channel you hear. Reference Knobs and settings Control Range Default Level 1–4 −1 … +1 +1 (channel 1), 0 (others) Scan 0 … 1 0 Master 0 … 2 1 Offset −1 … +1 0 Mode Sum, Average, Max, Min, Scan Sum Clip Off, Soft, Hard Soft Level: each channel's level; negative values invert it. Scan: only used in Scan mode. 0 is channel 1, 1/3 channel 2, 2/3 channel 3, 1 channel 4; in between, the two neighbours crossfade. Master: gain on the combined signal. Offset: added after Master . Clip: Soft leaves values up to ±0.8 untouched and bends smoothly into ±1; Hard cuts off at ±1; Off doesn't limit. Soft is the default because four full-scale signals added up easily leave the range. Inputs Input Signal What it does In 1–4 control The channels. In 1 unpatched reads +1; In 2–4 read 0. Outputs Output Signal What it does Out control The mix Inv control −Out Abs control the absolute value of Out

title: Math
text: Math Introduction Two rows of arithmetic for audio and control signals. Each row applies one operation to two values, A and B: add, subtract, multiply, divide, power, min or max. How does it work? Each row computes Out = A op B Every input has a constant knob next to it. An unpatched input reads its knob; a patched input replaces it, and its knob is ignored. So a row takes two signals, or one signal and a constant, or two constants. Add, Subtract: A + B, A − B. Multiply, Divide: A × B, A ÷ B. Dividing by a B very close to zero is limited so the result stays finite, and B keeps its sign. Power: A raised to B. A negative A keeps its sign: −2 ^ 2 is −4, not 4. Min, Max: the lower or higher of the two at each moment. Outputs are limited to ±1000, and never become NaN or infinite. A row whose output isn't patched does no work. How to use it? Scale and offset: Multiply with a constant B, then Add with a constant. Invert around 1: Subtract with A at 1 and a signal into B. Reciprocal: Divide with A at 1 and a signal into B. Squaring or square root: Power with B at 2 or 0.5. Clamp a signal: Min with a constant B as the ceiling, then Max with a constant as the floor. Combine two LFOs: Max or Min takes the upper or lower envelope. Reference Knobs and settings Control Range Default Op 1, Op 2 Add, Subtract, Multiply, Divide, Power, Min, Max Multiply, Add A1, B1 Constant −10 … +10 +1 A2, B2 Constant −10 … +10 0 The constants are modulation destinations. Inputs Input Signal What it does A1, B1 control Row 1 operands. Unpatched: the constant knob. A2, B2 control Row 2 operands. Unpatched: the constant knob. The inputs accept audio and pitch signals too. Outputs Output Signal What it does Out 1 control A1 op B1, limited to ±1000 Out 2 control A2 op B2, limited to ±1000

title: Matrix Mixer
text: Matrix Mixer Matrix Mixer in the module view Introduction A grid of up to 8 inputs by 8 outputs . Every crosspoint is a gain from −1 to +1, so each output is its own mix of all the inputs. It mixes audio (send and return busses, feedback networks, spreading one sound to several effects) and control signals (blending LFOs into many related movements). Every crosspoint is a knob you can modulate, and whole matrices can be stored as snapshots and morphed . How does it work? The mix. Out j = Level j × Σ (gain i→j × In i) . Inputs and Outputs set how many rows and columns are in use; jacks beyond them are hidden (their cables stay) and carry nothing. An unpatched input is 0, or 1 with Unpatched = 1, so its row becomes a set of fixed offsets. Crosspoints. In the grid a circle's size is the gain, warm colours are positive, cool ones negative. Click an empty crosspoint for +1, a set one for 0; Alt-click for −1; drag up and down to set it (Shift: fine); double-click to type a value. Every crosspoint is also a knob: cables can modulate it, even at audio rate (ring modulation). Changes ramp over 20 ms, so recalling a snapshot doesn't click. Mutes silence a row with a 5 ms ramp. Level sets each output from silent to +6 dB. Output Stage. Clean passes everything (limited to ±10). Soft clip rounds peaks above 0.9 smoothly towards ±1. Normalize divides each output by the sum of its gains when that is above 1, so a column never gets louder than its loudest input: feedback patches stay tame. Snapshots. The eight buttons below the grid hold whole matrices (gains, levels, mutes). Click recalls one, Shift-click stores the current matrix, right-click renames, clears or makes it morph end A or B. Morph. With Morph on, the gains blend from snapshot A to snapshot B as the Morph knob turns ( Morph Curve : Linear, Smooth, Equal power); levels blend too, mutes switch halfway. Cables on crosspoints still add on top. Editing a crosspoint then edits the snapshot nearest the Morph position, so move Morph to 0 % or 100 % to shape either end. Feedback. Patching an output back into an input works (one 32-sample delay); with Normalize such loops stay stable. How to use it? Effect sends: inputs are sounds, outputs go to a delay and a reverb; each crosspoint is a send amount. A feedback network: outputs through delays or filters back into the inputs, Normalize on, gains around ±0.5. Modulation blender: four LFOs in, eight related modulations out. Scene changes: store snapshots, patch a slow LFO into Morph . Demo patches Five whole patches show what Matrix Mixer does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Matrix Mixer under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Matrix Mixer: Four Into Stereo Four sources (bass, chords, lead, drums) go into a 4 by 2 matrix, each with its own left and right gain: the bass sits in the middle, the chords lean left, the lead right and the drums are spread. Click a crosspoint to change how much of a source goes to which side. Matrix Mixer: Scene Morph Two stored snapshots: A is a sparse scene with bass and a pad, B adds drums and the lead on the right. A slow LFO on Morph blends smoothly between them, so the arrangement builds and thins by itself. Drag Morph by hand, or edit a snapshot's crosspoints. Matrix Mixer: Voice Swap A saw arpeggio and a square arpeggio enter a 2 by 2 matrix. Each output carries a mix of both, and two LFOs in opposite phase move the crossing gains, so the voices drift from one side to the other and back. Change a gain to a negative value to hear phase effects. Matrix Mixer: One to Many One plucked line fans out to four outputs through four crosspoints with different gains; outputs 1 and 2 go to the speakers and outputs 3 and 4 pass through delays on the other side, so a single melody turns into a stereo echo field. Raise or lower the 1 to 3 and 1 to 4 gains to place the echoes. Matrix Mixer: Soft Clip Stage Four loud parts are summed into one output with every crosspoint at full gain, and the Output Stage setting is Soft clip, so peaks are rounded off instead of cutting hard. Try Clean and Normalize for the other behaviours, or turn Level 1 down to rebalance. Reference Knobs Knob Range Default i → j (64) −1 … +1 1 on the diagonal, else 0 Level 1 … 8 0 – 200 % 100 % Morph 0 – 100 % 0 % Every knob is a modulation destination. The knob list shows only the rows and columns in use. Settings Setting Values Default Inputs 1 – 8 4 Outputs 1 – 8 4 Mute 1 … 8 on / off off Output Stage Clean, Soft clip, Normalize Clean Unpatched 0, 1 0 Morph Off, On Off Morph Curve Linear, Smooth, Equal power Linear Inputs Input Signal What it does In 1 … In 8 audio (any signal) the sources Outputs Output Signal What it does Out 1 … Out 8 audio Level × the weighted sum of the inputs, after the output stage

title: Multiplier
text: Multiplier Multiplier in the module view Introduction Two multipliers that compute X × Y, with both signals allowed to be negative. With audio it's a ring modulator: metallic, bell-like tones from two oscillators. With modulation it lets one signal control the depth of another, for example an LFO whose depth follows an envelope. How does it work? Each section computes Out = (X + Bias X) × (Y + Bias Y) × Gain An unpatched Y reads +1, so the section simply passes X at Gain . An unpatched X2 takes Out 1 . Patch three signals into X1, Y1 and Y2 to multiply all three together. Bias adds a constant before multiplying. With Bias Y at 1, a bipolar Y gives amplitude modulation (the original tone stays); at 0 it's ring modulation (the original tone disappears, only sum and difference tones remain). Unlike the VCA, the Multiplier treats both inputs the same, has no response curve, and lets the gain go negative. Multiplying two audio signals creates new frequencies, which can fold back as aliasing. Oversampling computes the product at 2× or 4× the sample rate and filters it. This adds a short latency, so leave it off for modulation. How to use it? Ring modulator: two oscillators into X1 and Y1 , Out 1 to an output. Detune one oscillator for bell tones; set Oversampling to 4× for high notes. Tremolo with character: audio into X1 , an LFO into Y1 , Bias Y1 at 1. Depth from an envelope: LFO into X1 , envelope into Y1 : the LFO only moves while the envelope is open. Squaring: the same signal into X and Y. A sine becomes a sine at twice the frequency, an LFO gets a rounder, always-positive shape. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Multiplier does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Multiplier under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Multiplier: Ring Mod Bells Two sine oscillators multiplied together make only their sum and difference tones, which are not whole-number multiples of the note: clangorous bells that fade with each strike. Change the second oscillator's Coarse to retune the bell. Multiplier: Offset Tremolo A saw melody goes into X1 and a sine LFO into Y1, with Bias Y1 lifting the LFO above zero so it works as a smooth tremolo; without the bias the sound would also flip its phase. Lower Bias Y1 toward zero for a deeper, rougher ring. Multiplier: Envelope Times LFO Every note's decay envelope is multiplied by a slow LFO before it reaches the filter, so the notes open the filter wide when the LFO is high, hardly at all when it is low and even invert when it dips below zero. Raise Bias Y1 to keep the LFO positive. Multiplier: Twin Ring Modulators Both multipliers ring-modulate the same saw melody, one with a modulator at a fifth above and one at a ratio that sits between notes, and each goes to its own side: left is nearly musical, right is metallic. Change either modulator's Coarse to move the clangour. Multiplier: Robot Drums A whole drum loop is multiplied by a low sine so each hit turns pitched and robotic, mixed with the untouched loop underneath. Raise Oversampling to keep the highs clean, or change the sine's Coarse to tune the robot. Reference Knobs and settings Control Range Default Bias X1, Bias X2 −1 … +1 0 Bias Y1, Bias Y2 −1 … +1 0 Gain 1, Gain 2 −2 … +2 +1 Oversampling Off, 2x, 4x Off Inputs Input Signal What it does X1, Y1 control First multiplier. Y1 unpatched reads +1. X2, Y2 control Second multiplier. X2 unpatched takes Out 1; Y2 unpatched reads +1. The inputs accept audio and pitch signals too. Outputs Output Signal What it does Out 1 control (X1 + Bias X1) × (Y1 + Bias Y1) × Gain 1 Out 2 control the same for the second section

title: Utility
text: Utility Utility in the module view Introduction Utility is the glue between modules. It scales, inverts, offsets and mixes control signals, then shapes the result: rectify, fold, quantize to semitones or sample and hold. It can smooth the result with a slew and turn it into a gate with a comparator. Whenever a signal is almost what you need, put a Utility in between. How does it work? The signal passes through four stages, in this order: Mix: X × Scale X + Y × Scale Y + Offset . The scales are attenuverters: +1 passes the input unchanged, 0 mutes it, −1 inverts it. Mode: one shaping function (see Mode below). Slew: a smoothing filter that limits how fast the value can change. Outputs: Out is the result, Inv is the same value inverted, and Gate is high while Out is above Threshold . With nothing patched, Out is simply the Offset : a constant you can set by hand or modulate. How to use it? Attenuate or invert: patch a signal into X and set Scale X . At −1 an LFO runs the other way. Unipolar from bipolar: an LFO running −1 … +1 into X , Scale X 0.5, Offset 0.5 gives 0 … 1. Mix two modulators: one into X , one into Y , and balance them with the two scales. Quantized melodies: feed a slow random or LFO into X , choose Quantize , and patch Out into an oscillator's Pitch . Sample and hold: patch noise or an LFO into X , a clock into Clock , and choose Sample & Hold for stepped values on each clock. Portamento and smoothing: raise Slew to round off steps from a sequencer or Random. For pitch that gives glide. Wavefolding: choose Fold and push the level with Scale X or Offset beyond ±1. Folding turns a simple LFO into a complex shape. Gates from control signals: use Gate with a Threshold . An LFO into X becomes a square gate; an envelope follower becomes a trigger when a sound gets loud. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Utility does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Utility under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Utility: Sample and Hold Melody A slow triangle LFO is sampled by an eighth-note clock in Sample & Hold mode, and the stepped result is snapped to a scale to play the oscillator: a tune that never repeats. Change the LFO rate for a different walk, or pick another Mode to hear the raw values. Utility: Slew Glide The sequencer's pitch passes through the Utility's Slew before it reaches the oscillator, so every leap turns into a slide. Turn Slew down for sharp steps, or up until the notes smear into one long wail. Utility: Folded Sweeps Two slow LFOs are added in the Utility and together they swing past plus and minus one, where Fold reflects them back, so the filter on the arpeggio keeps turning around at new places. Switch Mode to Through to hear the same sweeps without the folds. Utility: Comparator Claps A slow triangle plus a fast sine run through the Utility, and its Gate output goes high whenever the sum rises above Threshold: the ripples cross the line in bursts and trigger the claps. Move Threshold to make the claps sparse or dense. Utility: Rectified Tremolo A sine LFO into Rectify mode flips its negative half upwards, so the pad's volume pulses at twice the LFO speed, always rising from silence. Change the LFO rate for a slow pulse or a fast shimmer, or switch Mode to Through for a plain tremolo. Reference Knobs and settings Control Range Default Scale X −1 … +1 +1 Scale Y −1 … +1 0 Offset −1 … +1 0 Slew 0 – 5 s 0 s Threshold −1 … +1 0 Mode Through, Rectify, Fold, Quantize, Sample & Hold Through Scale X: gain for the X input. Negative values invert it. Scale Y: gain for the Y input. It starts at 0, so Y does nothing until you turn it. Offset: a constant added to the mix. Shifts a signal up or down, or acts as a manual control on its own. Slew: smoothing time (a one-pole lag). The output covers about two thirds of a jump in this time. 0 is instant. The knob's centre is 100 ms. Threshold: the level Out must exceed for Gate to go high. Mode: how the mixed signal is shaped before the slew: Through: unchanged. Rectify: the absolute value; negative parts flip up. An LFO becomes a bouncing shape at twice the rate. Fold: anything beyond ±1 is reflected back inside, again and again. More input level means more folds. Quantize: rounded to steps of 1/12: semitones at 1 V/oct. Sample & Hold: the value is taken on each rising edge at Clock and held until the next. Scale X , Scale Y , Offset , Slew and Threshold are modulation destinations. Modulating Scale X from an envelope makes a simple VCA for control signals. Inputs Input Signal What it does X control first input, scaled by Scale X Y control second input, scaled by Scale Y Clock gate rising edges sample the signal in Sample & Hold mode X and Y take audio, pitch and control signals alike; they are just numbers. Outputs Output Signal What it does Out control the result (limited to ±10) Gate gate high while Out > Threshold Inv control − Out

title: Coin Toss
text: Coin Toss Coin Toss in the module view Introduction Coin Toss is a probability router. Every gate or trigger that arrives at its input is sent to output A or to output B , decided by a weighted coin. There are two channels, so one clock becomes two complementary rhythms that keep changing. Every toss comes from a seed, so a rendered song sounds exactly like the live playback. How does it work? Tosses. Each rising edge at In tosses the coin. Probability is the chance that it lands on B : 0 % always A, 100 % always B, 50 % a fair coin. In 2 listens to In 1 while nothing is patched into it, so channel 2 makes its own decision on the same events. Memory. With Memory above 0 % a toss sometimes simply repeats the last result instead of flipping a new coin. You get runs of A and runs of B, while the long-term balance stays the same. At 50 % the runs are about twice as long. Modes. Trigger: the chosen output copies the input gate (same length); the other stays low. A trigger in gives a trigger out. Latch: the chosen output goes high and stays high until a toss chooses the other side. A and B are always opposite: a random switch. Toggle: a toss that lands on B swaps which output is high; one that lands on A changes nothing. Probability becomes the chance of a change. Link. Independent: each channel tosses its own coin. Shared: one coin for both, compared against each channel's own Probability . If channel 1's probability is lower, channel 2 always goes B when channel 1 does: nested probability, e.g. hats at 70 % and an open hat at 20 %, never one without the other. Opposed: one coin, but channel 2 reads it from the other end, so the channels avoid each other: B on both never happens as long as the two probabilities add up to 100 % or less. In Shared and Opposed the tosses happen on channel 1's edges; In 2 only sets channel 2's gate lengths. Repeatable. Each channel counts its tosses. Reset (or a transport start) sets the count to 0, so the same decisions follow again. Loop makes the count wrap after 2 … 32 tosses: a fixed random rhythm that repeats. Change Seed for another one. How to use it? Two rhythms from one clock: patch a clock or a sequencer's gate into In 1 , A 1 to one drum, B 1 to another. Ghost notes: Probability 15 %, B 1 into a quieter second voice. Fills that build up: an LFO or a slow envelope on Probability 1 . A random switch: Mode 1 on Latch , Coin 1 into a crossfader or a sequential switch's address. Nested hats: Link on Shared , Probability 1 20 % (open hat on B 1 ), Probability 2 70 % (closed hat on B 2 ). A fixed random pattern: Loop on 8 or 16, and a Reset from the bar (e.g. the Step Sequencer's End ) so it stays on the bar. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Coin Toss does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Coin Toss under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Coin Toss: Kick or Snare Every eighth-note gate is sent either to a kick or to a snare by a fair coin, so the backbeat is never the same twice, over a fixed hat and bass line. Push Probability 1 up for more kicks, or change Seed for a different run of luck. Coin Toss: Weighted Hats A steady sixteenth-note stream is split by a loaded coin: four tosses in five give a closed hat and the rest an open one, over a plain kick and clap. Move Probability 1 toward 0.5 for a busier, more open hat line. Coin Toss: Looped Fate Eight eighth-note tosses decide whether a low note or a high note sounds, and Loop makes the same eight outcomes repeat, so a tune made by chance settles into a pattern you can hum. Set Loop to Off and it never repeats; change Seed for another tune. Coin Toss: Chord Roulette Once a bar the coin picks one of two pads, an A minor chord or an F major chord; in Latch mode the chosen side stays on until the next toss, so one chord always sounds. Raise Memory 1 and the coin tends to repeat the last result. Coin Toss: Opposed Channels With Link set to Opposed, channel 2 always chooses the other side from channel 1: when the first coin sends a gate to the kick, the second sends its gate to the hat, and the other way round. Try Shared to make both coins land together. Presets The preset bar of the Coin Toss view has 12 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Fair Coin Each gate goes to A or B at random, half and half. Mostly A Most gates go to A, B only sometimes: an occasional accent. Mostly B Most gates go to B, A only now and then. Rare Fill A very rare toss: a fill every so often. Sticky Streaks High memory repeats the last result: long runs on one side. Alternating Feel Two channels play opposite results for call-and-response. Shared Toss One toss decides both channels together. Latch Switch The chosen output stays on until the next toss. Toggle Flip Each toss can flip the output on or off. Loop Four Four tosses repeat in a loop: random but a repeating pattern. Loop Sixteen A sixteen-toss pattern that repeats for a bar of variation. Loop Three vs Eight Short loops give a rhythm that keeps shifting. Reference Knobs and settings Control Range Default Probability 1, 2 0 – 100 % 50 % Memory 1, 2 0 – 100 % 0 % Mode 1, 2 Trigger, Latch, Toggle Trigger Link Independent, Shared, Opposed Independent Loop Off, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 32 tosses Off Seed 0 – 999 1 Probability: the chance that a toss chooses B. Read at the moment of the edge, so modulating it never cuts a gate. Memory: the chance that a toss repeats the last result. Mode: see above. Changing it while a gate is high sets the outputs low until the next toss. Link: how the two channels' coins relate. Loop: the number of tosses before the decisions repeat. Seed: picks the sequence of tosses. Probability and Memory are modulation destinations. Inputs Input Signal What it does In 1 gate each rising edge tosses channel 1's coin; the gate is routed to A 1 or B 1 In 2 gate the same for channel 2; unpatched it listens to In 1 Reset trigger both toss counters back to 0; Latch and Toggle back to A Outputs Output Signal What it does A 1, B 1, A 2, B 2 gate the routed gates (see Mode ) Coin 1, Coin 2 control, 0 … 1 1 while the last toss chose A, 0 after B

title: CV to Gate
text: CV to Gate Introduction Turns a control signal into a gate. When the input rises above Threshold the gate goes high. It either stays high while the input does, or lasts a fixed time. How does it work? Length at 0: the gate follows the input. It is high while the input is above Threshold and falls when the input drops a little below it (a small hysteresis stops chatter on noisy signals). Length above 0: every time the input rises through Threshold a gate of that length fires, however long the input stays high. A new crossing during a pulse restarts it. How to use it? LFO to rhythm: an LFO into In , Threshold near the top, Length short. Each peak fires a short gate. Envelope follower to trigger: drums into an envelope follower, its output here: a trigger on each loud hit. Comparator: leave Length at 0. Reference Knobs and settings Control Range Default Threshold −10 … +10 0.5 Length 0 … 10 s (0 = follow the input) 0 Both are modulation destinations. Inputs Input Signal What it does In control The signal to compare. Outputs Output Signal What it does Gate gate High (1) or low (0).

title: Index
text: Index Introduction The Index turns a signal into a whole-number step : 0, 1, 2 … up to Steps − 1. Its main job is to drive things that are not knobs: a dropdown (an oscillator's Octave , a filter's Type , a chorus Mode ), a toggle, or a parameter in Ableton Live through a Live Params node. A cable on such a setting sets its value, and the Index sends exactly the position it reads. How does it work? Out carries the step as step / (Steps − 1) : 0 for the first choice, 1 for the last. Patch it to a dropdown and it picks that choice. Set Steps to the number of choices of the target (2 for a toggle); the Index cannot see the target, and a wrong number lands on a neighbour. Index carries the plain whole number, for the Math module or a display. Changed (optional) pulses when the step changes. Mode decides where the step comes from: CV splits the input In into Steps equal bands. An LFO, a sequencer lane or a knob picks the step; a little hysteresis stops a noisy CV from flickering at a border. Input Range says whether the input runs 0…1 or −1…+1. Count moves on triggers: Up , Down and Reset , in Order ( Forward , Backward , Ping-Pong , Random with a Seed ). Wrap wraps at the ends or stops. With Up unpatched and a Rate set, the step follows the song. Gates has Gate Inputs jacks: the highest gate that is high picks its step (Gate 1 is step 0). With none high, Default Step applies. Binary adds the gates up: Gate 1 is 1, Gate 2 is 2, Gate 3 is 4. Three gates reach eight steps; one gate is an on/off switch. Offset adds floor(Offset × Steps) to the step in every mode, wrapping. How to use it? Toggle on a square wave: a square LFO into In , Steps 2, Out onto a toggle or two-choice dropdown. Walk a dropdown: Mode Count with a clock into Up , or with a Rate set to follow the song. Pick with hits: drum lanes into the Gate jacks in Gates mode. Drive Ableton: Out into a Live Params row mapped to a menu or switch in Live; Steps is the number of items. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Index does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Index under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Index: Octave Walk With nothing patched into Up, the Index follows the song: every half bar it moves one step in Ping-Pong order over 7 steps, and the step goes to the Oscillator's Octave dropdown, so the melody climbs and falls through seven octaves. Change Order or Rate. Index: Chorus or Flanger A square LFO is one bar low, one bar high. The Index with 2 steps turns that into 0 or 1, and 0 or 1 picks the Chorus or the Flanger mode. Two steps make any gate or square wave an on/off switch for a toggle. Index: Sweeping the Filter Types A very slow triangle LFO crosses the 32 bands of the Index, and the step goes to the Filter's Type dropdown, so every few seconds the same riff goes through another kind of filter. Set Steps to the number of choices of whatever you drive. Index: Three Switches, Seven Waves Three square LFOs at one, two and four bars act as three switches. The Index in Binary mode adds them up (1, 2, 4), and the sum picks the wave of a vibrato LFO that wobbles the filter. A counter in four lines of patch. Index: Hits Pick the Octave The kick, snare and hat of the drum grid are three gates into the Index in Gates mode: a kick drops the next notes three octaves, a snare two, a hat one, and with none high the Default Step 3 is the octave you wrote. Try another Default Step.

title: Logic
text: Logic Logic in the module view Introduction Logic combines gates and triggers the way digital circuits do: AND, OR, XOR and their inverses, a flip-flop, and edge detectors. Two rhythms become a third, a clock is divided by two, and a gate turns into triggers at its start and end. How does it work? Every input is either high or low . It goes high when the signal rises above Threshold , and low again when it falls below Threshold minus Hysteresis . The hysteresis keeps slow or noisy signals from flickering around the threshold. The logic outputs combine A and B , plus C when it is patched: AND: high when all are high. OR: high when any is high. XOR: high when an odd number are high (for two inputs: when they differ). NAND , NOR: AND and OR inverted. NOT A: A inverted. An unpatched A or B counts as low, so AND needs both patched. That makes B an enable: AND of a clock and a gate passes the clock only while the gate is high. The flip-flop ( FF ) changes state on each trigger at Flip (or on each rising edge of A, see Flip Source ). Reset sets it low. Rise and Fall fire a trigger when A goes high and low. Change fires whenever AND, OR or XOR changes. How to use it? Rhythm from rhythms: two clocks or patterns into A and B. AND plays where they meet, XOR where they differ, OR everything. Mute a clock: clock into A, a gate into B, use AND . Clock ÷ 2: clock into A, Flip Source on A Rising Edge , use FF . Chain more Logic modules for ÷ 4, ÷ 8. Gate to triggers: a gate into A; Rise fires at the start, Fall at the end. Patch Fall into an envelope for a sound on note release. Pulses from an LFO: an LFO into A, Threshold 0.8; NOT A is low only near the LFO's peaks. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Logic does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Logic under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Logic: Two Lanes, Three Drums Two gate patterns, one irregular and one straight eighths, feed the Logic module: where both hit (And) the kick plays, where only one does (Xor) the snare, and Or adds a soft hat on every hit of either. Change either lane on the Drum Grid and the drums rearrange themselves. Logic: Flip-Flop Beat Swap Each kick flips the flip-flop, so its output is high on one beat and low on the next; one arpeggio plays while it is high and a second one while it is low, taken from a chained Logic module that inverts it. Speed up the flips for a stutter, or reset them for a fixed phrase. Logic: Edge Detectors A square wave is fed into Logic, and its Rise output fires a kick when the wave goes up, Fall a snare when it comes down, and Change a closed hat at either edge. Narrow the square's pulse width and the snare moves away from the kick. Logic: Nor, Nand and Not Three square waves at different speeds are combined three ways: Nor fires the kick when all of them are low, Nand the snare when any one drops, and Not-A a rim on the second half of A's cycle. Change any wave's speed to find new patterns. Logic: Three Lengths Collide Three sequencers of three, four and five steps run in parallel and drift in and out of phase; Logic turns their gates into a drum part, with And as a rare accent on the kick, Xor on the rim and Or on the hats. Change a sequencer's Length and the whole rhythm shifts. Reference Knobs and settings Control Range Default Threshold −1 … +1 0.5 Hysteresis 0 … 0.5 0.02 Flip Source Flip Jack, A Rising Edge Flip Jack Threshold: the level at which an input counts as high. Applies to every input, including Flip and Reset . Hysteresis: how far below Threshold an input must fall to count as low again. Flip Source: what toggles the flip-flop. Inputs Input Signal What it does A, B gate The main operands. Unpatched: low. C gate Optional third operand for AND, OR, XOR. Unpatched: ignored. Flip trigger Toggles FF Reset trigger Sets FF low; wins over a toggle on the same sample Outputs Output Signal What it does AND, OR, XOR gate The logic of A, B (and C) NAND, NOR gate AND and OR inverted NOT A gate A inverted FF gate The flip-flop Rise, Fall trigger When A goes high, when A goes low Change trigger When AND, OR or XOR changes

title: Patch Bay In
text: Patch Bay In Introduction The Patch Bay In collects signals into one bundle cable. Patch any signal into its free input and it becomes a channel, named after what you patched; a new free input appears. Take the Bundle output to a Patch Bay Out, here or on the other side of a cell. How does it work? A Patch Bay In and a Patch Bay Out are a pair. They stay in step by themselves: the Patch Bay Out always shows the channels of the Patch Bay In its bundle comes from. Nothing is processed: the engine turns every channel into a plain cable, so a patch bay costs nothing while it plays. How to use it? A panel for a module: put the dials that control a module in a cell, collect them in a Patch Bay In, send the bundle out of the cell, and put a Patch Bay Out next to the module. One bundle replaces a cable per dial. The Warm Saws preset is built this way. A long way across the board: one bundle cable instead of several parallel ones. Reference The jacks, the signal types and how the bundle is resolved are in the design, doc/specs/modules/patchbay.md . A bundle carries any signal except notes.

title: Patch Bay Out
text: Patch Bay Out Introduction The Patch Bay Out gives you the channels of a bundle back as separate outputs, named like the signals that went into the Patch Bay In at the other end. Cable them to knobs or inputs as you would any other output. How does it work? A Patch Bay In and a Patch Bay Out are a pair. They stay in step by themselves: the Patch Bay Out always shows the channels of the Patch Bay In its bundle comes from. Nothing is processed: the engine turns every channel into a plain cable, so a patch bay costs nothing while it plays. How to use it? A panel for a module: put the dials that control a module in a cell, collect them in a Patch Bay In, send the bundle out of the cell, and put a Patch Bay Out next to the module. One bundle replaces a cable per dial. The Warm Saws preset is built this way. A long way across the board: one bundle cable instead of several parallel ones. Reference The jacks, the signal types and how the bundle is resolved are in the design, doc/specs/modules/patchbay.md . A bundle carries any signal except notes.

title: Route
text: Route Introduction The Route sends its In to one of up to eight outputs. It takes any signal: audio, pitch, control, gate or trigger. Use it to send one melody to a chosen quantizer or voice, one drum to a chosen effect, or one clock to a chosen destination. A knob, a CV, a trigger or the song decides where the signal goes, and every change fades, so audio doesn't click. How does it work? Choosing the output. The Outputs setting (2 … 8) sets how many outputs there are; the unused jacks are hidden, and cables from them are kept. Select divides its range into one slot per output. With 4 outputs, 0 … 0.25 picks Out 1 , 0.25 … 0.5 picks Out 2 , and so on. Turn the knob, or patch a CV onto it: an LFO sweeps the signal through the outputs, a sequencer lane picks them, and a gate picks between two. A little hysteresis keeps a noisy CV from flickering at the borders. Next moves one output on each trigger, in Order : Forward , Backward , Ping-Pong or Random (never the same output twice, with Seed choosing the sequence). Select adds an offset, so a slow CV can sweep the outputs while triggers shift where the sweep starts. With Next unpatched and a Rate set, the Route follows the song, locked to the bars. Slot Triggers (off by default) gives the Route one trigger jack per output, Trig 1 … Trig N . A trigger on Trig k jumps straight to output k , and the next Next continues from there. Set it to the number of outputs you want to address. The other outputs. With Idle Outputs Zero the outputs that aren't selected are silent. With Hold they keep the last value they had, and fade back into the live signal when their turn comes. Hold is right for pitches and other control values; Zero for audio. Changing smoothly. Each change fades over Fade . The short default (2 ms) removes clicks from audio; 0 switches instantly, right for gates and stepped values. A change in the middle of a fade continues from what's playing, so fast switching never jumps. Fade Curve Equal Power keeps the loudness even between two different destinations; Linear is right for modulation. How to use it? Pick a voice: a quantized melody into In , Out 1–3 to three voices, a trigger into Next to hand the melody to the next voice. Pick an effect: a drum into In , Out 1–4 to a dry path, a delay, a filter and a reverb; a slow LFO onto Select . Roll a chord: a pitch into In , Idle Outputs Hold , a clock into Next , Out 1–4 to four oscillators: each oscillator keeps its note until its turn. One trigger per destination: Slot Triggers 3, drum lanes into Trig 1–3 ; each lane hit aims the signal at its output. Both ways round: pair a Route with a Select driven by the same clock to send one signal through one of several processors and pick up its result. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Route does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Route under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Route: One Melody, Three Voices One wandering melody is quantized once and sent to three different voices in turn by the Route: a bright saw, a hollow pulse and a soft sine, each for one bar. Set Idle Outputs to Hold and a voice keeps its last note while it waits. Route: A Slow LFO Sends the Riff Around A slow triangle LFO on the Select knob moves one riff between four treatments: dry, a long echo, a low-pass filter and a big reverb. The 120 ms Fade blends from one to the next; at 0 it cuts, at 1 s it morphs. Route: Slot Triggers Aim the Hit Slot Triggers is set to 3: a trigger on Trig 1, 2 or 3 aims the Route at that output. One snare hit is sent to a dry output, a short room or a long hall depending on which Drum Grid lane fired just before it. Route: Hold Keeps Every Voice Singing Idle Outputs is Hold: a new note goes to the next of four drones every bar, and each drone keeps the pitch it last got until its turn comes again. The result is a four-note chord that rolls forward one note at a time. Route: Random Hits Around Four Voices One hi-hat pattern is dealt out at random to four differently tuned percussion filters, one step at a time, by a Route that follows the song at 1/8 (nothing is patched into Next). Change Seed for another order, or Order to Forward for a fixed rotation. title: Select
text: Select Introduction The Select picks one of up to eight inputs and passes it to Out . It takes any signal: audio, pitch, control, gate or trigger. Use it to choose between three quantizers, cycle through melodies, or switch between sound sources. A knob, a CV, a trigger or the song decides which input is heard, and every change fades, so audio doesn't click. How does it work? Choosing the input. The Inputs setting (2 … 8) sets how many inputs there are; the unused jacks are hidden, and cables to them are kept. Select divides its range into one slot per input. With 4 inputs, 0 … 0.25 picks In 1 , 0.25 … 0.5 picks In 2 , and so on. Turn the knob, or patch a CV onto it: an LFO sweeps through the inputs, a sequencer lane picks them, and a gate picks between two. A little hysteresis keeps a noisy CV from flickering at the borders. Next moves one input on each trigger, in Order : Forward , Backward , Ping-Pong or Random (never the same input twice, with Seed choosing the sequence). Select adds an offset, so a slow CV can sweep the inputs while triggers shift where the sweep starts. With Next unpatched and a Rate set, the Select follows the song, locked to the bars. Slot Triggers (off by default) gives the Select one trigger jack per input, Trig 1 … Trig N . A trigger on Trig k jumps straight to input k , and the next Next continues from there. Set it to the number of inputs you want to address. Changing smoothly. Each change fades over Fade . The short default (2 ms) removes clicks from audio; 0 switches instantly, right for gates and stepped values. A change in the middle of a fade continues from what's playing, so fast switching never jumps. Fade Curve Equal Power keeps the loudness even between two different sounds; Linear is right for modulation and for two versions of the same sound. An unpatched input counts as silence (0). How to use it? Pick a quantizer: the same random or sequence into three Quantizers set to different scales, their outputs into In 1–3 , Out to the oscillator. Turn Select , or patch a trigger into Next . A/B switch: Inputs 2 and a gate (a square LFO, a button) onto Select : low is In 1 , high is In 2 . Sweep sources: four oscillators into In 1–4 and a slow triangle LFO onto Select . One trigger per source: Slot Triggers 3, drum lanes into Trig 1–3 ; each lane hit jumps to its input. Carry a gate along with a pitch: use two Selects driven by the same CV, one for the pitch and one for the gate, with Fade 0. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Select does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Select under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Select: Three Scales in Turn One wandering random value goes into three Quantizers set to different scales; the Select hands the melody to the next scale every bar with a short crossfade. Set Order to Random, or turn the Select knob by hand. Select: A Slow LFO Sweeps the Sources Four oscillators play the same riff and a slow triangle LFO on the Select knob sweeps through them, so the sound changes shape by itself. The Fade of 80 ms blends neighbours; set it to 0 for hard cuts or 600 ms for a smooth morph. Select: A/B Melodies on a Gate Two different sequences feed a two-input Select, and a square LFO used as a gate on the Select knob flips between them every two bars: low plays the first melody, high the second. With only two inputs, any gate is an A/B switch. Select: Slot Triggers Pick the Drum Slot Triggers is set to 3: a trigger on Trig 1, 2 or 3 jumps straight to that input. Two lanes of the Drum Grid pick between kick, snare and clap, so the one voice the Select lets through changes with the groove. Remove a cable to hear just one drum. Select: Rotating with the Song With nothing patched into Next, the Select follows the song at its Rate: one new drone every two bars, in Ping-Pong order, with a one-second crossfade. Lengthen Fade for a slow morph, or choose Random and another Seed. title: Switch
text: Switch Switch in the module view Introduction The Switch is a sequential switch with up to 8 steps. It picks one of eight inputs for its Out , and at the same time sends its In to one of eight outputs. The step moves on each trigger, follows the song, or is chosen with the Select knob. It can cycle through melodies, pick a sound source, send one sequence to several voices in turn, or, with nothing patched, be an 8-step sequencer of knob values. How does it work? One step, two sections. The current step chooses: 8 → 1: which of In 1 … In 8 plays at Out . Each input is multiplied by its Level . An unpatched input plays its Level as a constant, so the eight Level knobs are eight steps of a value sequencer. 1 → 8: which of Out 1 … Out 8 gets In . The other outputs are silent ( Idle Outputs Zero ) or keep their last value ( Hold ). Moving the step. Length sets how many steps are used (2 … 8). A trigger at Step moves one step in Direction : Forward , Backward , Ping-Pong , Random (never the same step twice) or Random Walk (one step up or down at random). Reset goes back to the first step. With Step unpatched and a Rate set, the switch steps with the song, locked to the bars: after a loop it is at the same step again. Select adds an offset: with Length 4, 0 … 0.25 is no offset, 0.25 … 0.5 one step, and so on. With nothing stepping, Select chooses the step; patch an LFO onto it to sweep through the steps. Changing smoothly. Each change fades over Fade . Short fades (the default 2 ms) remove clicks from audio; 0 switches instantly, right for gates and stepped values. A change in the middle of a fade continues from what's playing, so fast switching never jumps. Fade Curve Equal Power keeps the loudness even between two different sounds; Linear is right for modulation and for two versions of the same sound. With Mode Glide , Out doesn't crossfade but slides from the old value to the new one over Fade : portamento for a value sequencer driving a pitch. Gate drops for one sample at every step change (to restart envelopes), Changed fires a trigger, End fires when the steps start a new round, and Position tells where the switch is. How to use it? Source selector: four oscillators into In 1–4 , Out to the filter. Turn Select , or patch a slow random onto it. 8-step sequencer from knobs: leave the inputs unpatched, set the Levels , a clock into Step (or set Rate ), Out to an oscillator's pitch through a Quantizer. Gate plays an envelope on each step; Mode Glide adds slides. Alternating melodies: two sequencers' Pitch into In 1–2 , Length 2, one sequencer's End into Step . Spread notes over voices: one random source into In , Idle Outputs Hold , a clock into Step : eight outputs, each with its own held value. Rhythmic routing: a drum into In , Out 1–4 to four different effects, Rate 1/16, Direction Random . Demo patches Five whole patches show what Switch does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Switch under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Switch: Four Timbres in Rotation The same riff is played by four different oscillators, and the Switch hands the output to the next one every half note with a short crossfade: saw, hollow pulse, triangle and a bright octave. Change Direction to Ping-Pong or Random, or lengthen Fade to blend the voices. Switch: Random Walk Textures Four sustained layers, a soft pad, a breathy noise band, a deep sine and a shimmering high chord, are slowly crossfaded by the Switch in Random Walk order, one step at a time, so the texture wanders without ever jumping. Change Seed for another route. Switch: One Riff, Four Treatments Used the other way round, one input goes to eight outputs: a single riff is sent to a dry output, an echo, a high-pass filter and a huge reverb in turn, each for half a bar. Try Direction Random or Length 2 to make it jump between only two of them. Switch: Gliding Drone Chords Four sine drones stacked on different chord tones are passed one at a time through the Switch in Glide mode and ping-pong order, with a long Fade so each tone seems to slide into the next. Change Mode to Crossfade for a cleaner blend or Fade for a quicker move. Switch: Drum Voice Carousel One drum pattern plays four different drums at once, but the Switch lets only one of them through, stepping to the next each bar by a trigger: the same groove turns from kick to snare to clap to tom. Lengthen the Length setting to add silent bars, or change Direction. Reference Knobs and settings Control Range Default Level 1–8 −1 … +1 +1 Select 0 … 1 0 Fade 0 … 2 s 2 ms Length 2 … 8 4 Direction Forward, Backward, Ping-Pong, Random, Random Walk Forward Rate Off, 1/32 … 8 bars Off Fade Curve Equal Power, Linear Equal Power Mode Crossfade, Glide Crossfade Idle Outputs Zero, Hold Zero Seed 0 … 999 1 Rate: only used while Step is unpatched. One step per this length, locked to the song position. Seed: chooses the sequence of the random directions. Inputs Input Signal What it does In 1–8 audio The sources for Out . Unpatched: the Level as a constant. Any signal type passes. In audio The source for Out 1–8 Step trigger Moves one step Reset trigger Back to the first step Outputs Output Signal What it does Out audio The selected input Out 1–8 audio In at the selected output Gate gate Low for one sample at each step change, high otherwise End trigger When the steps start a new round Position control The current step, 0 (first) … 1 (last) Changed trigger A pulse at each step change

title: Chord Quantizer
text: Chord Quantizer Chord Quantizer in the module view Introduction One pitch in, a chord out. The input picks the chord's root, the module builds a chord on it, inverts and voices it, and plays it on four pitch outputs and a Notes output. Patch a melody in and get a chord that moves with it; switch on Voice Leading and each new chord picks the inversion that moves the voices least, so a jumpy sequence turns into smooth changes. How does it work? Mode decides how the root and the chord are found: Chromatic: the root is the input rounded to the nearest semitone and Chord chooses the chord (Major, Minor, Dominant 7, … Quartal). Diatonic: the input snaps to Root + Scale , and Chord chooses a stack of scale steps (Triad, Seventh, Sus4, Ninth, …). The chord quality follows the key: in C major a Triad on D is D minor. With Harmony on a bus, key and scale come from the Harmony Master. Follow: the chord is the Harmony Master's current chord (slash bass included); the input only moves it up and down. Without a Harmony Master on the bus it acts as Diatonic and says "no harmony". Voices sets how many notes the chord has (1–4). With fewer than the chord has, the fifth goes first, then extensions, the seventh, the third; with more, the root, fifth and third are doubled an octave up. Inversion moves the lowest voice up an octave (or the highest down, for negative values). Voicing spreads the chord: Drop 2 and Drop 3 move the 2nd or 3rd voice from the top down an octave, Spread opens it into a wide pad (bass down, the rest at least a fourth apart), Open moves every second voice up an octave. A voicing that needs more voices plays Close. Register. The chord is moved by octaves so its lowest voice ( Anchor = Bass ), its middle ( Centre ) or its top voice ( Top ) is as close to the input as possible. Range folds voices more than that many octaves above the bass back down. Voice Leading. Smooth tries every inversion of the next chord in a few octaves and plays the one whose voices move least (and that stays near the input). Smooth + Top also keeps the top voice still where it can, like a held melody note. Inversion is ignored then. Trig. Unpatched, the chord follows the input all the time; Hysteresis keeps a slightly noisy input from flickering between roots. Patch a trigger and the input is read only on each pulse, then held. A pulse that gives the same chord plays it again. Strum. With Strum above 0 a new chord reaches the voices one after the other ( Strum Order Up: bass first), spread over the Strum time. How to use it? Chords from a melody: a Step Sequencer's Pitch into Pitch , its Trigger into Trig , Notes into a Voice Cell. Smooth pads: Voice Leading Smooth , Voicing Spread , a slow sequence of roots. Follow the song's chords: Mode Follow , Harmony = the Harmony Master's bus; patch an LFO into Pitch to move the chord's register. Four oscillators: Voice 1 … 4 into four oscillators instead of a Voice Cell; Change retriggers their envelopes. Gated chords: patch a gate into Gate : notes sound only while it is high. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Chord Quantizer does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Chord Quantizer under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Chord Quantizer: Minor Seventh Pad A slow root line goes into the Chord Quantizer, which stacks each root as a minor seventh over four voices; the four oscillators swell into a lush, moving pad. Try Chord on Dominant 9 or Sus4, or Voicing on Spread for a wider sound. Chord Quantizer: Smooth Voice Leading Rhythmic triad stabs follow a four-chord loop, and Voice Leading chooses the inversion that moves least, so the top voice glides instead of jumping. Turn Voice Leading Off to hear every chord land in root position. Chord Quantizer: Quartal Glass Instead of thirds, each chord is stacked in fourths and spread wide: an open, floating sound that suits slow, bell-like notes. Try Inversion or Range to move the stack, or Chord to Fifth for a hollow drone. Chord Quantizer: Diatonic Harmoniser In Diatonic mode a melody in C major is harmonised note by note: each pitch becomes the root of the right triad for the scale, major on some steps, minor on others. Change the Stack to Seventh, or the setting Scale to Dorian. Chord Quantizer: Chords into an Arpeggio The Notes output of the Chord Quantizer holds each chord while an Arpeggiator breaks it into a running pattern for a single pluck voice. Change the chord, then the Arpeggiator's Pattern or Octaves, to reshape the same harmony. Presets The preset bar of the Chord Quantizer view has 15 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Major Triads Plain major triads on whatever root comes in. Minor Seventh Stabs Minor sevenths in Drop 2 voicing: warm, jazzy stabs. Dominant Seventh Bluesy dominant chords, first inversion. Diatonic Triads Triads that follow the key: major, minor and diminished as the scale dictates. Diatonic Sevenths Seventh chords built from A natural minor. Smooth Pad Voice leading with a wide spread for a flowing pad. Dorian Ninths Open ninth chords in Dorian, gently strummed. Suspended Air Unresolved sus4 chords that glide between roots. Quartal Voicing Stacked fourths: modern, open and unresolved. Power Fifths Two-note fifths for heavy, simple riffs. Slow Harp Strum A wide strum rolling the chord upward like a harp. Downward Strum Minor ninths strummed from the top down. Whole-Tone Augmented Every chord is augmented: ambiguous and shimmering. Top Voice Anchor Keeps the top voice near the melody while the chords change underneath. Follow the Key Takes the chord from a Harmony Master (set Harmony to its bus). Reference Knobs Knob Range Default Chord Chromatic: Unison … Quartal; Diatonic: Single … Quartal Major / Triad Inversion −3 … +3 0 Strum 0 – 100 ms 0 Velocity 1 – 100 % 80 % Every knob is a modulation destination. Chord is a dropdown (a cable can drive it) that shows the table in Chromatic and the scale stacks in Diatonic. Settings Setting Values Default Mode Chromatic, Diatonic, Follow Chromatic Root C … B C Scale the 17 scales Major Harmony Off, Bus A – D Off Voices 1 – 4 4 Voicing Close, Drop 2, Drop 3, Spread, Open Close Voice Leading Off, Smooth, Smooth + Top Off Anchor Bass, Centre, Top Bass Range 1 – 4 octaves 2 Strum Order Up, Down Up Hysteresis 0 – 50 % of a semitone 10 % Inputs Input Signal What it does Pitch pitch picks the root (and the register) Trig trigger patched: the chord is read at each pulse and held Gate gate patched: notes sound while it is high Outputs Output Signal What it does Voice 1 … Voice 4 pitch the chord, low to high; unused voices repeat the highest Root pitch the chord's root, at or above Voice 1 Notes notes the chord as notes; voices that keep their pitch keep sounding Change trigger a pulse when the chord changes

title: Harmony Master
text: Harmony Master Harmony Master in the module view Introduction Harmony Master says what key and chord the music is in right now, for the whole board. Modules that follow harmony (the Quantizer Suite and the Chord Quantizer, set to the same Bus ) quantize to it instead of their own Root and Scale: change the chord here and every follower changes with it, on every track of the Live set. The chord comes from the knobs, from a progression that runs with the song, or from chords you play into its Notes input. Its own outputs carry the key, the root, the bass and the chord tones as pitches, and the chord as notes. How does it work? Key and scale. Key and Scale set the key. Every chord is built in it. Source chooses where the chord comes from: Manual: the chord on scale degree Degree (1–7) with Quality . Diatonic Triad and Diatonic Seventh stack every other scale note, so degree 2 in C major is D minor, degree 5 with a seventh is G7. Any other quality (Sus4, Major 7, …) is built on the degree's note as it is. Patch a sequencer or a slow Random into Degree to walk through the key's chords. Progression: up to 16 slots, drawn in the view. Each slot has a root (a degree, or a fixed note C … B), a quality, an optional bass note (for slash chords) and a length in beats. Advance decides how it moves: Transport follows the song position, so loop jumps and renders always land on the right chord; Trigger moves one slot per pulse at Next ( Reset goes back to slot 1); Select plays the slot the Slot knob points at. When the transport stops, the chord holds. Detect: the chord is recognised from the notes held at Notes . Notes must be stable for 30 ms, so a strummed chord counts once. The lowest note is the bass, so C E G A is A minor 7 over A and C6 over C. With Latch on the last chord stays when you let go; off, it falls back to the Manual chord. Scale Policy. Keep publishes the scale as set. Adapt bends it to contain the chord: in A minor, an E major chord turns the scale into A harmonic minor while it lasts, so followers play the G♯. Transpose shifts key and chord by the input, in semitones. In Progression it takes effect at the next chord change (or Next/Reset), so a sequencer on it changes key in time with the progression; otherwise at once. Bus. The context goes to bus A, B, C or D. Followers pick the same bus. If two Harmony Masters share a bus, the first one wins and the other shows a warning and publishes nothing. How to use it? One key for the whole set: put a Harmony Master on the board, set the key, switch the followers' Harmony to Bus A . A progression: choose Progression . Click a slot to edit it, drag its right edge to change its length, + adds a slot. Play the changes: choose Detect , patch a MIDI input's Notes into Notes and play chords; the arpeggios and bass lines follow. A pad that plays the chord: patch Notes into a Voice Cell. Notes that stay in the next chord keep sounding. A bass line: Root or Bass into an oscillator; Change restarts its envelope at every chord change. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Harmony Master does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Harmony Master under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Harmony Master: Minor Journey A minor progression (i, VI, III, VII) runs with the transport; its Tone outputs hold a warm pad, Bass walks underneath and a sequenced lead on the bus rewrites itself to stay inside each chord's scale. Change Key or Scale and the whole board follows.
