Keyboard: Latched Arp The Keyboard's Notes output feeds an Arpeggiator set to Latch: a bass line and beat run alone until you press a few keys, and when you let go they keep arpeggiating until you press a new chord. Change the Arpeggiator's Pattern or Octaves to hear the same keys differently. Keyboard: Hold Drone Hold is on and Priority is Lowest, so the keys you click stay down and the lowest one sets a slow drone under a gentle bell melody. Click the same key again to release it, or press All off to clear the keys. Reference Knobs Knob Range Default Velocity 1 – 100 % 80 % Glide 0 – 2 s 0 s Every knob is a modulation destination. Settings Setting Values Default Octave −3 – +3 0 (C3 – C6) Priority Last, Lowest, Highest, First Last Hold Off, On Off Outputs Output Signal What it does Notes notes every key played Pitch pitch the active key, 1 V/oct Gate gate high while any key is held Velocity control the active key's velocity Trigger trigger a pulse each time the active key changes

title: Wheel
text: Wheel Wheel in the module view Introduction The Wheel is a pitch or mod wheel as a control signal. Drag it up and down and Out follows; with Spring on it returns to the middle when you let go, like the wheel on a keyboard. Patch Out onto an Oscillator's Pitch for a pitch bend, or onto a filter's cutoff for a mod wheel. How does it work? Out goes from Min at the bottom of the wheel to Max at the top. The default range is −1 to +1 with the wheel centred, so at rest Out is 0. For a mod wheel that rests at the bottom, set Min to 0 and turn Spring off. Spring (on by default) moves the wheel back to the middle when you let go. Off, it stays where you leave it. Smooth glides Out to a new position instead of jumping. A cable into Value moves the wheel like a hand would. In a panel, a Wheel control drives this module. How to use it? Pitch bend: Out onto an Oscillator's Pitch , cable amount ±2 semitones. Mod wheel: Min 0, Max 1, Spring off, Out onto a filter's Cutoff . Demo patches Five whole patches show what Wheel does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Wheel under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Wheel: Pitch Bend A lead line plays while the Wheel sits at rest in the middle (zero) and feeds the sequencer's Transpose input at a small amount: push it up or down and the whole line bends by a couple of notes, then springs back when you let go. Turn Spring off to leave it where you put it. Wheel: Fold Wheel Min is 0 and Spring is off, so this Wheel behaves like a mod wheel that stays where you leave it: it raises the wavefolder inside a dual oscillator, turning a plain tone into a bright, buzzing one. Drag it slowly across the tune and listen to the overtones appear. Wheel: Crunch Ride The Wheel rides the Drive and bit depth of a Crunch effect on a whole beat and bass: at rest the groove is clean and warm, pushed up it breaks into grit. Min is 0 here, so the wheel only adds grit; set it to -1 and the lower half takes the drive below the starting point. Wheel: Phaser Sweep A chord-like arpeggio passes through a slow phaser whose Centre frequency is steered by the Wheel instead of its LFO: roll it up and the notches climb, down and they sink. Raise the phaser's Feedback to make the sweep more vocal. Wheel: Tape Bend The Wheel pushes the delay time of a tape-style echo while a pluck melody plays: nudge it and the echoes slide in pitch as the tape speeds up or slows down, then settle when the wheel springs home. Turn Smooth up for lazier moves. Reference Knobs Knob Range Default Value 0 – 100 % 50 % Min −1 – +1 −1 Max −1 – +1 +1 Smooth 0 – 2 s 20 ms Every knob is a modulation destination. Settings Setting Values Default Spring off, on on Outputs Output Signal What it does Out control the wheel's position, scaled from Min to Max

title: Arpeggiator
text: Arpeggiator Arpeggiator in the module view Introduction The Arpeggiator plays the notes you hold one at a time , in a pattern, in time with the transport or a clock. Hold a chord and it becomes a running line. Its Notes output plays a Voice Cell directly; Pitch , Gate , Velocity and Trigger drive modules outside one. How does it work? The held notes form a pool, lowest first. Octaves repeats the pool one octave higher per copy (up to four), and Pattern chooses the order: Up / Down: lowest to highest, or the other way. Up-Down / Down-Up: there and back; the top and bottom notes are played once per cycle. Up & Down: there and back; the top and bottom notes are played twice. Played: in the order you pressed the keys. Random: any note, chosen with Seed . The same seed gives the same line every time, also in a render. Converge: lowest, highest, second lowest, second highest, and so on towards the middle. Diverge: from the middle outwards. One step lasts one Rate (1/1 … 1/32T). Gate Length sets how much of the step the note sounds, Swing delays every second step. With nothing patched into Clock , the steps lock to the song position, so the transport has to be running. Patch a trigger into Clock and every pulse is one step, whatever the transport does. A pulse into Reset ends the note and the next step starts the pattern again. With Latch on, the notes keep playing after you let go. The next key you press starts a new chord. Switch Latch off to stop. Adding or releasing keys while it plays changes the pool from the next step on; the pattern keeps its place. How to use it? Classic arpeggio: MIDI port Notes → Arpeggiator Notes ; Notes out → Voice Cell. Start the transport and hold a chord. Hands-free: Latch on, play a chord, take your hands off. Chord Quantizer as the source: its Notes output into the Arpeggiator for an arpeggio that follows a chord progression. Rhythmic gates: Gate Length around 25 % with Rate 1/16 for staccato; 100 % for a legato line. Mono synth voice: Pitch → Oscillator, Gate → ADSR. Wider range: Octaves 3 or 4 with Up-Down . Generative lines: Random plus a clock from a Pulse Generator or a Rotating Divider. Presets The preset bar of the Arpeggiator view has 15 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Classic Up Held notes climb in sixteenths: the standard arpeggio. Down Run Falls from the top note down across two octaves. Up-Down Two Octaves Climbs and falls over two octaves without repeating the end notes. Up and Down Repeat Climbs and falls, repeating the top and bottom notes. Played Order Plays notes in the order you pressed them. Staccato Pluck Very short gates for plucked, bouncy arpeggios. Legato Flow Notes join up across three octaves: a smooth, flowing line. Swung Sixteenths Shuffled sixteenths for a groovy house-style arp. Triplet Gallop Eighth-note triplets that gallop upward. Converge Alternates from the outside in, meeting in the middle. Diverge Starts at the middle and spreads outward. Random Sparkle Random notes over four octaves: glittery and unpredictable. Latched Pad Arp Latch keeps the arp going after you let go. Fast Trance Thirty-second notes over three octaves for a fast trance run. Slow Quarter Walk A slow, spacious quarter-note walk down and up. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Arpeggiator does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Arpeggiator under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Arpeggiator: Rising Pluck A four-bar progression of held chords is broken into a plucked run that climbs through two octaves and starts over. Try Pattern, Octaves and Rate on the Arpeggiator to turn the same chords into a different tune. Arpeggiator: Triplet Up-Down The Arpeggiator climbs and falls over three octaves in triplet eighths with a touch of Swing, giving a rolling, harp-like figure behind a slow chord change. Change Rate to 1/8 or 1/16 for straight timing. Arpeggiator: Random Sparks The pattern is Random over four octaves at sixteenth notes, so the chord tones scatter into a glittery, never-quite-repeating line over a beat. The Seed picks the shuffle: change it for a different sequence. Arpeggiator: Converging Bass A low saw bass takes the outside notes first and works inwards, the Converge pattern over two octaves, with a bit of Swing under a driving beat. Try Diverge for the reverse, or Down for a falling line. Arpeggiator: Slow Bell Wash A downward arpeggio at quarter-note speed with a short Gate Length turns each chord into a few soft bell strikes that fade into a long reverb. Increase Rate to eighth notes for a busier shimmer, or Latch to keep a chord ringing. Reference Knobs and settings Control Range Default Gate Length 1 … 100 % 50 % Swing 50 … 75 % 50 % Rate 1/1 … 1/32T 1/16 Pattern Up, Down, Up-Down, Down-Up, Up & Down, Played, Random, Converge, Diverge Up Octaves 1 … 4 1 Latch Off, On Off Seed 0 … 999 1 Sync To Auto, Clock, Transport Auto Sync To: what steps the module. Auto : the clock pulses while Clock is patched, otherwise the transport. Clock : only the pulses step it. Transport : the song position steps it, and a patched Clock is ignored. Seed: only used by Random . Inputs Input Signal What it does Notes notes The keys to arpeggiate Clock trigger One step per pulse; unpatched, the transport sets the steps Reset trigger Ends the note; the next step is step 0 Outputs Output Signal What it does Notes notes The arpeggio, one note at a time Pitch pitch The playing note, 1 V/oct (0 = C4); holds Gate gate High while a note sounds Velocity control The note's velocity, 0 … 1; holds Trigger trigger A pulse at each new note

title: Cartesian Seq
text: Cartesian Seq Cartesian Seq in the module view Introduction The Cartesian Seq is a sequencer on a grid : up to 8 × 8 cells, each with a gate (off, on or tied), a pitch , a velocity , a mod value and an access switch that takes it out of the path. Two playheads walk the grid, one across the columns ( X ) and one down the rows ( Y ), each with its own rate or clock and direction. The same handful of cells plays very different melodies depending on how the playheads move. In Cartesian mode the playheads stop walking and the X and Y knobs pick the cell instead: patch an LFO, an XY gesture or another sequencer onto them and the grid becomes a map you travel through. Patch Notes into a Voice Cell and press play: a new module plays a rising figure on the 4 × 4 corner of the grid right away. How does it work? The grid. The module always keeps all 64 cells. Columns and Rows set the playing area; cells outside it keep what you drew. Clocks mode (the default). The X playhead follows the transport at X Rate (or one column per pulse on X Clock ). What Y does depends on Y Rate : Wrap: Y moves one row each time X has crossed its row. That's a raster scan: row by row through the grid, like reading a page. A note value: Y moves on its own grid, independent of X. With 4 columns at 1/16 and Y at 1/4., X repeats every quarter note but Y every dotted quarter, so the 16 cells play a line that only repeats after 3 bars. Off: Y stays on the row chosen by the Y knob. With a cable in Y Clock , each pulse moves Y one row, whatever Y Rate says. When both playheads move on the same sample the cell plays once. Each axis has a Direction : forward, backward, back and forth ( Ping-Pong , ends not repeated) or a seeded random order that never repeats a cell twice in a row. The X and Y knobs shift the playheads: X at 50 % on a 4-column grid starts every row two columns later. Modulate them to rotate the pattern while it plays. Skipped cells. A cell with access Skip is taken out of the path; its notes stay. In a raster scan the path just gets shorter (skip 3 of 16 cells and the pattern repeats every 13 steps). With independent axes a skipped cell lends its turn to the next playing cell in the row; a row with every cell skipped stays silent. Cartesian mode. X and Y (knob plus cables) choose the column and the row directly. With Sample = Clock the position is read at every X step and that cell plays. With Change a cell plays as soon as the position moves into a new cell — no clock needed, and it keeps playing when the transport stops, which makes it a performance instrument. A little hysteresis stops a position sitting on a border from chattering. Skipped cells can't be reached; the nearest playing cell plays instead. Gates and ties. On plays for Gate Length of an X step. Tie holds the note into the next cell; a different pitch there starts before the old note ends, so a Voice Cell in Legato mode glides. Off plays nothing, but the playhead still visits the cell and Mod still moves. No note is ever left hanging: stopping, Reset, changing the size or mode, and skipping or silencing the sounding cell all end it. Pitch. A cell's pitch counts semitones above Root + Octave ; with the Transpose input it snaps to the nearest note of the Scale . Mod. Each cell carries a value from −100 % to +100 % that appears on the Mod output when the playhead arrives, gliding there over Mod Slew . Use it for a filter, a wavefold amount, a pan — a second melody for anything. How to use it? A melody right away: Notes into a Voice Cell's Notes input, press play. Drawing: pick a layer at the top. Gate : click cycles Off → On → Tie, drag paints. Pitch , Vel and Mod : drag up and down on a cell (Shift for fine steps; pitch snaps to the scale unless Shift is held); double-click resets. Access : click to skip a cell or bring it back. Alt-drag paints the first cell's value of the layer across others. Rotating: ◀ ▶ beside each row and ▲ ▼ under each column rotate that row or column by one cell. Right-click a cell to copy, paste or reset it. Randomize rewrites the shown layer inside the playing area; ▾ sets the density, pitch range, velocity range and how many cells to skip. Long phrases from short loops: set Y Rate to a dotted or triplet value against X Rate . XY performance: Mode = Cartesian, Sample = Change, and patch two slow LFOs (or a Random) onto X and Y . The crosshair shows where they go. Shuffling the order: X Direction = Random with a slow Function on Y . Chaining: Row End and Grid End make good clocks or resets for other modules; X Pos and Y Pos are handy modulation sources. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Cartesian Seq does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Cartesian Seq under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Cartesian Seq: Two-Row Riff A grid of eight columns and two rows: the X playhead runs along a row every sixteenth and Y drops to the second row when it reaches the end, so a sixteen-note riff in G Dorian comes out in order. Change Rows to 1 for a short loop, or edit a cell's pitch in the view. Cartesian Seq: Ping-Pong Marimba Both playheads bounce back and forth over a 6 × 4 patch of the grid, X on the eighths and Y once a bar, so a marimba line keeps reversing and the long path takes ages to repeat. Set the directions to Forward for a plain scan, or Random to lose the pattern. Cartesian Seq: Mod Bass Every cell also stores a Mod value, and here the Mod output opens the filter of an acid bass, so each step has its own brightness: notes with a high Mod bite, low ones stay dark. Edit the Mod of a cell or turn Mod Slew up to smear the changes. Cartesian Seq: Slow Crosshair Cartesian mode: no clocks, two slow LFOs steer the X and Y inputs across a full 8 × 8 grid of Lydian notes, and a note sounds whenever the crosshair enters a new cell. Move X and Y yourself, or change the LFO rates to wander faster. Cartesian Seq: Row End Fills X runs backward through a 5 × 3 grid, and the Row End and Grid End triggers play the drums: a hat each time a row finishes, a kick and clap when the whole grid has been walked. Change Columns or Rows and the drum accents move with the melody. Presets The preset bar of the Cartesian Seq view has 13 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Four by Four A 4 x 4 grid read left to right, row by row. Eight by Eight The full grid: sixty-four steps of melody. Single Row Just one row: a plain eight-step sequence. Slow Rows X steps fast, Y creeps slowly: rows change every half note. Backward Walk Both playheads run in reverse. Ping-Pong Grid Both playheads bounce back and forth. Random Walk Playheads jump about at random: a shuffled melody. Polymetric 5x3 Two clocks at the same rate on uneven sizes: patterns drift. Swung Grid A swung four by four. Triplet Grid Triplet steps across six columns. Manual Cartesian Pick notes with X and Y: modulate them with LFOs. Smooth Mod Walk X/Y control with a slewed mod output for a smooth line. Low Drone Grid A slow, held low-octave pattern. Reference Knobs Knob Range Default Gate Length 1 – 100 % of an X step 50 % Swing 50 – 75 % 50 % X 0 – 100 % 0 % Y 0 – 100 % 0 % Mod Slew 0 – 1 s 0 s Gate Length: how long each On cell sounds. Ties ignore it. Swing: delays every second X step. X / Y: Clocks mode: shift the playheads by whole cells. Cartesian mode: the position on the grid. Mod Slew: how long the Mod output takes to reach a new cell's value. Every knob is a modulation destination. Settings Setting Values Default Columns 1 – 8 4 Rows 1 – 8 4 Mode Clocks, Cartesian Clocks X Rate 1/1 … 1/32, dotted (.) and triplet (T) 1/16 Y Rate Wrap, Off, 1/1 … 1/32T Wrap X Direction, Y Direction Forward, Backward, Ping-Pong, Random Forward Sample Clock, Change (Cartesian mode) Clock Root C … B C Scale the Step Sequencer's scales Major Octave −3 … +3 0 Seed 0 – 999 1 Sync To Auto, Clock, Transport Auto Sync To: what steps the module. Auto : the clock pulses while X Clock / Y Clock is patched, otherwise the transport. Clock : only the pulses step it. Transport : the song position steps it, and a patched X Clock / Y Clock is ignored. Inputs Input Signal What it does X Clock trigger each pulse moves X one column; unpatched, the transport drives X Y Clock trigger each pulse moves Y one row (Clocks mode) Reset trigger both playheads start again at the first cell Transpose pitch added before quantizing (1 V/oct) Outputs Output Signal What it does Notes notes one note per played cell, ties as legato Pitch pitch the cell's quantized pitch, held between notes Gate gate high while a cell sounds, across ties Velocity control, 0 – 1 the cell's velocity, held Mod control, −1 – +1 the cell's mod value, through Mod Slew Trigger trigger a pulse when a cell starts a new note X Pos, Y Pos control, 0 – 1 the playing column and row Row End trigger a pulse when X starts a new row (raster) or wraps Grid End trigger a pulse when the whole path starts over

title: Lines
text: Lines Lines in the module view Introduction Lines is a text tracker with four tracks . You type rows of notes on the computer keyboard; each row can also carry a velocity, a gate length and one effect : retrigger, slide, probability, transpose, jump or skip. Patterns of 16–64 rows are chained by an order list . What makes it different is that every track has its own speed and length . Track 1 may run 16 rows at normal speed while track 2 runs 5 rows at 3/2 speed and track 3 runs 7 rows at half speed. They start together and slowly drift apart, then meet again; the drift panel next to the grid shows where every track is and after how many rows all four line up. Each track has its own Notes , Pitch , Gate and Velocity outputs, so four voices can play from one module. How does it work? Rows and time. One Row Rate step (default 1/16) is one master row. With nothing in Clock the rows follow the transport, so Lines stays on the bars and lands right after a loop jump; with a trigger in Clock each pulse is one row. Reset makes the next row row 0. Speed and length. Track k plays rows at its Speed (¼ … ×4 of the master rows) and wraps after its Length rows (never longer than the pattern). Because the speeds and lengths differ, the tracks drift. Tracks decides what a new pattern does: Free-run lets every track keep counting through the order list, so the drift carries on across patterns; Per pattern restarts all tracks at row 0 whenever a pattern starts. Cells. A cell has five columns: Note : a pitch, or === which ends the note. Velocity 00–7F (hex); 00 uses the Velocity setting. Gate 1–F: the note's length in eighths of a row (8 is a whole row, F almost two); 0 uses the Gate setting. Notes shorter than a row leave a gap; longer ones play into the next row. Effect letter and a two-digit hex parameter. An empty cell does nothing: the previous note keeps its own gate. Effects. Effect Parameter What it does R retrigger 02 – 10 plays the note that many times inside the row S slide 00 – FF ties into the note: the new note starts before the old one ends (a Voice Cell in legato mode glides), and Pitch glides over up to four rows P probability 00 – FF the cell plays with chance parameter / 255; otherwise nothing happens T transpose 00 – 7F up, 80 – FF down (FF = −1) shifts this note by semitones J jump row the track's next row is this row K skip count the track leaves out that many rows after this one Pitch. Cells hold MIDI notes. Octave 1…4 shifts a track by octaves and Transpose moves everything. With Quantize on, notes snap to Scale , or to a Harmony Master's key and scale when Harmony is set. Order and patterns. The order list plays its patterns one after another and starts over; Pattern fires at every change and End when the list restarts. A pattern's row count (16–64) sets how long it lasts. How to use it? Typing notes: click a cell, then play the keys: Z S X D C V G B H N J M are one octave (C … B), Q 2 W 3 E R 5 T 6 Y 7 U the next one. [ and ] change the octave. 1 types a note off. Step sets how many rows the cursor moves down after each entry. Moving: arrows, Tab (next track), Page Up/Down (16 rows), Home/End. A click selects a cell directly. Editing: Delete clears the field, Shift + Delete the whole cell. + and - transpose the note under the cursor (Shift: octaves). Enter inserts a row in the current track and moves the rest down; Shift + Enter removes it. Hex fields: type the digits; velocity takes two, the effect parameter two, the gate one. Muting: click a track's header. Drifting patterns: give tracks lengths such as 16, 12, 9 and 7 and watch the drift panel. Odd speeds like ×2/3 slow a track against the others. Patterns: Duplicate copies the pattern into the next empty one; + adds the shown pattern to the order list after the selected entry, right-click on an entry removes it. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Lines does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Lines under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Lines: Drifting Four Four lines of 16, 5, 7 and 9 rows start together and slide against each other, so the bass, a lead, an arp and a stab only meet again after 5040 rows. The drift panel in the view shows each track's place. Change a track's Length or Speed to move the meeting point. Lines: Ratchet and Slide A bass line that uses the effect column: slide cells tie notes together with a glide and retrigger cells split a row into quick repeats. A second track answers with probability cells, so it never plays quite the same bar. Edit the Fx column in the view. Lines: Odd Speeds The same twelve-row length on four tracks, but at speeds of one, two thirds, three halves and three quarters: the tracks stay in a simple ratio and phase slowly against each other, like gears. Change one Speed and the whole weave shifts. Lines: Order of Three Three patterns of 16, 16 and 32 rows run in an order list: a verse, a verse with a new bass note, and a long answer. Tracks restart with each pattern here (Tracks: Per pattern), so every section begins together; switch it to Free-run and the drift carries on. Lines: Chords from Three Tracks Tracks 1 to 3 each hold one voice of a chord at different lengths and speeds, and all three Notes outputs play one polyphonic Voice Cell: the harmony shifts as the three tracks drift. Track 4 adds a quiet high bell. Try the Quantize setting with another Scale. Presets The preset bar of the Lines view has 16 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Drifting Four Four lines of 16, 5, 7 and 9 rows slide against each other. Locked Lines All tracks the same length: a plain four-part pattern. Double and Half Bass at half speed, a line at double, one at normal. Thirds and Fifths Same length, speeds in simple ratios: a slow phase shift. Ratchet Row Retrigger effects fill rows with quick repeats. Slide Line Slide cells tie notes together with a glide. Maybe Melody Every note carries a probability, so the tune varies. Transposed Echo Track 2 plays track 1's notes shifted by an effect column. Jump Around Jump and skip effects make the row order unpredictable. Two Patterns An order of two patterns: verse and variation. Per-Pattern Restart Tracks restart with each pattern instead of drifting on. Long Thirty-Two Four slow lines of 32, 24, 20 and 28 rows: very long drift. Octave Layers One motif on three tracks, an octave apart and at two speeds. Gate Lengths The gate column from a short tick to nearly two rows. Scale-Snapped Run Plain chromatic notes pulled into the scale on playing. Row Jumper Short loops at odd speeds: fast cells over a slow base. Reference Knobs Knob Range Default Gate 5 – 100 % of a row 50 % Velocity 5 – 100 % 80 % Speed 1 … 4 x1/4, x1/3, x1/2, x2/3, x3/4, x1, x3/2, x2, x3, x4 x1 Length 1 … 4 1 – 64 rows 16 Every knob is a modulation destination; Speed and Length are stepped knobs. Settings Setting Values Default Row Rate 1/1 … 1/32, dotted and triplet 1/16 Tracks Free-run, Per pattern Free-run Octave 1 … 4 −3 … +3 0 Mute 1 … 4 off, on off Root C … B C Scale the Step Sequencer's scales Natural Minor Quantize Off, To scale Off Harmony Off, Bus A … Bus D Off Seed 0 – 999 1 Sync To Auto, Clock, Transport Auto Inputs Input Signal What it does Clock trigger each pulse is one row Reset trigger the next row is row 0; ends all notes Transpose pitch added to every note (1 V/oct) Outputs Output Signal What it does Notes 1 … 4 notes the track's notes Pitch 1 … 4 pitch the track's latest note; glides with a slide Gate 1 … 4 gate high while the track's note sounds, a short dip at a retrigger Velocity 1 … 4 control, 0 – 1 velocity of the track's latest note Pattern trigger a pulse whenever a new pattern starts End trigger a pulse when the order list starts over Row control, 0 – 1 where the master row is inside the pattern

title: Melody Mirror
text: Melody Mirror Introduction Melody Mirror listens to the last few notes of a notes stream, with their timing, and plays them back turned around : backwards, upside down, with the pitches shifted along the rhythm, or both turns at once. In Answer mode it behaves like a second player: it waits for you to pause, replies with your phrase turned around, and listens again. The notes out play a Voice Cell like any other note source. How does it work? The phrase. The module remembers the last Length notes (2–16) with when each began and how long it was held. That is the phrase. The turns ( Mode , a knob you can modulate): Reverse: the phrase played backwards in time. The last note comes first and the rhythm runs backwards too. Invert: every pitch mirrored around an axis, the rhythm unchanged. The Axis is the phrase's first note, its average pitch ( Mean ), or a Fixed note you choose. Pitches that would leave the keyboard are folded back by octaves. Rotate: the pitches move Rotate places along the phrase while the rhythm stays where it is: the same tune, shifted against its rhythm. Mirror: Reverse and Invert together. Answer: the twist. While you play it only listens. When you have been quiet for the Gap it plays the phrase turned by Reply (Reverse, Invert, Rotate or Mirror) and then listens again. While it answers, new notes are heard through Thru but not remembered, so it never answers itself. Starting. Start After Gap plays the turned phrase whenever you stop for Gap (1/2 beat … 2 bars at the transport's tempo) after new notes; it does not repeat until you play something new. Start Trigger plays only when a trigger arrives at Trig or you press Replay , as often as you like. Starting while a phrase plays begins it again. Playback shaping. Speed (0.25× … 4×) changes the tempo of the replay, Transpose moves it by semitones, Velocity scales how hard it plays and Gate Length how long each note holds. Snap To Scale pulls the replayed notes to the Root and Scale (or the key of a Harmony Master bus), so an inversion cannot leave the key. Thru passes what you play to the output as well, or mutes it so you hear only the turned version. A note that you hold while the module plays the same pitch never gets cut by the other: they share the note. How to use it? Call and response: Mode Answer, Gap 1 beat, MIDI keyboard in. Play four notes, stop, and hear the mirror image come back. Counter-melody: Mode Invert with Snap To Scale on and a slower Speed ; mix with the original through Thru . Hands-free variation: a Step Sequencer feeding it, Mode Reverse; patch an LFO into Mode to change the turn from phrase to phrase. Perform it: Start Trigger and a button on Trig , so the turned phrase comes in when you want it. Sync with others: the Playing gate and Phrase trigger tell other modules when the reply is sounding or has just started. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Melody Mirror does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Melody Mirror under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Melody Mirror: Backwards Tune A pentatonic phrase plays once every four bars; a beat after its last note the Mirror answers with the same notes played backwards, rhythm included. Change Length to turn more or fewer notes around, or Speed to play the reply slower. Melody Mirror: Upside Down The phrase is mirrored in pitch around its first note and pulled into A minor pentatonic, so the reply climbs where the original fell. Turn Axis to Mean or Fixed to move the mirror, and Transpose to lift the reply. Melody Mirror: Call And Response Answer mode: the module listens to the phrase, waits for the pause, plays the mirror image as a reply and listens again, ignoring itself while it answers. Try Reply Invert or Rotate, or a longer Gap. Melody Mirror: Turned Motif A four-note motif comes back with its pitches rotated two places along the same rhythm, so it sounds related but different. Change Rotate, or Mode to Mirror, to turn it another way. Melody Mirror: Wandering Turns A slow LFO sweeps the Mode knob, so each reply is a different turn of the phrase: reversed, inverted, rotated or mirrored. Patch your own modulation into Mode, or set Start to Trigger to play replies by hand. Presets The preset bar of the Melody Mirror view has 16 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Backwards Tune A beat after you stop, the last six notes come back in reverse. Upside Down The phrase mirrored in pitch around its first note, same rhythm. Rotated Pitches The pitches shift one place along the same rhythm. Mirror Image Backwards and upside down together. Call And Response Play a phrase; it waits for your pause, answers with the mirror image and listens again. Answer Upside Down A calm answer: your phrase inverted after two beats of silence. Answer In Reverse A quick reply that plays your last four notes backwards. Slow Retrograde The reversed phrase at half speed. Double Time Mirror The mirror image at double speed, like a tape running fast. Octave Up Reverse The reversed phrase an octave higher. Scale Snapped Inversion The inverted phrase is pulled into C major so it never leaves the key. Fixed Axis Flip Pitches mirrored around C5: low notes become high ones. Mean Axis Flip Mirrored around the average pitch of the phrase. Triggered Replay Plays only when a trigger arrives or you press Replay. Short Motif Turner A four-note motif comes back with its pitches turned two places. Soft Reply The answer is quieter and shorter than the question. Reference Knobs and settings Control Range Default Mode Reverse, Invert, Rotate, Mirror, Answer Reverse Reply Reverse, Invert, Rotate, Mirror (Answer) Mirror Length 2 … 16 notes 6 Axis First Note, Mean, Fixed First Note Axis Note 0 … 127 (Fixed) 60 Rotate −8 … +8 1 Start Trigger, After Gap After Gap Gap 1/2 beat, 1 beat, 2 beats, 1 bar, 2 bars 1 beat Speed 0.25× … 4× 1× Transpose −24 … +24 0 Velocity 0 … 100 % 100 % Gate Length 25 … 200 % 100 % Thru Pass, Mute Pass Snap To Scale Off, On Off Root, Scale, Harmony as in the Chord Quantizer C, Major, Off Mode , Length , Axis Note , Rotate , Speed , Transpose , Velocity and Gate Length have modulation inputs. Buttons: Replay plays the phrase now, Clear forgets it. Inputs and outputs Jack Signal What it does Notes (in) notes The notes to listen to Trig trigger Plays the phrase now Notes (out) notes What you play (Thru) and the turned phrase Playing gate High while a turned phrase sounds Phrase trigger A pulse when a turned phrase starts

title: Note Echo
text: Note Echo Introduction Note Echo sits in a notes cable and gives every note an echo of notes : repeats that come later, softer, and not always on the same pitch. Where an audio delay copies sound, this copies notes , so each repeat can be moved along the board's scale, fanned into a chord, left out at random, or pulled towards (or pushed away from) the beat grid. The notes out play a Voice Cell like any other note source. How does it work? When a note starts, Note Echo plans the whole train of repeats at once. The plan uses the knobs as they are at that moment, so turning a knob changes the next note, never one that is already echoing. Time. Repeats (1–16) come one Rate apart: a note value from 1/1 to 1/32T at the transport's tempo, or Free , where Time sets the gap in seconds. Length is how much of the gap each repeat sounds. Decay. Each repeat is quieter than the one before by the Decay share. Repeats that would be inaudible are not played. Scale Steps. Every repeat moves further along the scale: repeat k is k × Scale Steps scale notes above (or below) the played note. The scale is the Root and Scale setting, or the key of a Harmony Master when Harmony names a bus. In a chromatic scale a step is a semitone. A note that is not in the scale is first moved to the nearest scale note. Drop is the chance, per repeat, that it is left out. It is seeded with Seed and the note's count, so a render repeats exactly. Spread (the twist). At 0 the repeats keep to the stepped pitch. Raising it adds chord tones, built by stacking thirds in the scale: 25 % adds the third, 50 % the fifth, 75 % the seventh, 100 % the ninth. Fan decides the order the repeats walk through them: Up , Down , Up-Down or Random . The played note counts as the root, so a three-tone fan on C plays C, E, G, C, E … around it. Gravity (the twist). Positive values pull each repeat towards the nearest line of the Grid (1/4 … 1/32), at 100 % exactly onto it; negative values push it towards the point halfway between two lines. Triplet repeats pulled onto a sixteenth grid skip; straight repeats pushed off it lag behind the beat. Gravity needs a running transport (without a song position the time stays as it is). Original passes the played note too, or mutes it so only the echoes are heard. Notes of the same number never cut each other off: when a repeat meets a sounding note of the same pitch, that note ends and the repeat starts again, and the note-off of the original never ends a repeat. How to use it? Tail on a keyboard: MIDI port → Note Echo → Voice Cell. Try Rate 1/8., Repeats 5, Decay 35 %. Climbing figures: Scale Steps 1 with a short Length makes every note start a little scale run. Arpeggio from one key: Spread 50 %, Fan Up, Rate 1/16 and Original Pass. Sparse and human: Drop 30–50 % gives echoes that differ for each note. Groove: Rate 1/8T with Gravity 100 % and Grid 1/16, or Gravity −100 % for behind-the-beat repeats. Modulate Gravity from an LFO. Rhythmic trigger: the Tap output fires for every repeat that starts; use it to trigger drums or envelopes in time with the echoes. Follow the song: put Harmony on a bus and the repeats walk through whatever key the Harmony Master plays. Presets The preset bar of the Note Echo view has 16 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Dotted Eighth Tail Five fading repeats a dotted eighth apart: the classic rhythmic tail. Slapback One quiet, short repeat right behind the note. Rising Staircase Each repeat is one scale step higher: the note climbs the board's scale. Falling Cascade Each repeat one scale step lower: a tumbling run down the scale. Triad Fan Up Repeats take the chord tones above the note in turn: an arpeggio from one key. Triad Fan Down The same chord tones, falling. Seventh Ping-Pong Four chord tones bounce up and down in triplets. Random Sparkle Fast random chord tones with gaps: glitter around every note. Sparse Ghosts Half the repeats go missing, differently for every note. Pulled Tight Triplet spacing, dragged onto the sixteenth grid: a skipping, almost straight feel. Off The Grid Repeats pushed halfway between the grid lines: behind-the-beat echoes. Loose Pull Gravity at half: repeats drift towards the grid without landing on it. Free Wash Repeats in seconds, not beats, long and overlapping: a wash behind the playing. Echo Only The played note is muted: you hear only its climbing repeats. Pentatonic Rain Climbing repeats in A minor pentatonic: nothing sounds wrong. Fourths Climb Three scale steps per repeat: open, fourth-like leaps. Reference Knobs and settings Control Range Default Repeats 1 … 16 4 Rate Free, 1/1 … 1/32T 1/8 Time 10 ms … 2 s (Rate Free) 250 ms Decay 0 … 90 % 30 % Scale Steps −7 … +7 0 Drop 0 … 100 % 0 Length 5 … 98 % 50 % Spread 0 … 100 % 0 Fan Up, Down, Up-Down, Random Up Gravity −100 … +100 % 0 Grid 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, 1/32 1/16 Original Pass, Mute Pass Seed 0 … 999 1 Root, Scale any root and scale C, Major Harmony Off, Bus A … D Off Repeats , Decay , Scale Steps , Drop , Length , Spread , Gravity and Time are knobs with a modulation input. Inputs and outputs Jack Signal What it does Notes (in) notes The notes to echo; controller messages pass through Notes (out) notes The original (unless muted) and its repeats Tap trigger A pulse for every repeat that starts

title: Note Gate
text: Note Gate Introduction Note Gate is a door for a notes stream. Every note-on has to get through a row of checks, and the ones that pass can come out changed : moved to another pitch class, given a different velocity. It combines a note filter, a note remapper and a velocity shaper, with an input to open and close it and rule lanes that decide by position in the bar, by count and by how busy the line is. How does it work? A note-on goes through these stages, in this order, and stops at the first one that says no. A note-off always follows its note-on: a blocked note never produces one, and a note that did pass is ended even if the gate closed in the meantime. Gate. With a cable in Gate , notes pass while it is high ( Gate Input Pass When High ) or while it is low ( Block When High ). Unpatched, the gate is open. Range. Low Note and High Note make a window of MIDI notes, 60 being middle C. Window chooses whether notes inside pass or are blocked. Velocity limits. Floor : softer notes are dropped ( Below Floor Drop ) or raised to it ( Lift ). Ceiling : harder notes are limited to it. Rule lanes (the twist). Every lane that is switched on must agree: Step lane: sixteen steps across the bar ( Beats Per Bar long). A note passes only if the step nearest to its moment is lit in the lane. Click steps in the view. This lane needs a running transport; without a song position it does not decide. Every Nth: of the notes that got this far, only every N th passes; Nth Offset chooses which of each N . Density Limit: at most this many notes pass per Density Window (1 beat … 2 bars). 0 switches it off. The more you play, the more is held back. Remap. With Remap on, each of the twelve pitch classes is sent to another pitch class (in the same octave) or blocked, as set in the view's table. Velocity curve. The velocity is reshaped by Bend (soft notes louder when positive, quieter when negative) or, with Curve on Drawn , by the curve you draw in the view. A velocity never becomes 0, which would be a note-off. The Passed and Blocked outputs give a short trigger for every note that passed or was stopped. How to use it? Split a keyboard: two Note Gates on one MIDI port, one for Low Note 0–59, one for 60–127, into different Voice Cells. Keep it in key: Remap with the sharps sent to the natural below (the preset Naturals Only ) or to blocked . Evening out touch: Bend positive, or draw a curve that is flat at the top. Rhythmic mute: Step lane with the four beats lit lets only downbeat notes through; a Clock Divider into Gate does the same from outside. Taming a busy line: Density Limit 3 per beat on a fast arpeggio. Probability by hand: a Coin Toss into Gate decides note by note. Chains: put it before a Note Echo to echo only the strong notes, or after an Arpeggiator to thin it out. Presets The preset bar of the Note Gate view has 17 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Low Register Only notes below middle C get through. Upper Register Only notes from middle C up. Notch Out The Middle A hole in the middle of the keyboard: lows and highs pass. Soft Notes Out Notes played softer than 30 % are dropped: ghost notes disappear. Lift The Floor Soft notes are raised to 45 % instead of dropped. Ceiling Squash Nothing plays harder than 60 %. Compress Curve Soft notes come out louder: an even, compressed touch. Expand Curve Soft notes get softer, hard notes stay: more dynamics. Hard Hits Only A drawn curve that mutes everything below the middle and jumps to full above it. Naturals Only Sharps and flats fall down to the natural below: a C-major-ish keyboard. Major To Minor E, A and B drop a semitone: the same tune in a minor mood. Mute Black Keys Every black key is blocked: only the white keys play. Fifths Swap Every note moves up a fifth within its octave. Downbeats Only Notes pass only on the four beats of the bar. Offbeat Eighths Notes pass only on the 'and' of each beat. Every Other Note Passes the 1st, 3rd, 5th note and so on: halves a busy line. Thin Out Busy Runs At most three notes per beat get through, however fast you play. Reference Knobs and settings Control Range Default Low Note, High Note 0 … 127 0, 127 Window Pass Inside, Block Inside Pass Inside Floor, Ceiling 0 … 100 % 0, 100 % Below Floor Drop, Lift Drop Curve Knob, Drawn Knob Bend −100 … +100 % 0 Remap Off, On Off Gate Input Pass When High, Block When High Pass When High Step Lane Off, On Off Beats Per Bar 1 … 8 4 Every Nth, Nth Offset 1 … 8, 0 … 7 1, 0 Density Limit 0 (off) … 16 0 Density Window 1 beat, 2 beats, 1 bar, 2 bars 1 beat Low Note , High Note , Floor , Ceiling and Bend have modulation inputs. The remap table, the drawn curve and the step lane are saved with the node. Inputs and outputs Jack Signal What it does Notes (in) notes The notes to filter; controller messages pass through Gate gate Opens or closes the door Notes (out) notes The notes that passed, remapped and reshaped Passed trigger A pulse for every note that passed Blocked trigger A pulse for every note that was stopped

title: Note Looper
text: Note Looper Introduction Note Looper records the notes you play, not the sound, and loops them for one to sixteen bars. Because it keeps notes, you can change a loop after the fact: quantize it, thin it with probability, play it at half or double speed, overdub more notes and take the last layer away again. The loop is shown as a small piano roll and is saved with the board. The notes out play a Voice Cell like any other note source. How does it work? The loop is Bars × Beats Per Bar quarter notes long. The playhead is locked to the song position while the transport plays, so the loop always stays on the beat, also after a jump; with the transport stopped it runs freely at the tempo. Speed Half or Double makes the head cross the loop at half or twice the rate. Notes are stored with their position in the loop and their length, so the loop plays the same at any tempo. Mode: Play: the loop plays; what you play is heard but not recorded. Record: the old loop is thrown away and what you play is recorded. Overdub: what you play is added to the loop. Each time you enter Record or Overdub from Play it begins a new layer ; Undo removes the newest layer. A cable into Rec is a punch-in: high means Overdub, low means Play, and the Mode setting is ignored while it is patched. Clear empties the loop. A note you hold longer than the loop is cut to the loop's length. A note that crosses the loop's end sounds on at the start. Shortening Bars hides the notes beyond the end without deleting them; lengthening it brings them back. Quantize moves note starts towards a grid (1/4 … 1/16T) by Strength : 100 % puts them on the grid, 50 % halfway. It acts on playback, not on what is stored, so you can turn it off again. Probability is decided for each note on each pass (seeded by Seed , so a render repeats): at 60 % about six in ten notes play and the loop never sounds quite the same twice. Thru passes what you play to the output, or mutes it until the loop comes round (what you play is still recorded). How to use it? Loop a figure: Mode Record, play two bars, switch Mode to Play. Build up layers: Overdub , play a bass line, then a melody. Undo the melody if it was not right. Tidy a loose take: Quantize 1/16 at 100 %, or 50 % to keep some feel. Make it breathe: Probability 60–80 % for ghost notes, or a Coin Toss into the Probability knob. Feed the loop elsewhere: Notes → Note Echo or Melody Mirror, so the loop is echoed, reversed or answered. Perform with a pedal: a button into Rec for punch-in overdubbing. Sync outside modules: Pass triggers at every loop start, Phase is a ramp over the loop, Recording is high while it records. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Note Looper does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Note Looper under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Note Looper: Recorded Groove A two-bar bass line, recorded earlier, loops over a beat. Set Mode to Overdub and play along to add notes on top, press Undo to take the last layer off again, or Clear to start over. Note Looper: Ghost Notes A one-bar sixteenth-note figure is played with 55 % Probability, so every pass keeps a different set of its notes. Change Seed for another sequence of passes, or raise Probability to 100 % for the full figure. Note Looper: Half Speed Drift A two-bar tune loops at half speed, so it takes four bars to come round and every note is twice as long. Set Speed to Double or Normal to hear the same notes at other speeds. Note Looper: Tidied Take A loosely played one-bar riff, quantized to sixteenths by a Strength that a slow LFO sweeps from none to full: you hear the take tighten and loosen again. Turn Strength up for a fixed amount, or try Quantize 1/8T. Note Looper: Loop Into Echo A sparse two-bar loop feeds a Note Echo that climbs the scale and fans into chord tones, so a handful of recorded notes becomes a shimmering figure. Mute the Echo's Original or change its Rate to reshape it. Presets The preset bar of the Note Looper view has 15 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Two Bar Loop A two-bar loop in play: set Mode to Record and play it in. One Bar Pulse A one-bar loop for short, repeating figures. Four Bar Phrase Four bars: room for a melody that goes somewhere. Eight Bar Story Eight bars for a whole verse of notes. Overdub Layers Records on top of what is already looping; Undo takes the last layer off. Fresh Take Throws the old loop away and records a new one. Half Speed Drift The loop plays at half speed: the same notes, twice as long. Double Speed Flurry The loop at double speed. Tight Sixteenths Notes snap fully to the sixteenth grid. Loose Eighths Notes move halfway to the eighth grid: tidied, but still human. Triplet Snap Everything snaps to triplets. Ghost Notes Each pass plays about 60 % of the notes, differently every time. Sparse Memory A handful of notes per pass: the loop hints at the tune. Silent Thru What you play is recorded but not heard until the loop comes round. Waltz Loop Bars of three beats. Reference Knobs and settings Control Range Default Mode Play, Record, Overdub Play Bars 1 … 16 2 Beats Per Bar 1 … 8 4 Speed Half, Normal, Double Normal Probability 0 … 100 % 100 % Quantize Off, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, 1/32, 1/8T, 1/16T Off Strength 0 … 100 % 100 % Thru Pass, Mute Pass Seed 0 … 999 1 Bars , Probability and Strength have modulation inputs. Buttons: Clear , Undo . At most 256 notes fit in a loop. Inputs and outputs Jack Signal What it does Notes (in) notes The notes to record Rec gate High: Overdub, low: Play (while patched) Notes (out) notes What you play (Thru) and the loop Pass trigger A pulse at the start of every pass Recording gate High while Record or Overdub is active Phase control 0 … 1 across the loop

title: Polymeter Seq
text: Polymeter Seq Polymeter Seq in the module view Introduction The Polymeter Seq takes what a step usually holds — does it play, which note, which octave, how long, how likely, how many repeats — and gives each its own track : Trigger , Note , Octave , Gate , Probability and Ratchet . Every track has its own length , loop window , clock division and direction , so they drift against each other. A 16-step rhythm over a 7-step melody and a 5-step octave pattern takes 560 steps to repeat — and it still lands on the song's grid and renders the same every time. Patch Notes into a Voice Cell and press play: a new module plays exactly that drifting line. How does it work? Base ticks. With nothing in Clock , ticks follow the transport at Rate ; with a trigger in Clock , each trigger is one tick. Each track runs at its division of the tick: ×2, ×3, ×4 step two to four times per tick, /2 … /16 every 2 to 16 ticks. Its position is worked out from the tick count, so after a loop jump, or starting in the middle of the song, every track is exactly where it would have been. Loops and directions. A track plays the steps between its loop start and end: forward, backward, back and forth (ends not repeated) or at random (seeded). Hits. A note happens when the Trigger track steps onto an On or Accent step and the Probability step wins the dice (plus Prob. Bias ). The other tracks are read at that moment: Note holds a scale degree (0 = the root, 1 = the next note of the scale, −1 the one below …), so changing Scale keeps the melody's shape and every note stays in key. Octave shifts by −3 … +3 octaves. Gate is the share of the hit the note lasts (times Gate Scale ), or Tie : the note holds into the next hit. Above 100 % notes overlap, and a Voice Cell in Legato mode glides. Ratchet splits the hit into 1–8 quick repeats, evenly spaced, accelerating or decelerating; each repeat is 8 % softer. Accent steps play 20 % louder than Velocity . Spread adds seeded human feel: a little velocity variation and a slight delay. A track's skipped values are simply never heard: a Note track at ×2 under a Trigger track at 1 plays every other note. That's part of the fun. Mute makes a track give its neutral value (Trigger: always on; Note, Octave: 0; Gate: 50 %; Probability: 100 %; Ratchet: 1). Bar and Track Ends. Bar fires when every unmuted track is back at its loop start on the same tick — the full cycle, shown at the top of the view. Track Ends fires whenever any track wraps. Pattern slots. Up to 8 slots, each a complete set of six tracks. Choose one with the slot buttons, or patch the Pattern input (0 … 1 across Slots used ). Pattern Change decides when a new slot takes over: immediately, at the next track end, at the next full cycle or at the next bar. The tick count isn't reset, so the new slot comes in in time. Hold stops every track from advancing while it's high. No note is left hanging: stop, Reset, slot changes, edits and releasing Hold all end the sounding note. How to use it? A generative line: Notes into a Voice Cell. Change the Note track's length to 5 or 9 and hear the phrase change. Editing: each row is a track. Trigger : click cycles Off → On → Accent, drag paints. Note , Octave , Gate , Probability , Ratchet : drag up and down (Note shows the note name on hover). Shift-click a Gate step for Tie, a Ratchet step for its shape (» accelerate, « decelerate). Double-click resets a step. Drag the bracket under a row to set the loop window. Row controls: length, division, direction (→ ← ↔ ?), M mute and ⟳ randomize that track. Randomize all rewrites every track; ▾ sets the trigger density, the degree range, step-wise melodies and the ratchet chance. Slots: build variations in slots 2–8 (Copy / Paste), set Slots used and sequence them with a slow ramp into Pattern . Thinning out: a slow LFO on Prob. Bias thins the line and fills it up. Chaining: Track Ends into a Random's trigger gives a new value every time any track wraps; Bar marks the whole cycle. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Polymeter Seq does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Polymeter Seq under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Polymeter Seq: Five Against Seven The trigger track is five steps long and the note track seven, so each rhythm cycle meets a different pitch and the tune only repeats after thirty-five steps. Change the length of either track in the view to find another cycle. Polymeter Seq: Seven-Step Groove A bass line built on a seven-step trigger track plays against a half-time beat, so the groove keeps leaning forward and landing again. The Track Ends output rings a hat whenever a track wraps around; try dragging Swing or Gate Scale. Polymeter Seq: Probability Garden The probability track gives each step a chance of sounding, so a Dorian marimba tune keeps thinning out and filling in. Push Prob. Bias up for a dense, almost fixed tune or down towards silence; change Seed to grow a different garden. Polymeter Seq: Ratchet Rolls Some steps of the ratchet track split into two, three or four quick repeats, so a simple lead line stutters and rolls at odd places. Ratchet Amt scales how far the repeats go: bring it to 0 for a plain line, or leave it up for rolls. Polymeter Seq: Pattern Slots Two stored patterns, a calm one and a busy one, share a voice, and a slow ramp on the Pattern input moves from one to the other at the next bar. Click a slot in the view to play it alone, or change Pattern Change to switch immediately. Presets The preset bar of the Polymeter Seq view has 14 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Straight Sixteenths Plain sixteenth notes: the neutral setup. Tight Gates Short gates for plucks and percussion. Long Gates Gates stretch past the step so notes overlap. Swung Shuffle A loose swing across all six tracks. Slow Eighths Eighth notes: a roomier polymeter. Triplet Polymeter Triplet steps against the bar for a rolling feel. Sparse Chance Lowers every step's probability: only some notes play. Always Play Raises every probability so all steps fire. Heavy Ratchets Ratchet steps repeat at full strength: stuttering hits. No Ratchets Ratchets switched off: clean single notes. Wide Spread Spreads the tracks across pitch and velocity for a lively line. Soft Velocity Quiet notes for a gentle background pattern. Low Octave Bass Two octaves down in E minor: a bass polymeter. Blues Polymeter A blues scale with light swing. Reference Knobs Knob Range Default Gate Scale 10 – 200 % 100 % Prob. Bias −100 … +100 % 0 % Ratchet Amt 0 – 100 % 100 % Swing 50 – 75 % 50 % Velocity 0 – 100 % 80 % Spread 0 – 100 % 0 % Gate Scale: multiplies every gate; above 100 % notes overlap. Prob. Bias: added to every probability; −100 % silences, +100 % plays every trigger. Ratchet Amt: scales the Ratchet track; 0 % plays single hits. Swing: delays every second tick. Velocity: the base velocity; accents add 20 %. Spread: seeded velocity variation (±25 %) and timing delay (up to 5 % of a tick). Every knob is a modulation destination. title: Roll
text: Roll Roll in the module view Introduction Roll is a note editor you play. Notes are drawn on a pitch grid with any start, any length and any pitch, up to 8 bars long. They may overlap , so a pattern can be a chord, a bass line under a melody, or notes held through one another. Notes plays a Voice Cell with all of it at once; the Low , High and Last outputs give you the lowest, the highest and the latest note as ordinary pitch and gate signals for monosynths. Each note carries its own chance and ratchet count. Eight slots hold eight patterns. Two ideas are particular to Roll: a ghost of the slot that played before sits behind the notes you edit, and the Morph knob blends the playing slot into a second slot note by note. How does it work? Time. A beat is divided into 96 ticks, a bar is four beats. With nothing in Clock the playhead follows the transport, so the pattern stays on the bars and lands right after a loop jump. Speed runs the pattern at ¼, ½, 1, 2 or 4 times the tempo. With a trigger in Clock each pulse advances the playhead by Clock Step instead. Reset returns to the start of the loop region. Loop region. The ruler above the notes sets where the playhead loops inside the pattern's bars; the rest of the pattern stays as drawn. Double-click the ruler to loop all bars again. Overlap. Every note is its own voice with its own note-on and note-off. If the same pitch is started again while it still sounds, it is restarted, so no note can stick. Length scales every note's length (from 10 % to 200 %). Ratchet and chance. A ratchet of 4 divides the note's length into four repeats; a chance of 50 % lets the note play every second time on average. The choice is seeded ( Seed ) and depends on the loop count, so the same Seed renders the same variation every time. Humanise. At the top the notes are late by up to 30 ms and vary in velocity by up to a quarter. Notes are only delayed, never early, and the lengths stay. Pitch. Notes are drawn as MIDI pitches. Octave and Transpose move them; with Quantize set to To scale every note is snapped to the Scale (or to the key and scale of a Harmony Master when Harmony is set). The rows of the editor light up with the scale, following the Harmony Master. Slots, Ghost and Morph. Slot (or the Pattern input, 0–1 over the eight slots) chooses what plays. A change waits for Slot Change : the next bar, the end of the loop, or no wait at all. The Ghost shows the slot that played before the current one as soft blocks behind your notes, so a new pattern can answer the old one. While you edit a slot that is not playing, the ghost shows the one that is. Morph blends the playing slot with the slot Morph To . The first note of one is paired with the first of the other, the second with the second, and so on, in order of time. Paired notes move between the two in start, length, pitch and velocity. Notes without a partner fade in or out one by one as the knob moves. At 0 % you hear the playing slot exactly, at 100 % the other one. The target slot shows as dashed outlines. How to use it? Drawing: click empty grid to add a note (its length is the Snap value) and drag sideways to make it longer. Drag a note to move it, drag its right edge to resize it. Hold Alt to ignore the snap. Right-click or double-click a note, or press Delete, removes it. Shift-click selects more than one; the arrow keys nudge the selection (Shift: an octave). Lanes: the strip below the notes sets velocity , chance or ratchet of the note under the pointer (all selected notes if it is one of them). Pick the lane in the Lane menu. Zoom: the mouse wheel scrolls the pitch, Shift + wheel scrolls in time and Ctrl/⌘ + wheel zooms. Fit shows all bars. Slots: click a slot number to edit and play it; Shift-click edits without switching what plays. A bar under a number marks the slot that plays (bright) and the one that played before (dim). Copy → copies the slot to the next one, Double repeats a pattern into twice the bars. Dice writes a random line in the scale into the loop region of the slot. A bass and a lead from one pattern: patch Low Pitch / Low Gate to a bass voice and High Pitch / High Gate to a lead. Evolving: put a slow LFO on Morph and the pattern slides between two slots; or an LFO on Slot for a pattern per bar. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Roll does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Roll under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Roll: Chord Stack Four overlapping chords drawn on a four-bar roll play a Voice Cell as a pad, while the Low Pitch and Low Gate outputs pick out the lowest note of each chord for a bass. Open the roll and drag a note to change a chord. Roll: Morph Drift Slot 1 is a steady eighth-note arp, slot 2 an offbeat line with a few extra notes. A slow LFO turns Morph so the arp bends note by note into the other pattern and back; the spare notes fade in and out. Set Morph by hand to freeze a blend. Roll: Ratchet and Chance Every note of this two-bar line has its own ratchet count and chance, so some notes split into quick repeats and others play only now and then. Seed changes which ones sound; Humanise adds a loose feel. Roll: Low and High One pattern with a bass line, a lead above it and a long held note between: the Low outputs play a bass voice and the High outputs a lead, while Notes plays a soft pad with all of it. Move a note across and it changes hands. Roll: Slow Eight Bars Long overlapping notes make an eight-bar drone chord progression, and a few quiet notes with ratchets and a chance of sounding sparkle on top. Everything starts a little apart thanks to Humanise. Draw a note to add your own. Presets The preset bar of the Roll view has 16 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Rising Line A short rising line, the starting point. Minor Chords Four overlapping five-note chords, a bar each. Walking Bass Eight-note bass line over two bars. Held Pad Stack Long notes starting a little apart and ringing through each other. Ratchet Pulse Notes that split into 2-6 quick repeats. Chance Garden Sixteen notes that each play only some of the time. Humanised Keys Chords that arrive a hair late and uneven. Triplet Roll A rolling run on the triplet grid. Morph Pair Two arps; Morph 50 % sits halfway between them. Eight Bars A long melody that takes eight bars to come round. Swung Arp A sixteenth-note arpeggio with a rolling swing. Half-Time Drift Everything at half speed: a slow, stretched pattern. Double-Time Run The pattern at twice the speed, snapped to the scale. Loop Window Four bars drawn, only the second one loops. Scale Snap Cluster A chromatic cluster pulled into Dorian when played. Ghost Answer Slot 1 calls, slot 2 answers; the ghost shows the call. Reference Knobs Knob Range Default Morph 0 – 100 % 0 % Humanise 0 – 100 % 0 % Length 10 – 200 % 100 % Swing 50 – 75 % 50 % Slot 1 – 8 1 Morph To 1 – 8 2 Swing: delays notes that start on an odd sixteenth. Slot and Morph To are stepped knobs: a cable moves them through the eight slots. Every knob is a modulation destination. Clock only moves with pulses; Transport ignores a patched Clock . Inputs Input Signal What it does Clock trigger each pulse moves the playhead by Clock Step Reset trigger back to the start of the loop region; ends all notes Transpose pitch added to every note (1 V/oct) Pattern control, 0 – 1 chooses the slot over the eight slots Outputs Output Signal What it does Notes notes every note, polyphonic Low Pitch / Low Gate pitch / gate the lowest sounding note; the gate dips for a moment when another note becomes the lowest High Pitch / High Gate pitch / gate the highest sounding note Last Pitch / Last Gate pitch / gate the most recently started note that still sounds Velocity control, 0 – 1 velocity of the latest note Trigger trigger a pulse whenever any note starts Loop trigger a pulse when the loop starts over Position control, 0 – 1 where the playhead is inside the loop region Pitch outputs hold their last value when no note sounds.

title: Stage Seq
text: Stage Seq Stage Seq in the module view Introduction The Stage Seq plays stages instead of steps. Each of up to 16 stages has a pitch and a length in pulses (1–8), and a gate mode that decides what those pulses sound like: one long note, a note on every pulse, only the first pulse, silence, or fast ratchets . Slides glide into a stage, accents make it louder. Because every stage has its own length, a few stages make long, uneven phrases: the factory pattern is 8 stages and 12 pulses, so it shifts against the bar every time round. It's a natural bass-line and lead sequencer. Patch Notes into a Voice Cell and press play. How does it work? Pulses. With nothing in Clock , pulses follow the transport at Rate ; with a trigger in Clock , each trigger is one pulse. A stage of 3 pulses lasts three pulses, then the next stage starts. Order. Mode chooses how the stages follow each other: Forward 1 … S, Reverse S … 1, Pendulum 1 … S … 2 (the end stages once per turn). Random jumps to a random stage, never the same one twice in a row. Brownian walks: one stage on (50 %), one back (25 %) or stays (25 %), wrapping around at the ends. The fixed orders are worked out from the song position, so a loop jump lands on the right stage and pulse. Random and Brownian start a new walk at every Phrase (1–16 bars): the walk depends only on Seed and the phrase, so it plays the same in every render, and after a jump the module replays the walk from the phrase start and lands where it should. A stage that would cross the end of a phrase is cut short there. Gate modes. Mode Gate Notes Rest low none; Pitch and Velocity hold First Gate Length of the first pulse one Every Gate Length of each pulse one per pulse Hold the whole stage one long note Ratchet each pulse split into 2–4 fast gates pulses × ratchets Slide. A stage with slide is entered legato : the previous note keeps sounding into it (its gate is stretched to the stage boundary), the new note-on comes before the old note-off, and Pitch glides there over Slide Time . A Voice Cell in Legato mode glides with it. A slide into a Rest stage does nothing. Accent. An accented stage plays louder — by how much is set with the Accent knob — and holds the Accent gate high while its notes sound. Hold. While the Hold input is high, a stage that ends starts again. With a clock, the order carries on where it stopped when Hold falls. With the transport, the module rejoins the song position at the next pulse, so it's never out of time. No hanging notes. Stopping, Reset, changing Stages , Mode or Phrase , and changing the sounding stage's gate mode or pulses all end the note. How to use it? A bass line: Notes into a Voice Cell with a low Octave . Use Hold stages for long notes and a slide or two for the squelch. Editing: the timeline shows each stage as wide as its pulses. Drag in the Pitch lane (it snaps to the scale; Shift for semitones; double-click resets). Drag sideways in Pulses to set the length, or scroll on the dots. Click Gate to cycle Rest → First → Every → Hold → Ratchet; scroll (or Shift-click) a Ratchet stage to set 2–4. Click Slide and Accent to toggle them; drag Vel . Randomize rewrites the lanes you tick in ▾ (pitch, pulses, gate, slide, accent, velocity), with the pitch range, the longest stage and the slide and accent chances. ◀ ▶ rotate the stages; Clear starts over. Generative lines: Mode = Brownian, Phrase = 4 bars. Change Seed until you like the walk; it stays the same every time you play. Breaks: patch a gate from another sequencer into Hold to stutter the current stage. Chaining: Stage Start fires on every stage, End when the cycle (or phrase) starts over. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Stage Seq does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Stage Seq under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Stage Seq: Held Pulses Each stage holds its note for a different number of pulses, from one to six, so a slow pad-like line in Eb Lydian lingers on some notes and moves quickly past others. Change a stage's Pulses in the view to stretch or squeeze the phrase. Stage Seq: Gate Modes Eight stages that each use a different gate mode: a single First hit, notes that repeat on Every pulse, a long Hold, a Ratchet burst and a Rest, so one riff shows all the ways a stage can fire. Click a stage's gate mode in the view to change it. Stage Seq: Slide Bass Stages marked Slide glide into the next pitch over the Slide Time, and the accented stages fire an extra gate that snaps the filter open, giving a squelchy bass over a four-on-the-floor beat. Raise Slide Time for slower glides or Accent for a harder bite. Stage Seq: Pendulum Bells Twelve stages are played in Pendulum mode: forward to the last stage and back again, with the Phrase length marking the repeat. Switch Mode to Forward, Reverse, Random or Brownian to hear the same stages in other orders. Stage Seq: Brownian Walk In Brownian mode the playhead takes a random step to a neighbouring stage each time, so a Dorian melody wanders without jumping, and the Stage Start output ticks a hat on every new stage. Change Seed to take another walk, or Stages to widen the range. Presets The preset bar of the Stage Seq view has 14 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Eight Stages Eight stages played forward: the neutral setup. Sixteen Stages All sixteen stages for a long phrase. Short Four A four-stage loop: tight and repetitive. Reverse Stages play backward. Slow Pendulum Swings forward and back through the stages. Random Stages Stages in random order. Brownian Wander Each step moves one stage up or down: a drifting melody. Slidey Lead Long slide times make marked stages glide. Snappy Slide Very short slides: a quick portamento snap. Hard Accents Accented stages hit at full strength. Soft Accents Accents barely stand out: an even, gentle line. Swung Stages A shuffle across the stages. Triplet Phrase Triplets over a two-bar phrase. Long Phrase Bass A long eight-bar phrase an octave pair down. Reference Knobs Knob Range Default Gate Length 1 – 100 % of a pulse 50 % Slide Time 1 ms – 2 s 80 ms Accent 0 – 100 % 50 % Swing 50 – 75 % 50 % Gate Length: the gate of First , Every and Ratchet notes (for ratchets, of each fast gate). Slide Time: how long Pitch takes to reach a slide stage (99 %). Accent: how much accented stages are boosted, from not at all to full velocity. Swing: delays every second pulse. Every knob is a modulation destination. Auto : the clock pulses while Clock is patched, otherwise the transport. Clock : only the pulses step it. Transport : the song position steps it, and a patched Clock is ignored. title: Step Sequencer
text: Step Sequencer Step Sequencer in the module view Introduction The Step Sequencer plays a melody of up to 32 steps . Each step has a gate (off, on or tied to the next step) with its own length , a pitch , a velocity and a ratchet (1–16 notes inside the step), drawn in four lanes. Pitches snap to a scale , so every pattern stays in key. Randomize buttons write new gates, pitches, velocities or ratchets in one click, and the Variation knob adds seeded variation while the pattern plays, without changing it. Patch Notes into a Voice Cell and you have a polyphonic synth playing a sequence. The Pitch , Gate and Velocity outputs drive everything else. How does it work? Timing. With nothing in Clock , the sequencer follows the transport: the step is worked out from the song position at the chosen Rate , so it's always in time with the bars and lands on the right step after a loop jump. When the transport stops, the note ends. Patch a trigger into Clock and each pulse moves one step instead. Reset makes the next step step 1. Steps. Length sets how many steps play (1–32). Steps beyond it keep what you drew, so shortening a pattern loses nothing. Direction plays the steps forward, backward, back and forth ( Ping-Pong ) or in a seeded random order that never repeats a step twice in a row. Gates and ties. On plays a note for Gate Length of the step, scaled by the step's own length bar. Tie holds the note into the next step. If the next step has another pitch, the new note starts before the old one ends, so a Voice Cell in Legato mode glides instead of retriggering. With the same pitch, the note just continues. Off plays nothing; Pitch and Velocity keep their last values. Pitch. A step's pitch counts semitones above Root + Octave . The result (plus the Transpose input) snaps to the nearest note of the Scale ; halfway between two notes it goes down. Transpose is applied before snapping, so a transposed melody stays in the scale. Variation. At each step, with the chance set by Variation , the step plays a random scale note within Var. Range of its own pitch, and a velocity up to 25 % louder or softer. Gates never change. The choices come from Seed and the step's place in the song, so the same Seed plays the same variations every time. How to use it? A sequenced synth: patch Notes into a Voice Cell's Notes input. Press play. Drawing: click the strip on top of the gate lane to cycle Off → On → Tie; drag across it to paint. Click or drag in the bars below it to set each step's gate length (height = share of Gate Length ; an Off step turns On). In the ratchet lane, the height is the number of notes (1–16) the step is divided into; each one is retriggered with the same pitch and velocity, and a tie does not carry over. Double-click a bar to reset it. Drag in the pitch lane to draw a melody; it snaps to the scale (hold Shift for single semitones outside it). Double-click a pitch to reset it to the root. Drag in the velocity lane to draw accents. New ideas: each lane has its own dice button (⚄) next to its name: new gates and ties, new pitches from the scale, or new velocities, leaving the other lanes alone. Randomize all rewrites all three. The ▾ button sets how many steps get a gate ( Density ). Next to each dice, a range slider sets the values the dice may pick (gate length, pitch in semitones from the root, velocity, ratchet count): narrow it to reduce the spread, or drag both handles together to set every step to one value. Each click is one undo step. Moving patterns: ◀ and ▶ rotate the steps; Clear turns all gates off. Evolving lines: patch a slow Function or Random onto Variation . The melody wanders off and comes back. Key changes: patch another sequencer's Pitch , or a MIDI Device's Pitch , into Transpose . Without Voice Cells: Gate into an ADSR, Pitch into an Oscillator. Chaining: End fires when the pattern starts over; use it to reset or advance other modules. Presets The preset bar of the Step Sequencer view has 15 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Straight Sixteenths Plain forward sixteenth notes in C major: the neutral starting point. Tight Staccato Short, clipped gates in minor pentatonic for plucks and bass. Legato Eighths Full-length gates in eighths so the notes run together. Swung Shuffle Sixteenths with a loose swing in Dorian for a laid-back groove. Triplet Roll Eighth-note triplets for a rolling, rounded feel. Slow Pendulum Eight steps bouncing back and forth in Lydian: dreamy and floating. Backward Run Plays the pattern in reverse for a falling line. Short Loop Eight A tight eight-step loop in Phrygian for driving basslines. Odd Five Five steps against a four-beat bar: the pattern keeps shifting. Dense Random Thirty-second notes in random order across the whole scale. Gentle Drift Notes wander a few semitones from the written pitches. Wild Variation Heavy variation of up to an octave: the sequence never plays the same twice. Blues Walk Dotted eighths in an A blues scale with a little swing. Eastern Lines Sixteenth triplets in a Phrygian dominant scale. Low Octave Drone Slow, held quarter notes two octaves down for a sub line. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Step Sequencer does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Step Sequencer under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Step Sequencer: Pentatonic Pluck Sixteen steps of C major pentatonic, with rests and a few quieter steps, played as short plucks: every note you edit snaps to the scale. Try Scale, Root or Length to reshape the tune, or Gate Length to go from staccato to legato. Step Sequencer: Acid Ties A bass line with tied steps, which hold the previous pitch into the next step so the notes run together, and a little Swing for a rolling feel, over a four-on-the-floor beat. Try more Swing, or shorten Gate Length to hear the ties disappear. Step Sequencer: Ping-Pong Bells Twelve steps of D Dorian run forward and then backward, in triplet eighths, so the bell line rises and falls without repeating the end notes. Switch Direction to Forward, Backward or Random, or change Length to move the turning points. Step Sequencer: Shaken Tune Variation is set to about half, so around every other step may jump up to a fifth away from its programmed note, and a slow LFO swells and fades that chance. Change Var. Range for bigger leaps, or Seed to deal a different set of surprises. Step Sequencer: Chord Walker A second, slow Step Sequencer walks a four-bar progression and its Pitch goes into the first one's Transpose input, so the same eight-step figure is carried to a new root each bar. The slow one also plays the sub bass. Edit either sequence to change the harmony or the figure. Reference Knobs Knob Range Default Gate Length 1 – 100 % of a step 50 % Swing 50 – 75 % 50 % Variation 0 – 100 % 0 % Var. Range 0 – 24 semitones 12 Gate Length: how long each On step sounds. Ties ignore it. Swing: delays every second step; 50 % is straight, 75 % a heavy shuffle. Variation: the chance per step of playing a varied note. Var. Range: how far a varied note may move from the step's own pitch. Every knob is a modulation destination.
