Auto : the clock pulses while Clock is patched, otherwise the transport. Clock : only the pulses step it. Transport : the song position steps it, and a patched Clock is ignored. Inputs Input Signal What it does Clock trigger each pulse plays the next step; unpatched, the transport drives the steps Reset trigger the next step is step 1 Transpose pitch added before quantizing (1 V/oct: 1/12 per semitone) Outputs Output Signal What it does Notes notes one note per step, ties as legato Pitch pitch the step's quantized pitch, held between steps Gate gate high while a step sounds, across ties Velocity control, 0 – 1 the step's velocity, held between steps Trigger trigger a pulse when a step starts a new note End trigger a pulse when the pattern starts over Step control, 0 – 1 where the playhead is: first step 0, last step 1

title: Drum Grid
text: Drum Grid Drum Grid in the module view Introduction The Drum Grid is a drum machine's step sequencer: 8 tracks by up to 32 steps , and each step is off, on or accented . Every track has its own Gate , Accent and Velocity outputs, so each row plays one drum module. The module holds 16 pattern slots that you can switch while it plays, and single patterns can be saved to a pattern library shared by all your sets. A set of factory patterns gets you started. How does it work? Timing. The grid plays steps of Rate . Time comes from one of three places: Transport (the default): the step is worked out from the song position, so the grid stays in time with the bars and after loop jumps. It stops with the transport. Tempo: set Source to Tempo and the grid runs from its own Tempo knob, transport or not. Tempo is a knob, so you can modulate it. Clock: patch a clock into Clock and it takes over. Clock PPQN says how many pulses make a quarter note (24 and 48 are common), or 1 per step for one pulse per step whatever the Rate. If the pulses don't divide the Rate evenly, the view shows ⚠ PPQN and steps are rounded to whole pulses. Run and Reset. A gate into Run starts and stops the grid: a rising edge starts again at step 1, low stops it. Without a cable the grid just runs. Reset jumps to step 1 without stopping. Steps. On steps open the track's gate for Gate Length . Accent steps do too and also open the track's Accent gate. Velocity is 100 % on an accented step and the Velocity knob on a normal one, and holds until the track plays again, so a drum's Velocity input reads the right value at the hit. Two steps in a row always make two separate hits, even at 100 % Gate Length. Patterns. Each slot has its own pattern and Length . Choosing another slot switches at the end of the current pattern ( Switch: At End ) or at the next step ( Immediate ). A cable into Pattern chooses the slot instead (0 … 1 covers slots 1 … 16). An empty slot plays silence: a break. How to use it? A drum kit: patch Gate 1 into a kick's Trig and Velocity 1 into its Velocity ; the same for the other tracks. Press play. Drawing: click a step to cycle off → on → accent; Shift-click toggles accent directly. Drag across steps to paint. Drag the marker on the ruler, or type in Length , to set the pattern's length. Tracks: click a name to rename it. M mutes, S solos. Hover a row for ‹ › to rotate just that row; ◀ ▶ rotate them all. Slots: click a number to play it (it blinks until it starts) and edit it. Alt-click edits a slot without playing it. Copy and Paste move a pattern between slots; Clear empties one. Presets: Presets ▾ loads a factory or saved pattern into the slot you're editing. Save Pattern… stores the slot in your library. Loading a pattern only renames tracks that still have their default names. Accents elsewhere: Accent n or the shared Accent output can open a filter, push a VCA or switch a drum's tone on the accented hits. Chaining: Step Clock clocks other sequencers in step with the grid; End fires when a pattern starts over. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Drum Grid does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Drum Grid under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Drum Grid: Four on the Floor A house groove from five of the eight tracks: kick on every beat, clap on two and four, hats on the off-beats. Capital X steps are accents and play louder than x steps; click a step in the grid to cycle off, on and accent. Drum Grid: Pattern Chain An LFO sweeping once every four bars feeds the Pattern input, so the grid plays a groove twice, then a busier variation, then a fill with toms, and starts over. Set Switch to Immediate to hear it change mid-bar, or take the cable out and pick slots by hand. Drum Grid: Twelve-Step Waltz The pattern is only 12 steps long, so the grid wraps after three beats and the groove counts in three, with Swing leaning on the off-steps. Each pattern keeps its own Length: stretch it to 16 in the grid view and the waltz turns into a march. Drum Grid: Accent Pump The grid's Accent output, high only when an X step plays, fires an envelope that opens a filter on a low drone, so every accented hit pumps the pad while the quiet x steps leave it closed. Change the grid's Velocity knob to scale the soft hits. Drum Grid: Eight-Track Rolling Percussion All eight tracks work across two bars of 12/8 (Rate 1/8T, 24 steps): a kick, two toms, a clave, a cowbell, a clap, shaker hats and a distant cymbal. Mute a track in the grid view to hear how the parts interlock. Reference Knobs Knob Range Default Tempo 20 – 300 BPM 120 Gate Length 1 – 100 % of a step 25 % Swing 50 – 75 % 50 % Velocity 0 – 100 % 70 % Tempo: the speed when Source is Tempo . Gate Length: how long each hit's gate stays high. Swing: delays every second step; 50 % is straight, 75 % a heavy shuffle. Velocity: the velocity of normal steps; accented steps are always 100 %. Every knob is a modulation destination. Settings Setting Values Default Source Transport, Tempo Transport Rate 1/4 … 1/32, dotted (.) and triplet (T) 1/16 Clock PPQN 1 per step, 2, 4, 24, 48 1 per step Switch At End, Immediate At End Sync To Auto, Clock, Transport Auto Sync To: what steps the module. Auto : the clock pulses while Clock is patched, otherwise the transport. Clock : only the pulses step it. Transport : the song position steps it, and a patched Clock is ignored. With Transport , the Source setting still picks the song position or the internal tempo. Inputs Input Signal What it does Clock trigger external clock; overrides Source Run gate rising: start at step 1; low: stopped; unpatched: running Reset trigger the next step is step 1 Pattern control, 0 – 1 chooses the slot, read when a switch can happen Outputs Output Signal What it does Gate 1 … 8 gate high for Gate Length on each on or accented step Accent 1 … 8 gate the same, on accented steps only Velocity 1 … 8 control, 0 – 1 the step's velocity, held between hits Accent gate high while any track plays an accent Step Clock trigger a pulse at every step End trigger a pulse when the pattern starts over or switches Running gate high while the grid plays

title: Drum Map
text: Drum Map Drum Map in the module view Introduction The Drum Map plays kick , snare and hats from a map of patterns . Move X and Y and the beat travels smoothly between rhythms: from straight to broken along X, from sparse to busy along Y. One Density knob per voice thins a part out or fills it up, and Chaos adds seeded variation that comes back the same in every render. There's nothing to draw. Patch its triggers into drum modules ( Trig and Velocity ), or Notes into a drum rack in Live, press play, and perform the beat — by hand on the map, or with an LFO or a Random on X and Y. How does it work? The map. The map is a 5 × 5 grid of nodes . Each node holds, for each voice, 32 levels (two bars of 16ths). A level says how much a step wants to be a hit: the backbone is high, ghost notes and fills are low. X and Y pick a point between four nodes and mix their levels. They're read once per step, so a fast LFO changes the pattern step by step, never mid-step. The factory map is built from rhythmic rules, not taken from any machine: Kick: on every beat at the straight edge; toward broken it moves off beats 2 and 4 to pushed 16ths and a 3 + 3 + 2 feel. Busier rows add pickups. Snare: a backbeat on 2 and 4, turning into a half-time snare on 3 and then a displaced backbeat toward the broken edge. Busier rows add ghost notes. Hats: quarters at the sparse edge, 8ths in the middle, 16ths at the busy edge; toward broken the strong hats move to the off-beats. The last beat of every second bar is lighter, with rising kick and snare pickups, so raising Density or Fill reveals a fill. Density. A step plays when its level is above (1 − Density) · 255 . At 0 % nothing plays, at 100 % everything above zero. Because the important steps have the highest levels, turning Density up adds hits from the backbone outward and never takes one away. Accent and velocity. Louder levels play louder ( Vel = 30 % … 100 %); a level above Accent also fires the voice's Acc output. Fill. While the Fill gate is high, Fill Amount is added to every Density. Chaos nudges every step's level up or down by a seeded amount, so weak hits come and go while the backbone stays. The nudges change every bar (or every 2, 4, 8 bars — Chaos Rate — or never: Frozen ), counted from the song position, and they're the same every time you play that bar. Timing. With nothing in Clock , steps follow the transport at Rate and land on the right step after a loop jump; with a trigger in Clock , each pulse is a step. At 1/8 the two-bar map becomes four bars, at 1/32 it's double time. Length shortens the pattern; End fires when it starts over. Every hit is also a note at the voice's note number, ending after Note Length ; no note is left hanging on stop, Reset or a note change. How to use it? Drums on the board: Kick into a kick's Trig and Kick Vel into its Velocity ; the same for snare and hats. Drums in Live: Notes into a MIDI Out port with a drum rack (36, 38 and 42 are kick, snare and closed hat). Performing: drag the puck on the map. The ring is where the knobs are; the dot (with its trail) is where X and Y really are, cables included. Evolving beats: a slow LFO on X and a Random on Y: the groove wanders through the map and stays musical. Fills: a gate from a clock divider or another sequencer's End into Fill gives a fill every 4 or 8 bars. Your own map: press Edit node , click a node on the map and draw its levels in the lanes. Edited nodes show as larger dots; Reset node brings back the factory node. The lanes show what plays right now: level bars, a threshold line per voice and the hits (accents bolder). Demo patches Five whole patches show what Drum Map does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Drum Map under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Drum Map: Wandering the Map Two slow LFOs move X and Y through the map, so the beat drifts from sparse to busy and back without ever repeating exactly. Grab the X and Y knobs yourself to park on a pattern you like; the three Density knobs thin out any spot. Drum Map: Sparse with Fills Low Density settings leave a spacious beat with only the strongest hits, and a square LFO holds the Fill input for the last bar of every four. Raise Fill Amount for a bigger fill, or raise a Density knob to bring a drum back in. Drum Map: Chaos Re-roll Chaos at 55 % swaps in a few random changes every bar, a lively breakbeat that is never quite the same twice. Set Chaos Rate to Frozen, or change the Seed, to lock in a version you like. Drum Map: Triplet Shuffle Rate 1/16T and a 24-step Length turn the map into a rolling triplet shuffle, with Swing and Accent adding a lazy push on top. Switch Rate back to 1/16 to hear the same map played straight. Drum Map: Notes to Other Drums The Notes output sends the map as note events (Kick Note, Snare Note, Hats Note), and Drum Notes turns them into triggers for a different kit: a ring kick, a clap on the snare note and a cowbell on the hats note. Change the three note settings to move a part to another drum. Reference Knobs Knob Range Default X 0 – 100 % 25 % Y 0 – 100 % 25 % Kick, Snare, Hats Density 0 – 100 % 50 % Fill Amount 0 – 100 % 35 % Chaos 0 – 100 % 0 % Accent 50 – 100 % 78 % Swing 50 – 75 % 50 % Note Length 10 – 100 % of a step 50 % X / Y: the position on the map (straight → broken, sparse → busy). Density: how many of a voice's possible hits play. Fill Amount: added to every Density while Fill is high. Chaos: how far the seeded variation moves the levels. Accent: the level above which a hit is accented. Swing: delays every second step. Note Length: how long the notes on Notes last. Every knob is a modulation destination. Settings Setting Values Default Length 1 – 32 steps 32 Rate 1/8, 1/8T, 1/16, 1/16T, 1/32 1/16 Chaos Rate Every bar, Every 2 / 4 / 8 bars, Frozen Every bar Seed 0 – 999 1 Kick Note, Snare Note, Hats Note 0 – 127 36, 38, 42 Sync To Auto, Clock, Transport Auto Sync To: what steps the module. Auto : the clock pulses while Clock is patched, otherwise the transport. Clock : only the pulses step it. Transport : the song position steps it, and a patched Clock is ignored. Inputs Input Signal What it does Clock trigger each pulse is a step; unpatched, the transport drives the steps Reset trigger the next step is step 1 Fill gate while high, every Density is raised by Fill Amount Outputs Output Signal What it does Kick, Snare, Hats trigger a pulse per hit Kick Acc, Snare Acc, Hats Acc trigger a pulse with an accented hit Kick Vel, Snare Vel, Hats Vel control, 0 – 1 the hit's velocity, held until the next hit Notes notes every hit as a note at the voice's note number Step control, 0 – 1 the playhead: first step 0, last step 1 End trigger a pulse when the pattern starts over

title: Gate Sequencer
text: Gate Sequencer Gate Sequencer in the module view Introduction The Gate Sequencer is a rhythm sequencer with deep steps : four tracks of up to 32 gates, where every step has its own probability , gate length (or a tie), ratchets (fast repeats inside the step), nudge (playing a little early or late) and a condition (every Nth loop, only the first time, only during a fill …). Each track has its own length and rate , so tracks drift against each other and still land on the bars. It has no pitches: it's about how hits happen. Patch its gates and triggers into drum modules or envelopes, or Notes into a drum rack. The chances are seeded, so a pattern that "breathes" plays the same in every render. A new module plays a small beat on tracks 1–3 straight away. How does it work? Timing. With nothing in Clock , every track follows the transport on its own grid (its Rate ), worked out from the song position, so a loop jump lands each track on the right step. A 16-step track against a 12-step track lines up again every 3 bars; the Cycle output fires when all four are back on step 1 together. With a cable in Clock , each pulse is a 1/16 tick and the tracks run at their rates relative to it (a 1/32 track plays twice per tick, spaced by the measured tick length). Whether a step plays. A step that is On plays when: its condition is true: A:B — on the A-th of every B loops (2:4 = the second of every four); First / Not First — on the first loop since the transport started (or since Reset), or on every other loop; Fill / Not Fill — while the Fill input is high, or while it isn't; Prev / Not Prev — when the last earlier chance-or-condition step on the track played (or didn't). Chain them for "if this, then that". its probability wins the dice: 100 % always plays; below that the chance is scaled by the track's Chance knob (0 % leaves only the certain steps, 200 % doubles every chance). The dice come from Seed , the track, the step and the loop, so renders repeat and a jump replays the same choices. Dice decides how often they change: every loop, every 2/4/8 loops, or never ( Fixed ). the track isn't muted (the M button or the Mute input). Inside a step. Length is the gate as a share of the step; Tie keeps the gate up until the next step on the track that doesn't play. Ratchet splits the step into 1–8 hits: Even , Faster (gaps shrink) or Slower (gaps grow). Ratchet Decay makes each repeat softer. Nudge moves the whole step up to half a step early or late, scaled by Nudge Depth . Early hits really are early: the module looks ahead. Velocity goes to the Vel output and the notes. Two gates that touch drop for 1 ms, so the next one starts with a clean edge. Notes. Each hit is a note at the track's Note number, ending with its gate. No note is left hanging: stopping, Reset, Mute, changing a track's length, rate or note, and editing the step that's sounding all end it. How to use it? Drums on the board: Trig 1 into a kick's Trig , Vel 1 into its Velocity ; the same for tracks 2–4. Drums in Live: Notes into a MIDI Out port with a drum rack; Note 1–4 default to kick, snare, closed and open hat. Editing: choose what a click edits with On / Prob / Len / Ratch / Nudge / Cond / Vel . On : click toggles, drag paints. Prob , Len , Vel , Ratch : drag up and down. Nudge : drag sideways. Cond : click cycles the condition. Click a step to select it (Shift: several) and set every field in the inspector line below. Steps drawn hollow won't play on this pass. Length and rate: at the start of each row, or drag the marker at the end of the row. Track tools act on the track you last clicked: Randomize (density, probability range, ratchet chance and nudge in ▾), Euclid (k hits spread evenly, with a rotation), ◀ ▶ rotate, Copy / Paste . Fills: patch a gate into Fill (every 4th bar from a Clock divider or another sequencer's End ) and mark some steps Fill or Not Fill . Thinning and filling: a slow LFO on Chance 3 makes the hats breathe. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Gate Sequencer does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Gate Sequencer under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Gate Sequencer: Loose Probability Beat Coin-flip steps (?) and quiet ghost notes (o) make a drum pattern that breathes differently on every pass; Swing adds a lazy lean. Turn a track's Chance knob down for fewer hits, or set Dice to Fixed to lock one version in. Gate Sequencer: Ratchet Rolls Steps marked 2 and 3 fire quick repeats inside one step: two on the snare, a rising run of three on the hats. Ratchet Decay fades each repeat out, so try raising it for a bouncing-ball feel. Gate Sequencer: Phasing Plucks Four tracks of different lengths (3, 4, 5 and 7 steps) each pluck one note of a chord, so the pattern only realigns after 420 steps and keeps shifting shape. Change a Length setting by one to get a different cycle. Gate Sequencer: Fill Switch Steps marked ! only play while the Fill input is high and steps marked - only while it is low, so a square LFO that holds Fill for the last bar of every four swaps the main beat for a busy fill. Some steps are nudged early or late for a human feel; Nudge Depth scales them all. Gate Sequencer: Mute Arrangement Slow square LFOs patched into the Mute inputs bring the four tracks in and out on their own cycles of 2, 4 and 8 bars, so a simple pattern arranges itself. Patch a different LFO Sync into a mute jack to rewrite the structure. Reference Knobs Knob Range Default Chance 1 … 4 0 – 200 % 100 % Nudge Depth 0 – 100 % 100 % Ratchet Decay 0 – 100 % 0 % Swing 50 – 75 % 50 % Chance: scales the probabilities below 100 % of a track. Nudge Depth: scales every step's nudge; 0 % plays straight. Ratchet Decay: repeat i of r plays at 1 − Decay · i / r of the velocity. Swing: delays every second step of each track, on its own grid. Every knob is a modulation destination. Settings Setting Values Default Length 1 … 4 1 – 32 steps 16 Rate 1 … 4 1/1 … 1/32, dotted (.) and triplet (T) 1/16 Dice New every loop, Repeat every 2 / 4 / 8, Fixed New every loop Seed 0 – 999 1 Note 1 … 4 0 – 127 36, 38, 42, 46 Sync To Auto, Clock, Transport Auto Sync To: what steps the module. Auto : the clock pulses while Clock is patched, otherwise the transport. Clock : only the pulses step it. Transport : the song position steps it, and a patched Clock is ignored. Inputs Input Signal What it does Clock trigger each pulse is a 1/16 tick; unpatched, the transport drives the tracks Reset trigger every track's next step is step 1; loop counts restart Fill gate while high, Fill steps play and Not Fill steps don't Mute 1 … 4 gate while high, the track plays nothing (it keeps counting) Outputs Output Signal What it does Gate 1 … 4 gate high for each hit's gate Trig 1 … 4 trigger a pulse at each hit, ratchets included Vel 1 … 4 control, 0 – 1 the latest hit's velocity, held Notes notes every hit as a note at the track's note number Cycle trigger a pulse when all four tracks are on step 1 together

title: Rhythm Bank
text: Rhythm Bank Rhythm Bank in the module view Introduction Four related rhythms from one number. Choose a Family (how the rhythms are made) and turn Pattern (0 – 127) to browse grooves: all four outputs change together, as parts of one beat. Out 1 is the strongest part (think kick), Out 4 the busiest. Modulate Pattern with something slow and the drum part develops over the song, the same in every render. How does it work? Families. In most families the lower bits of Pattern set the density and the higher ones how the four parts relate. Even: evenly spread hits ("Euclidean"); the parts are copies in canon, a ladder of densities, halves and doubles, mirror images, off-beats, … Prime: each part repeats every 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 or 13 steps; with Length Open the parts drift against each other. Metric: hits by metric weight: Pattern 0 is kick on 1, snare on 1 and 3, quarters and eighths; higher numbers move parts to the off-beats (backbeat). Poly: each part plays 2 – 9 hits per cycle, not tied to the steps (polyrhythms); Grid = Free plays them at their exact time. Interlock: parts that never hit on the same step. Seeded: random grooves weighted towards strong beats; every number is its own groove. Steps. With nothing in Clock , one step is Rate at the song tempo, locked to the song position. Patch a trigger into Clock and every pulse is a step. Reset makes the next step the first. Length sets the cycle (2 – 32 steps, or Open : no cycle). Shaping. Rotate 1 … 4 delay or advance each part. Mute 1 … 4 silence a part. Complement makes the parts work together: Avoid (a part only plays where no lower part plays), Fill (the same, and the last part fills every empty step), Pairs (Out 2 plays where Out 1 doesn't, Out 4 where Out 3 doesn't). Changes. With Change = Cycle a new Pattern (or Family, Length, Complement) starts at the next step 1; with Step at the next step. Outputs. Gates last Width of a step (or one-sample triggers with Output = Trigger ). Any is high while any part plays, Accent where two or more parts hit together (before Complement), Cycle fires at step 1. How to use it? A drum part: Out 1 – 4 into a drum kit's triggers; turn Pattern . A part that develops: a slow LFO or Random into Pattern , Change = Cycle . Accents: Accent into a drum's level or a VCA. Choke groups: Complement = Avoid : hi-hat and snare never collide. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Rhythm Bank does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Rhythm Bank under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Rhythm Bank: Even Groove Kit The Even family spreads hits as evenly as it can: four related rhythms of different density drive a kick, snare, hats and a rim. Turn Pattern to change all four grooves at once, or turn Width for longer or shorter gates. Rhythm Bank: Prime Cycles Length 15 and the Prime family give four rhythms with uneven, prime-based spacing, each playing a different pluck of an A minor chord. Because the lengths never line up the same way twice, the figure keeps turning; try Family = Poly for a different split. Rhythm Bank: Pattern Browser A stepped random LFO picks a new Pattern number every bar, and Change is set to Cycle so each new rhythm waits for the end of the current one: the part develops by itself without a break. Set Change to Step to switch mid-pattern, or turn the LFO cable down to stay near one groove. Rhythm Bank: Interlocking Pair With Complement set to Pairs, output 2 fills the gaps left by output 1 (and 4 those of 3), so a low and a high voice share one steady line like two hands. Switch Complement to Off to hear the raw rhythms collide, or to Avoid to keep them from landing together. Rhythm Bank: Seeded Open Loop Length is Open, so the rhythms never loop, and the Seeded family makes up a fresh but related set from the Pattern number. Rotate nudges each rhythm against the others and Grid Free lets hits sit between steps; set Length back to 16 to hear a plain loop. Reference Knobs Knob Range Default Pattern 0 – 127 0 Rotate 1 … 4 −16 … +16 steps 0 Width 1 – 100 % of a step 50 % Settings Setting Values Default Family Even, Prime, Metric, Poly, Interlock, Seeded Even Length 2 – 32 steps, Open 16 Rate 1/1 … 1/32, dotted (.) and triplet (T) 1/16 Complement Off, Avoid, Fill, Pairs Off Change Step, Cycle Cycle Grid Snap, Free (Poly) Snap Mute 1 … 4 on / off off Output Gate, Trigger Gate Sync To Auto, Clock, Transport Auto Sync To: what steps the module. Auto : the clock pulses while Clock is patched, otherwise the transport. Clock : only the pulses step it. Transport : the song position steps it, and a patched Clock is ignored. Inputs Input Signal What it does Clock trigger patched: each pulse is one step Reset trigger the next step is step 1 Outputs Output Signal What it does Out 1 … Out 4 gate the four parts Any gate high while any part is high Accent gate steps where two or more parts hit Cycle trigger a pulse at step 1

title: Automata
text: Automata Introduction Automata is a sequencer that nobody programs. A small system lives inside it and takes one step every clock tick; what that system does becomes the music. Its cells light up and go dark, a walker leaves a trail, a chain of notes moves from one degree of the scale to the next, a phrase rewrites itself. You choose the kind of system with Mode , a seed decides where it starts, and the module turns what happens into a gate, a pitch in your scale, a velocity, a trigger whenever something is born and a Density voltage that says how alive the whole thing is. Two controls make it behave differently from a pattern sequencer. Interference injects tiny seeded disturbances, one flipped cell or one mutated symbol at a time, so the evolution never repeats exactly. Rewind steps the system back by a number of generations from a ring of snapshots: the music returns to something it just played, then forks into a slightly different future. How does it work? Every step, the system advances one generation ; the module then reads it: Gate is high for Gate Length of the step when the system plays a note. Pitch is one of eight scale degrees spread over Octaves (1 – 3) of Scale above Root (or the key and scale of a Harmony Master bus, with Harmony ), plus Transpose . Velocity is a 0 … 1 voltage from how crowded, how surprising or how high the thing that played was. Birth is a trigger when something new appears at the place being read. Density is a 0 … 1 voltage: the share of cells alive, marks laid, notes in the last sixteen steps or notes in the string. Step is a trigger on every step. The five systems Ring. Up to 32 cells in a circle. Each step every cell takes its next value from itself and its two neighbours according to Rule (0 – 255); rule 30 and rule 90 are classic starting points. A read head moves one cell round the ring per step: a lit cell is a note, the five cells around the head give the degree, and Birth fires when the cell under the head just came alive. Density sets how many cells are alive at the start; at 0 the ring begins with one lit cell. A ring that dies out gets one new cell. Grid. An 8 × 8 wrapping grid under a life-like rule ( Grid Rule , written as birth/survival counts, such as B3/S23). The read head moves one column per step: the column plays if any cell in it is alive, the lowest live row gives the degree, the number of live cells the velocity, and Birth fires when a cell in that column was born. An extinct grid is sown again. Chain. A Markov chain over the eight scale degrees and a rest. The 9 × 9 transition table in the view holds a weight (0 – 9) for every move from one state to the next; each step the chain draws its next state from the row of the current one. Rare moves are accented, and Birth fires on a surprising move. Learn makes the table change as you play: with a melody patched into Learn , every move you play from one degree to the next is added to the table; with nothing patched, the chain reinforces its own habits. Learned weights fade slowly. Walker. A walker on an 8 × 8 wrapping grid with marks on some cells. On each step it looks at the mark under it, turns right or left as Turns says for that mark, changes the mark to the next kind, and moves forward. It plays when it arrives on a marked cell; its column gives the degree and its row the velocity. Birth fires when it leaves a fresh mark. Density is the share of marked cells. Rewrite. A string of symbols (A, B, C, R, U, D) that is rewritten each time the read head reaches its end, using the three rules of the chosen Rules set. A, B and C play a note (B then moves up a degree, C down); R is a rest; U and D move the next note an octave up or down. When the string would get too long it starts over from its first symbol. Birth fires at every rewrite. Interference and Rewind Interference is the chance (up to 50 % per step) that one thing is disturbed before the system evolves: a cell flips, the walker's mark or direction changes, the chain picks a neighbouring state, a symbol mutates. The disturbances come from Seed and a counter, so a render is repeatable. Rewind goes back Rewind By generations (1 – 16, up to 63 in all) when the Rewind button is pressed or a gate arrives on the Rewind input. The state returns exactly. Because the disturbance counter keeps counting, the same stretch replays with different disturbances whenever Interference is up, and exactly the same when it is 0. Reset, seeds and repeatability Reset (a pulse on the Reset input) returns the system to its seed. The seed comes from Seed , Density and the mode. When the transport starts or jumps, the module replays the system from its seed up to the current step (up to 4,096 steps), so a render from the same position is always identical. Rewinds and learning are not part of that replay. The view Ring: the cells on a circle with the read head circled, and the last generations as rows beside it. Grid / Walker: the 8 × 8 cells; the column being read lit (Grid), the walker as a white dot. Chain: the transition table, rows = from, columns = to, the last row and column are the rests. Brightness shows the chance. Click a cell to raise its weight, right-click (or Shift-click) to lower it. The current state's row is outlined. Rewrite: the string as chips, the symbol being read outlined. The bar below shows Density ; the number is the generation. How to use it? A melody that grows: Ring , rule 30, Density 0; Pitch to an oscillator, Gate to its envelope. Rhythm from births: Grid ; Birth to a hat, Gate to a kick. Never the same twice: raise Interference to 10 – 30 %. Return to a phrase: a slow square LFO into Rewind . Teach it a style: Chain , Learn up, a looping melody into Learn . Dynamics: Density into a filter cutoff or a VCA. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Automata does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Automata under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Automata: Ring Melody A ring of sixteen cells grows under rule 30 from a single seed cell; the read head sweeps round the ring, so the lit cells become notes and the dark ones rests. Change Rule (90 mirrors itself, 110 drifts) or raise Interference to nudge the pattern off its course; Reset returns to the seed. Automata: Grid Garden An 8 by 8 wrapping world: colonies grow, collide and die. Gate and Pitch play a bell-like lead, every birth of a cell triggers a soft hat, and Density, how alive the grid is, opens a filter. Try the other Grid Rule choices, or raise Density for a crowded start. Automata: Chain Learns a Tune A frozen eight-note loop plays on the left and is patched into the chain's Learn input; the chain on the right listens, adds the moves it hears to its transition table and improvises in the same style. Turn Learn down to hear the plain, stepwise table, or open the module to edit the table by hand. Automata: Walker Drums A walker with four turn rules roams an 8 by 8 wrapping grid; it plays a note whenever it steps onto a marked cell and fires Birth when it lays a fresh mark. Gate drives a bass, Birth drives hats and a snare, and the walker's route repeats until Interference nudges it somewhere new. Automata: Rewrite and Rewind A phrase rewrites itself each time it ends, growing longer and then starting over. A slow square LFO patched into Rewind pulls the system four generations back every few seconds, so the phrase keeps returning to something it has played, but never exactly the same way. Change Rewind By or the Rules choice. Presets The preset bar of the Automata view has 18 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Rule 30 Ring One seed cell grows into a lopsided, never-quite-repeating pattern. Rule 90 Lace A symmetrical lattice: the melody mirrors itself as it grows. Rule 110 Drift Structures drift sideways through a longer ring. Rule 184 Traffic Cells move along the ring like cars in traffic: slow, flowing lines. Garden Grid A small wrapping world: colonies grow, collide and die out. Mazy Grid Structures build up slowly into a maze of long-lived notes. Seeds Burst Every cell lives one step: a restless, sparkling grid. Gentle Chain Mostly stepwise motion with occasional rests. Student Chain Patch a melody into Learn: the chain picks up its habits. Wandering Walker A walker with two turn rules draws a looping highway. Crowded Walker A walker among old marks: gaps and bursts. Wide Walker Six turn rules: a sprawling, unpredictable path over three octaves. Cascade Phrase A phrase that rewrites itself every time it ends. Climbing Phrase Rising lines with octave jumps. Breathing Tide Slow phrases with rests that breathe. Restless Ring Interference keeps nudging the ring: it never settles into a pattern. Fork Phrase A rewriting phrase with a few mutations each pass. Free Grid Ignores the song tempo and steps at a set rate. title: Recall
text: Recall Recall in the module view Introduction Recall generates random rhythms and melodies in two sections that share one clock. T makes random gates: coin tosses between two outputs, random divisions and ratchets, or drum-like patterns weighted by the bar. X makes three random voltages whose distribution you shape and whose steps go from smooth glides to notes of a scale. Each section has a Recall knob that makes it repeat its own recent past: from always new, through variations on what just happened, to a locked loop you can capture into the board. How does it work? Clock. Each tick comes from Clock if patched, else from the song position when Sync is on a note value and the transport plays, else from Rate (or the synced length while the transport is stopped). Clock out fires on every tick. Reset makes the next tick tick 0: the loops start again at their first slot, and the memory stays. T section. On every tick the section takes a decision from four random numbers. T Mode turns it into gates: Coin: exactly one of T1 and T2 fires; T Bias is the chance of T1. Chance: T1 and T2 fire independently, each with the chance T Bias . Ratchet: each output picks a rate: ÷4, ÷3, ÷2 (fires on the first tick of its group), ×1, or ×2, ×3, ×4 (two to four evenly spaced pulses in one tick). T Bias left of the middle prefers divisions, right of it multiplications. Drums: T1 is a kick, strong on beats 1 and 3 of a 16-tick bar; T2 a snare, strong on 2 and 4. At T Bias 50 % you get a plain backbeat with occasional ghost notes; more fills in, less thins out. T Jitter delays each gate by up to half a tick (never early). Gate Length sets the gate length as a share of a tick (of a sub-pulse when ratcheting). X section. On each X event (every tick, every T1 or T2 gate, or each pulse at X Clock , chosen with X Source ) the section draws three values: X Spread is the width: 0 % is a constant; up to 50 % a bell around the middle; up to 85 % it widens to even; above that values are pushed to the edges. X Bias pulls values down (left) or up (right). X Steps: below 45 % the outputs glide to each new value (at 0 % over the whole time to the next one, a smooth random curve); 45 – 55 % plain steps; above 55 % the values snap to Scale from Root . From 70 % on, scale notes drop out (for seven-note scales the 2nd, 6th, 4th, 7th, 3rd and 5th degree) until at 100 % only the root is left, in octaves. X Range: −1 … +1, 0 … 1 or −2 … +2 (±2 octaves into a pitch input). X Mode Sorted sorts the three so X1 ≤ X2 ≤ X3: low, middle, high. Recall. Each section remembers its last Loop decisions. With Recall at 0 % every decision is new; at 50 % about half of them repeat the decision from one loop ago, so the pattern keeps its shape while it changes; at 100 % the loop is locked: exactly what was playing when the knob reached the top. The memory holds the raw random numbers, not the gates and voltages, so Bias , Spread , Steps , Scale and T Mode still reshape a locked loop: lock a melody, then change the scale, and it keeps its contour. Capture. Capture T and Capture X store a section's loop in the board and switch on Use for it: the section then plays the stored loop on every tick, whatever the Recall knob, the seed or the song position. Use T / Use X in the view switch back to the live memory and forth again. Repeatable. New decisions come from Seed and the tick number. On a transport start or a loop jump the memory is rebuilt by replaying the ticks before it, so a render from the same position always sounds the same. How to use it? Two drum voices: T Mode Drums, T1 to a kick, T2 to a snare, Clock out to a hi-hat. A melody that stays itself: X Steps 65 %, X1 into an oscillator's pitch, T1 into its envelope, X Source T1. Raise X Recall until you like the phrase, then Capture X . Chords: X Mode Sorted, X Steps 60 %, X1 … X3 into three oscillators. Smooth random modulation: X Steps 0 %, X Spread 40 % into a filter. Human timing: T Jitter 15 %. Rolls: T Mode Ratchet, T Bias 75 %. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Recall does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Recall under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Recall: Coin-Flip Drums Every clock step Recall flips a coin for two gates: T1 plays the kick, T2 the snare, and the Clock output drives steady hats. T Bias leans the coin towards or away from firing, T Jitter adds extra randomness; try raising T Recall to repeat the recent past. Recall: Ratchet Bass Line T Mode Ratchet turns the random gates into bursts of quick repeats, and each burst plays a bass note chosen by X from F Phrygian dominant. Lower X Spread for a narrower line, or move X Bias to put the bass higher or lower. Recall: Settling Loop A slow sawtooth LFO raises both Recall knobs from 0 to 100 % over 16 bars: the melody starts out new on every step, gradually repeats itself more and more, and ends up as a locked loop before the cycle begins again. Move T Recall or X Recall yourself to freeze or free it at any time. Recall: Sorted Triad Rising X Mode Sorted puts the three random voltages in ascending order, so X1, X2 and X3 always form a stack from low to high, and three voices play them as a changing chord. Switch X Mode to Independent and the voices cross over; change Scale for a different colour. Recall: Free-Running Bells Sync is set to Free at 1.6 Hz, so Recall ticks on its own clock rather than the song's, and each random T1 gate rings a bell whose pitch is read from X on its own X clock. Change Rate to speed the shimmer up or slow it down. Auto : the clock pulses while Clock is patched, otherwise the transport. Clock : only the pulses step it. Transport : the song position steps it, and a patched Clock is ignored. It applies to Clock ; X Clock keeps its own job as the external X source. X Source External with nothing at X Clock draws on every tick. The knobs and the two loop lengths are modulation destinations; T Mode is a dropdown a cable can drive. title: Shift Register
text: Shift Register Shift Register in the module view Introduction Shift Register is a looping row of 16 bits. On every step the bits move one place along and the bit at Length comes back in at the front, sometimes flipped. Everything it outputs is read from those bits: a stepped voltage, a quantized pitch, eight gates, a combined gate and a weighted mix. Because only one bit is new on each step, consecutive values are related, and the gates are delayed copies of each other: rhythms and melodies that echo through the register like a canon. One knob, Lock , moves the pattern from frozen through slowly changing to fully random. How does it work? The register. Bit 1 is the newest bit, bit 16 the oldest. On each step: The bit at position Length is read: that's the bit that comes back. Every bit moves one place along. The bit comes back in at position 1, flipped or not, depending on Lock . Lock is the chance that the returning bit stays as it is. At +100 % nothing ever flips: the pattern repeats every Length steps. Between +100 % and 0 % it changes now and then and stays recognisable; at 0 % every bit is a coin toss. At −100 % every returning bit is flipped: the pattern repeats every 2 × Length steps, with the second half the inverse of the first. Source chooses what comes back: Loop (the register's own bit), Data (the Data input, so the register delays an incoming rhythm, corrupted by Lock below +100 %) or Data ⊕ Loop (the input scrambles the loop). Voltage and Pitch read the first eight bits as a number from 0 to 255, with bit 1 counting most. Each step roughly halves the previous value and adds the new bit on top, which gives melodies from the register a recognisable contour. Voltage is that number scaled to 0 … 1 (times Level ); Pitch spreads it over Octaves , adds Transpose and snaps it to Scale . Bit 1 … Bit 8 are high for Gate Length of a step while their bit is 1. At 100 % consecutive 1s merge into one long gate. Bit 2 is Bit 1 one step later, Bit 3 two steps later, and so on. Bits beyond Length keep shifting, so with Length 4, Bit 5 … 8 are older copies of the same pattern. Combo combines the bits chosen with the toggles in the view: Any (one of them is 1), All (all of them are 1) or Odd (an odd number of them is 1). Mix is a weighted sum of bits 1 … 6, using the six Weight knobs, scaled so it stays within −1 … +1. The defaults (1, ½, ¼, ⅛) make a 4-bit version of Voltage ; other weights give stepped patterns that don't follow the register's number. Steps come from Clock if patched, else from the song position when Sync is on a note value and the transport plays, else from Rate (or the synced length while the transport is stopped). Reset reloads the start pattern on the next step. Repeatable. The flips come from Seed and the step number. The register also has a start pattern : a transport start loads it and replays the steps up to the song position, so a render from the same position always sounds the same, wherever you start. The view The top row shows the live register (newest left; bits beyond Length dim; ▲ marks the bit that comes back; a ring flashes when the entering bit was flipped). Click a bit to flip it in the running register. The row below is the start pattern. Click to edit it. Capture copies the live register into the start pattern, so a pattern you like comes back on every play. Load loads the start pattern now. Combo toggles choose the bits for Combo . The strip shows the last 32 values of Voltage ; × marks steps where the entering bit was flipped. How to use it? Canon rhythms: Bit 1 , Bit 3 and Bit 6 to three drums, Lock 90 %. A melody that evolves: Pitch into an oscillator, Step into its envelope, Lock 80 %. Raise Lock to 100 % to keep a phrase, then Capture it. Stepped modulation: Mix to a filter, an LFO on Weight 2 morphs between two stepped patterns. Delay a rhythm: Source on Data , a gate pattern into Data : the bit outputs play it back delayed by 0 … 7 steps. Accents: Combo on All with two bits chosen, into a velocity or a VCA. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Shift Register does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Shift Register under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Shift Register: Frozen Eight-Note Loop Lock at its top position freezes the register, so its eight bits recycle forever as a fixed little melody in D minor pentatonic over two octaves. Change the seed or Length to get a different tune; Length 5 or 7 against the drums makes the melody drift against the beat. Shift Register: Slowly Mutating Tune Lock sits just below frozen, so now and then a bit flips and the melody changes by a note or two instead of repeating exactly. A slow LFO nudges Lock between nearly frozen and quite loose; turn it down to hear the tune stay put, up to hear it wander. Shift Register: Canon of Drums As the bits travel along the register, each bit output plays the same rhythm one step later than the one before, so a kick, snare, hat and clap echo one rhythm in canon. Change Length to reshape the pattern for all four at once, or Lock below the top to let it mutate. Shift Register: Bits from a Data Input Source is set to Data, so the register is fed from a gate patched into its Data input, here a pair of square LFOs with different speeds mixed together. The register turns that slow on-off pattern into a lively stepped melody. Switch Source to Data ⊕ Loop to blend the old loop with the new input. Shift Register: Weighted Mix Filter The Mix output adds the bits up with the Weight knobs, here as a stepped voltage that sweeps the cutoff of a filter on a held saw bass, while Voltage plays the pitches. Change Weight 1 to 3 to reshape the sweep, or set a weight negative to flip it. Presets The preset bar of the Shift Register view has 15 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Frozen Loop The pattern repeats exactly every eight steps. Slowly Mutating Mostly stable, with an occasional note changing. Restless Changes often but keeps a recognisable contour. Pure Random Every bit is a coin toss: random melodies. Inverted Echo Repeats every twelve steps, the second half inverted. Short Four A four-step loop for a hypnotic riff. Odd Seven Seven steps: the loop slides across the bar. Long Sixteen A long register that drifts slowly over time. Slow Eighths Slower steps with long gates for a calm line. Staccato Burst Fast, short notes in an Eastern scale. Wide Four Octaves The pitch spreads over four octaves: big leaps. Free Running Ignores the song tempo and steps at a set rate. Gate Weights Different weights make the Mix output stepped and uneven. All-Bits Combo Combo goes high only when every chosen bit is 1: sparse rhythms. Odd-Parity Combo Combo of an odd number of bits: busy, shifting gate patterns. Reference Knobs and settings Control Range Default Lock −100 … +100 % +80 % Rate 0.05 – 50 Hz 4 Hz Level 0 – 100 % 100 % Gate Length 1 – 100 % of a step 50 % Weight 1 … 6 −1 … +1 1, 0.5, 0.25, 0.125, 0, 0 Length 2 – 16 bits 8 Sync Free, 1/32, 1/16, 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, 1 bar, 2 bars, 4 bars, 8 bars 1/16 Source Loop, Data, Data ⊕ Loop Loop Combine Any, All, Odd Any Octaves 1 – 4 2 Root C … B C Scale the Step Sequencer's scales Minor Pentatonic Seed 0 – 999 1 Sync To Auto, Clock, Transport Auto Sync To: what steps the module. Auto : the clock pulses while Clock is patched, otherwise the transport. Clock : only the pulses step it. Transport : the song position steps it, and a patched Clock is ignored. With Transport (or Auto and nothing patched), the Sync setting still picks a note value or free running. Lock: the chance the returning bit is kept: flip chance = (1 − Lock) / 2. Rate: steps per second when Sync is Free and Clock is unpatched. Level: scales Voltage . Gate Length: length of the bit gates and Combo , as a share of a step. Weight 1 … 6: the mixer's weights for bits 1 … 6. Length: which bit comes back. Changing it never clears bits. Sync: one step per note value at the song tempo. Source, Combine, Octaves, Root, Scale: see above. Seed: picks the sequence of flips. Lock , Rate , Level , Gate Length , the weights and Length are modulation destinations. Inputs Input Signal What it does Clock trigger each pulse is a step; overrides Rate and Sync Reset trigger the next step reloads the start pattern and counts as step 0 Data gate the bit to write with Source on Data or Data ⊕ Loop Transpose pitch added to Pitch before quantizing, read at each step Outputs Output Signal What it does Voltage control, 0 … 1 the first eight bits as a number, times Level Pitch pitch the same number over Octaves , quantized to Scale Bit 1 … Bit 8 gate high while that bit is 1 Combo gate the chosen bits combined Mix control, −1 … +1 weighted sum of bits 1 … 6 Step trigger a pulse on every step Loop trigger a pulse every Length steps

title: Clock Div
text: Clock Div Introduction Eight clock dividers on one clock, each with its own division. Set Div 1 to 2 and Out 1 fires every second step; set Div 4 to 7 and Out 4 fires every seventh. Patch a clock in, or leave Clock empty and it follows the song: everything is worked out from the song position, so it stays on the bars, after loop jumps and in renders. For eight divisions that are a family and move together with one knob, see Rotating Div. How does it work? The base step. Unpatched, one step is Base (1/16 by default) at the song's tempo. Patch a trigger into Clock and every pulse is a step instead. Divisions. Div 1 … Div 8 are whole numbers from 1 to 64. Output k fires on step 0 and then every Div k steps. The defaults are the classic /2 /3 /4 /5 /6 /8 /16 /32. A new division takes effect at that output's next cycle; a gate that is already high always finishes its length. Realign. Odd divisions drift against the bar: /3 of 1/16 notes repeats only every 3 bars. Realign restarts every output every 1, 2, 4 or 8 bars; the last cycle before the restart is shortened, and its gate ends at least 1 ms before the next one starts. With a patched clock there is no bar, so Realign has no effect: patch a bar-rate trigger into Reset instead. Gates. In Gate output, an output is high for Width of its own period ( Gate Length = Division ) or of one base step ( Base Step ). Trigger output sends a one-sample pulse instead. Reset makes the next base step the start of every output's cycle (with a clock: the next pulse). When the transport stops, every output goes low; on play, nothing fires until the next due step. How to use it? Drum rhythms from one clock: Out 1 … 8 into drum triggers, set to /2, /3, /4 and /16 for a hat, a clap, a kick and a crash. Phrases: /16 or /32 into a sequencer's Reset , or into a Harmony Master to change chord every two bars. Odd against even: /3 and /4 together, Realign 1 bar so they meet on every downbeat. Slow modulation: Trigger output of a long division into a Random or a Shift Register. Demo patches Five whole patches show what Clock Div does. In the standalone app open File → Presets… (⌘P) and pick Clock Div under Demos by module ; on the website, Run in Play opens one in your browser. Loading one replaces the project and starts the transport. Patch What it shows Clock Div: Layered Percussion One 16th-note clock is cut into /2, /3, /5, /8 and /16: hats on the fast outputs, a kick every eight steps, a rim every three and a cowbell every five, so the layers drift in and out of line. Edit any Div knob to retune a layer; they all realign on the downbeat of the 16-step cycle. Clock Div: Polyrhythm Chimes Four outputs divide an eighth-note clock by 3, 4, 5 and 7 and each rings a different bell tone, so a calm major pentatonic cluster slowly rearranges itself. Change one Div by a single step and the whole pattern shifts. Clock Div: Binary Counter Bass Powers of two (/1, /2, /4, /8) in Trigger mode play a kick, snare, hat and bass in a fixed, regular pattern, a bit like the bits of a counter. Change Base to 1/8T for a rolling feel, or set Realign to 4 bars to snap the layers back together on a longer cycle. Clock Div: Slow Gate Pad With Output set to Gate and Gate Length on Division, the slow outputs (/16, /24, /32 and /48) hold long gates that swell three chord tones in and out at different times. Narrow Width shortens the swells; try Gate Length = Base Step for short blips instead. Clock Div: Clocks for Two Melodies Two Step Sequencers have no clock of their own: one takes /2 and one takes /3 of the divider, so an 8-note arpeggio and a 5-note bass line run at different speeds and phase against each other. Move a Div knob to speed one of them up or down. Presets The preset bar of the Clock Div view has 12 factory presets. Pick one to set the knobs, then change them to taste; your own presets sit next to them. Preset What it does Default Ladder A mix of even and odd divisions for polyrhythmic gates. Powers of Two Classic binary divisions: everything lines up on the downbeat. Even Grid Even divisions only: steady, interlocking pulses. Odd Primes Primes: the outputs rarely coincide, so the rhythm takes ages to repeat. Triggers Only Short triggers instead of gates, for drums and envelopes. Short Pulses Narrow gates: staccato hits on every output. Long Gates Nearly full-width gates that sustain between pulses. Base Step Gates Every gate is one base step long, whatever the division. Eighth Base Slow The base clock at eighths: a slower, more spacious set. Triplet Base Triplet base clock for shuffling cross-rhythms. Bar Realign Odd divisions snapped back together every bar. Four-Bar Polyrhythm Complex divisions that resync every four bars. Auto : the clock pulses while Clock is patched, otherwise the transport. Clock : only the pulses step it. Transport : the song position steps it, and a patched Clock is ignored.
